literature.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 在系统评价纳入的 17 项研究中,11 项参与了主要荟萃分析,另外一项研究仅参与了敏感性分析。在老年人中,汇总 INB 为 105.05 美元 [95% 置信区间 (CI):41.89–168.21 美元;I2 = 93.2%]。对于婴儿,汇总 INB 为 5.81 美元(95% CI:-35.44-47.07 美元;I2 = 89.4%)。在欧洲亚组中,老年人的汇总 INB 为 123.63 美元(95% CI:41.23-206.02 美元;I2 = 89.4%),而婴儿的 INB 为 15.00 美元(95% CI:-4.33-34.34 美元;I2 = 43.4%)。 [10.1186/s40249-026-01520-y]
纳入气候变量的模型无法捕获所有地区 HMPV 活动的时间,但包含 RSV 活动的模型可以重现 HMPV 的两年一次模式,其中 HMPV 传播 在 RSV 存在的情况下减少。 [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014810]
计算筛选将文库缩小到 05 个结构兼容且具有预测结合亲和力的命中 IgDAb。ELISA 证实了纯化的 IgDAb 与 RSV-F 蛋白的特异性结合。体外微中和试验表明,两种“先导”IgDAb 可中和 RSV A2(长株),其 EC50 分别为 1.3 μg/mL 和 3.5 μg/mL。 [10.1007/s11095-026-04226-w]
在兔 疫苗接种 模型中,仅 RSV-A 血清可有效中和所有 RSV-A 分离株和 RSV-B1 参考株,但对同时代 RSV-B 分离株的活性减弱。 [10.1128/jvi.01221-26]
该研究将确定接触 RSV 的年龄如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和呼吸系统结果,研究结果将通过出版物、科学会议和参与者交流进行传播。 [10.1136/bmjopen-2026-127619]

literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval (CI): USD 41.89–168.21; I2 = 93.2%]. [10.1186/s40249-026-01520-y]

The models incorporating climate variables could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions, but models including RSV activity could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV, with HMPV transmission reduced in the presence of RSV. [10.1371/journal.ppat.1014810]

Among 366 hospitalized infants with RSV bronchiolitis, 345 were previously healthy. Of these, 165/345 (47.8%) had received nirsevimab. Breakthrough cases were younger than non-breakthrough cases (2.0 months [IQR, 1.1-3.6] vs 5.2 months [IQR, 3.3-6.6]; p < 0.001). [10.1007/s00431-026-07596-w]

Computational screening narrowed the library to 05 structurally compatible hit IgDAb with predicted binding affinity. ELISA confirmed specific binding of purified IgDAbs to the RSV-F protein. [10.1007/s11095-026-04226-w]

In a rabbit vaccination model, RSV-A-only sera efficiently neutralized all RSV-A isolates and the RSV-B1 reference strain but showed diminished activity against contemporary RSV-B isolates. [10.1128/jvi.01221-26]

news.headline_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒本期公共卫生新闻动态
news.lead_zh: 本期呼吸道合胞病毒新闻集中呈现以下动态。
key_findings_zh: 本文概述了随时间变化的呼吸道疾病水平,包括提及 RSV (呼吸道合胞病毒) 和相关主题。但是,它不报告特定的 暴发 或事件。 [news-dffa8b70b4a1f75d]
李柯及其同事进行的一项研究发现,人类偏肺病毒(HMPV)暴发的出现时间受到呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)病毒干扰的影响,而不是受区域气候条件的影响。 [news-2c8c7922e074cec2]
据 Bioengineer.org 报道,一项临床前研究评估了鼻内 Poly I:C 佐剂与预输注 F 抗原结合使用以增强 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗 对小鼠的保护。 [news-f64dc77ec785af53]
据《汉密尔顿观察家》报道,流感和呼吸道合胞病毒正在汉密尔顿蔓延,甲型流感确诊病例和呼吸道合胞病毒检测不断上升。 [news-4d3a10ff82c63297]
一名65岁女性脊柱退行性患者最初出现类似普通感冒的轻微症状,如咳嗽、低烧、咽痛、咳痰等。然而,三天后,她出现严重呼吸困难、喘息和低氧血症,需要住院治疗并接受氧疗、无创通气和雾化。 [news-c4f7ead8b7cb900b]

news.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following Respiratory syncytial virus news developments.
key_findings_en: The article provides an overview of respiratory illness levels over time, including mentions of RSV (Respiratory Syncytial Virus) and related topics. However, it does not report a specific outbreak or event. [news-dffa8b70b4a1f75d]

A study conducted by Ke Li and colleagues found that the timing of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) outbreaks is influenced by viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), rather than regional climate conditions. [news-2c8c7922e074cec2]

A preclinical study evaluated the use of an intranasal Poly I:C adjuvant in combination with a prefusion F antigen to enhance respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine protection in mice, as reported by Bioengineer.org. [news-f64dc77ec785af53]
Flu and RSV are spreading in Hamilton, reported by The Hamilton Spectator, with confirmed cases of influenza A and rising RSV tests. [news-4d3a10ff82c63297]

A 65-year-old female patient with spinal degeneration initially presented with mild symptoms resembling a common cold, such as cough, mild fever, sore throat, and sputum production. [news-c4f7ead8b7cb900b]

papers.title: Cost-effectiveness of respiratory syncytial virus vaccines in post-marketing settings: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, particularly among infants and older adults worldwide. This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines. Methods In this review, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 20, 2025. Grey literature and reference lists were also searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for older adults and infants. Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions. Results Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval ( CI ): USD 41.89–168.21; I 2 = 93.2%]. For infants, the pooled INB was USD 5.81 (95% CI: USD − 35.44–47.07; I 2 = 89.4%). elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 在这篇综述中,检索了截至 2025 年 11 月 20 日的 PubMed、Embase、Web of Science 和 Cochrane 图书馆。还检索了灰色文献和参考文献列表。分别对老年人和婴儿进行随机效应荟萃分析。使用特定人群的亚组分析和单变量元回归探讨了异质性的潜在来源。

This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines.

Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. papers.title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 疫苗 在上市后环境中的成本效益:系统评价和荟萃分析。
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of acute lower respiratory infections, hospitalizations, and deaths, particularly among infants and older adults worldwide. This study aims to summarize cost-effectiveness evidence by pooling incremental net benefit (INB) estimates of marketed RSV vaccines. Methods In this review, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched through November 20, 2025. Grey literature and reference lists were also searched. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted separately for older adults and infants. Potential sources of heterogeneity were explored using population-specific subgroup analyses and univariable meta-regressions. Results Of the 17 studies included in the systematic review, 11 contributed to the primary meta-analysis and one additional study to sensitivity analysis only. Among older adults, the pooled INB was USD 105.05 [95% confidence interval ( CI ): USD 41.89–168.21; I 2 = 93.2%]. For infants, the pooled INB was USD 5.81 (95% CI: USD − 35.44–47.07; I 2 = 89.4%). In the European subgroup, the pooled INB among older adults was USD 123.63 (95% CI: USD 41.23–206.02; I 2 = 89.4%), while that for infants was USD 15.00 (95% CI: USD − 4.33–34.34; I 2 = 43.4%). Leave-one-out sensitivity analyses showed robust pooled INBs among older adults, whereas infant estimates were sensitive to study exclusion. Conclusions At the thresholds used in the included studies, RSV vaccination might be cost-effective for older adults in post-marketing settings, while the evidence for maternal vaccination remained inconclusive. Descriptive findings suggested that age- and risk-based targeting in older adults and seasonal maternal vaccination may yield higher INB estimates. Substantial between-study heterogeneity warrants cautious interpretation of the pooled estimates and highlights the need to consider local epidemiology and implementation conditions when developing RSV vaccination policies.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 背景 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是急性下呼吸道感染、住院和死亡的主要原因,特别是在全世界的婴儿和老年人中。本研究旨在通过汇总市售 RSV 疫苗 的增量净效益 (INB) 估计值来总结成本效益证据。方法 在这篇综述中,检索了截至 2025 年 11 月 20 日的 PubMed、Embase、Web of Science 和 Cochrane 图书馆。还检索了灰色文献和参考文献列表。分别对老年人和婴儿进行随机效应荟萃分析。使用特定人群的亚组分析和单变量元回归探讨了异质性的潜在来源。结果 在系统评价纳入的 17 项研究中,11 项参与了主要荟萃分析,另外一项研究仅参与了敏感性分析。在老年人中,汇总 INB 为 105.05 美元 [95% 置信区间 (CI):41.89–168.21 美元;I 2 = 93.2%]。对于婴儿,汇总 INB 为 5.81 美元(95% CI:USD − 35.44–47.07;I 2 = 89.4%)。在欧洲亚组中,老年人的汇总 INB 为 123.63 美元(95% CI:USD 41.23–206.02;I 2 = 89.4%),而婴儿的 INB 为 15.00 美元(95% CI:USD − 4.33–34.34;I 2 = 43.4%)。留一法敏感性分析显示,老年人中的汇总 INB 很稳健,而婴儿的估计值对研究排除很敏感。结论 在纳入研究中使用的阈值下,RSV 疫苗接种 对于上市后的老年人来说可能具有成本效益,而孕产妇 疫苗接种 的证据仍不确定。描述性研究结果表明,针对老年人和季节性母亲 疫苗接种 基于年龄和风险的目标可能会产生更高的 INB 估计值。研究间的显着异质性需要对汇总估计值进行谨慎解释,并强调在制定 RSV 流行病学 政策时需要考虑当地 流行病学 和实施条件。

papers.title: RSV bronchiolitis admissions in infants immunized with nirsevimab: a multicenter observational study.
papers.abstract: UNLABELLED: Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations. This study aimed to evaluate the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of RSV bronchiolitis admissions following successful nationwide implementation of nirsevimab. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study across 15 Spanish pediatric emergency departments during the 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants eligible for the RSV prophylaxis, defined as those younger than six months at the start of or during the RSV season, with laboratory-confirmed RSV bronchiolitis requiring hospitalization were included. Patients immunized fewer than seven days before admission or with unknown immunization status were excluded. Epidemiological and clinical data were analyzed according to nirsevimab status, with age-stratified and multivariable analyses performed. Among 366 hospitalized infants with RSV bronchiolitis, 345 were previously healthy. Of these, 165/345 (47.8%) had received nirsevimab. Breakthrough cases were younger than non-breakthrough cases (2.0 months [IQR, 1.1-3.6] vs 5.2 months [IQR, 3.3-6.6]; p < 0.001). Overall, immunized and non-immunized infants showed similar rates of pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission (26.7% vs 21.1%; p = 0.2) and length of hospital stay (5 days [IQR, 3-7] vs 5 days [IQR, 4-7]; p = 0.6). After age stratification, clinical characteristics and outcomes remained comparable between groups. In multivariable analyses, no statistically significant association was observed between nirsevimab immunization and PICU admission, advanced respiratory support, or length of hospital stay. CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status. These findings suggest that, once hospitalization is required, nirsevimab may offer limited additional protection against severe disease. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations. WHAT IS NEW: • In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status.

papers.title_zh: 接受 尼塞韦单抗 免疫的婴儿中 RSV 毛细支气管炎 入院:一项多中心观察研究。
papers.source_body_en: UNLABELLED: Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations. This study aimed to evaluate the epidemiological and clinical characteristics of RSV bronchiolitis admissions following successful nationwide implementation of nirsevimab. We conducted a retrospective multicenter study across 15 Spanish pediatric emergency departments during the 2024-2025 RSV season. Infants eligible for the RSV prophylaxis, defined as those younger than six months at the start of or during the RSV season, with laboratory-confirmed RSV bronchiolitis requiring hospitalization were included. Patients immunized fewer than seven days before admission or with unknown immunization status were excluded. Epidemiological and clinical data were analyzed according to nirsevimab status, with age-stratified and multivariable analyses performed. Among 366 hospitalized infants with RSV bronchiolitis, 345 were previously healthy. Of these, 165/345 (47.8%) had received nirsevimab. Breakthrough cases were younger than non-breakthrough cases (2.0 months [IQR, 1.1-3.6] vs 5.2 months [IQR, 3.3-6.6]; p < 0.001). Overall, immunized and non-immunized infants showed similar rates of pediatric intensive care unit (PICU) admission (26.7% vs 21.1%; p = 0.2) and length of hospital stay (5 days [IQR, 3-7] vs 5 days [IQR, 4-7]; p = 0.6). After age stratification, clinical characteristics and outcomes remained comparable between groups. In multivariable analyses, no statistically significant association was observed between nirsevimab immunization and PICU admission, advanced respiratory support, or length of hospital stay. CONCLUSIONS: In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status. These findings suggest that, once hospitalization is required, nirsevimab may offer limited additional protection against severe disease. WHAT IS KNOWN: • Real-world studies have confirmed the high effectiveness of nirsevimab, preventing approximately 80% of RSV bronchiolitis hospitalizations. WHAT IS NEW: • In-hospital outcomes of RSV bronchiolitis admissions did not differ significantly by immunization status.

papers.title: Enhanced respiratory syncytial virus surveillance of young children admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network, 2019-2023.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVES: In this study, we aimed to comprehensively describe the clinical characteristics, management and outcomes of children with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease admitted to the Sydney Children's Hospitals Network (SCHN), determine the full burden of severe disease and identify population-specific risk factors for intensive care unit (ICU) admission. STUDY TYPE: Multi-centre, retrospective cohort study conducted over 5 years. METHODS: The study was conducted at two tertiary paediatric hospitals in metropolitan New South Wales, Australia, before implementation of government-funded immunisation programs against RSV in children. Participants were children aged <2 years hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV from 1 January 2019 to 31 December 2023, comprising all ICU admitted, and a random sample of non-ICU admitted patients. The main outcome measures were characteristics and incidence rate of RSV hospitalisations and ICU admissions among children aged <2 years. RESULTS: Over a 5-year period, 4414 children were hospitalised with laboratory-confirmed RSV, of whom 11.3% (499/4414) were admitted to ICU. The median age was younger in the ICU cohort (n = 499) compared with the non-ICU sample (n = 1000; 3.3 vs 7.1 months, P < 0.0001). Factors associated with higher odds of ICU admission in multivariate logistic regression were decreasing month of age (OR 1.10, 95% CI 1.06-1.11), prematurity (OR 2.17, 95% CI 1.61-2.91), Indigenous identity (OR 4.10, 95% CI 2.30-7.56) and cardiac disease (OR 3.39, 95% CI 2.06-5.70). The average hospitalisation incidence rate was 1615 per 100,000 (95% CI 1565-1666), with higher rates among children aged <1 year, 2141 per 100,000 (95% CI 2061-2224) compared with those aged 1-2 years, 1088 per 100,000 (95% CI 1030-1148). CONCLUSIONS: RSV immunisation programs are expected to substantially reduce the burden of hospitalisation among Australian children in their first year of life. Children who are Indigenous, were born prematurely or have heart disease are at greatest risk of severe disease and may benefit from extended preventative programs.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States.
papers.abstract: Human metapneumovirus (HMPV) causes acute lower respiratory infections, primarily affecting young children and older adults, with seasonal outbreaks peaking annually in March or April in the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. However, the factors driving HMPV seasonality in the United States remain poorly understood. We analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases and age-specific emergency department visits across 10 US regions, fitting an age-stratified dynamic transmission model to assess spatiotemporal patterns and investigate the influence of environmental variables and viral interference from RSV on HMPV transmission rates. We found that models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all regions. Instead, HMPV timing was associated with RSV activity, with the HMPV transmission rate reduced in the presence of RSV. We showed that among the candidate models considered, only the models that included an RSV-associated term could reproduce the biennial pattern of HMPV observed in some regions, characterized by alternating "late-small" and "early-large" epidemics. When the best-fit model including the RSV-associated term was used to predict the potential impact of RSV interventions on HMPV transmission, we found that RSV interventions are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity despite reducing competition from RSV. Our work unravels the spatiotemporal dynamics of HMPV and its interaction with RSV, informing future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV.

papers.abstract_zh: 人类偏肺病毒 (HMPV) 会引起急性下呼吸道感染,主要影响幼儿和老年人,美国和北半球其他温带地区的季节性 暴发 高峰期为每年 3 月或 4 月。然而,人们对推动美国 HMPV 季节性的因素仍知之甚少。我们分析了美国 10 个地区的实验室确诊的 HMPV 病例和特定年龄的急诊科就诊情况,拟合了按年龄分层的动态 传播 模型,以评估时空模式,并研究环境变量和 RSV 病毒干扰对 HMPV 传播 发病率的影响。我们发现,将气候变量纳入 传播 速率(包括蒸气压、降水、潜在蒸散量和最低温度)的模型无法捕获所有地区 HMPV 活动的时间。相反,HMPV 时间与 RSV 活性相关,在 RSV 存在的情况下,HMPV 传播 率降低。我们表明,在考虑的候选模型中,只有包含 RSV 相关术语的模型才能重现在某些地区观察到的 HMPV 两年一次的模式,其特点是交替出现“晚期小规模”和“早期大规模”流行病。当使用包含 RSV 相关项的最佳拟合模型来预测 RSV 干预对 HMPV 传播 的潜在影响时,我们发现,尽管 RSV 的竞争减少,但 RSV 干预不太可能导致 HMPV 活性大幅增加。我们的工作揭示了 HMPV 的时空动态及其与 RSV 的相互作用,为未来的 HMPV 季节性预测和干预策略提供信息。

papers.title: Infant RSV immunity study (IRIS): protocol for a prospective birth cohort in Vancouver, Canada examining how age at respiratory syncytial virus exposure affects how infants respond to the virus immunologically.
papers.abstract: Introduction Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of severe respiratory illness in infants. Age at first infection is strongly associated with disease severity. Infants exposed to RSV at a younger age may not produce an immune response against RSV that is as protective as infection at a later age, and early life infection may influence the risk of recurrent or persistent wheezing, or subsequent asthma. However, how immune development at the time of exposure shapes RSV-specific immunity and long-term respiratory health remains unclear. Methods and analysis The Infant RSV Immunity Study (IRIS) is a prospective birth cohort of 300 healthy infants in British Columbia, Canada, followed to age 3 years. The primary objective is to determine how age at exposure influences RSV-specific immunity and respiratory outcomes. Infants are enrolled in April–June or September–November so that they enter the peak RSV season at either more than 6 months or less than 6 months of age. Symptom-triggered oropharyngeal nasal swabs and post-season RSV serology will identify RSV infections. Birth, pre-season dried blood spot and post-season blood samples will assess RSV-specific antibody, neutralisation, functional antibody and T-cell responses. Clinical outcomes include medically attended respiratory illness, RSV hospitalisation, daily wheezing and inhaler use, and asthma risk at age 3 assessed using the Childhood Asthma Risk Tool. A subgroup of infants will undergo infection-timed blood samples ⁓2 weeks into their first RSV infection. Maternal RSV vaccination and antibody status will be examined as determinants of infant responses. A microbiome upper-airway sample will be collected from the infant at 2 weeks, pre-season and post-season, and around PCR-confirmed RSV infection. In addition, serial stool samples will be collected at 2 weeks, 3, 6, 9 and 12 months of age. Analyses will distinguish developmental, seasonal and infection-associated influences on microbiome and immune development trajectories and test associations with antiviral responses, disease severity and recurrent wheezing post-RSV infection. Infants’ diet will be assessed by serial questionnaires, as another determinant of microbiome development. Ethics and dissemination The study was approved by the University of British Columbia Children’s and Women’s Research Ethics Board (H25-02623). Findings will be disseminated through publications, scientific meetings and participant communication. Trial registration number NCT07653347.

analysis.study_design_and_population: A prospective birth cohort of 300 healthy infants in British Columbia, Canada, followed from birth to age 3 years, was enrolled to examine the impact of age at RSV exposure on immunity and respiratory outcomes.

analysis.main_results: The study will identify how age at RSV exposure influences RSV-specific immunity and respiratory outcomes, with findings to be disseminated through publications, scientific meetings, and participant communication.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study aims to determine how immune development at the time of exposure shapes RSV-specific immunity and long-term respiratory health, providing novel insights into the relationship between age at exposure and immune response.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在了解首次接触 RSV 的年龄如何影响婴儿的 免疫应答 和呼吸系统健康,从而解决 RSV 免疫学和疾病严重程度方面的知识差距。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省 300 名健康婴儿进行了 队列研究 前瞻性出生试验,从出生到 3 岁进行随访,以检查 RSV 暴露年龄对免疫力和呼吸系统结果的影响。
elements_zh.methods: 婴儿在 4 月至 6 月或 9 月至 11 月期间入组,以确保他们在 6 个月以上或 6 个月以下进入 RSV 高峰季节。他们接受了症状触发的口咽鼻拭子、赛季后 RSV 血清学 以及连续血液和粪便样本,以评估 免疫应答 和临床结果。
elements_zh.main_results: 该研究将确定接触 RSV 的年龄如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和呼吸系统结果,研究结果将通过出版物、科学会议和参与者交流进行传播。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究旨在确定暴露时的免疫发育如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和长期呼吸道健康,为暴露时年龄与 免疫应答 之间的关系提供新的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以告知 监测、诊断 和 治疗 有关 RSV 感染的信息,以及 疫苗接种 策略和预防复发性或持续性喘息和哮喘的信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括其前瞻性设计以及对 免疫应答 的季节性和发育影响的可能性,这可能会限制普遍性。由于该研究的观察性质,证据强度中等。

papers.abstract_zh: 简介 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿严重呼吸道疾病的主要原因。首次感染的年龄与疾病的严重程度密切相关。在较年轻时接触 RSV 的婴儿可能不会产生像晚年感染那样具有保护作用的针对 RSV 的 免疫应答,并且早期感染可能会影响复发性或持续性喘息或随后的哮喘的风险。然而,暴露时的免疫发育如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和长期呼吸道健康仍不清楚。方法与分析 婴儿 RSV 免疫研究 (IRIS) 是对加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省 300 名健康婴儿进行的一项预期出生 队列研究,随访至 3 岁。主要目标是确定暴露年龄如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和呼吸系统结果。婴儿在 4 月至 6 月或 9 月至 11 月入学,以便他们在 6 个月以上或 6 个月以下时进入 RSV 高峰季节。症状触发的口咽鼻拭子和季后 RSV 血清学 将识别 RSV 感染。出生、季前干血斑和季后血液样本将评估 RSV 特异性抗体、中和、功能抗体和 T 细胞反应。临床结果包括呼吸系统疾病的就医、呼吸道合胞病毒住院、每日喘息和吸入器的使用,以及使用儿童哮喘风险工具评估的 3 岁时哮喘风险。一部分婴儿将在首次感染 RSV 后 ⁓2 周接受感染定时血液样本。母体 RSV 疫苗接种 和抗体状态将作为婴儿反应的决定因素进行检查。我们将在婴儿出生后 2 周、赛季前和赛季后以及 PCR 确认的 RSV 感染前后采集微生物组上呼吸道样本。此外,还将在 2 周、3、6、9 和 12 个月大时收集系列粪便样本。分析将区分发育、季节性和感染相关对微生物组和免疫发育轨迹的影响,并测试与 抗病毒药物 反应、疾病严重程度和 RSV 感染后反复喘息的关联。婴儿的饮食将通过系列调查问卷进行评估,作为微生物组发育的另一个决定因素。伦理与传播 该研究得到了不列颠哥伦比亚大学儿童和妇女研究伦理委员会 (H25-02623) 的批准。研究结果将通过出版物、科学会议和参与者交流来传播。试用注册号NCT07653347。

analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 对加拿大不列颠哥伦比亚省 300 名健康婴儿进行了 队列研究 前瞻性出生试验,从出生到 3 岁进行随访,以检查 RSV 暴露年龄对免疫力和呼吸系统结果的影响。
analysis_zh.methods: 婴儿在 4 月至 6 月或 9 月至 11 月期间入组,以确保他们在 6 个月以上或 6 个月以下进入 RSV 高峰季节。他们接受了症状触发的口咽鼻拭子、赛季后 RSV 血清学 以及连续血液和粪便样本,以评估 免疫应答 和临床结果。
analysis_zh.main_results: 该研究将确定接触 RSV 的年龄如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和呼吸系统结果,研究结果将通过出版物、科学会议和参与者交流进行传播。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究旨在确定暴露时的免疫发育如何影响 RSV 特异性免疫和长期呼吸道健康,为暴露时年龄与 免疫应答 之间的关系提供新的见解。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以告知 监测、诊断 和 治疗 有关 RSV 感染的信息,以及 疫苗接种 策略和预防复发性或持续性喘息和哮喘的信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的局限性包括其前瞻性设计以及对 免疫应答 的季节性和发育影响的可能性,这可能会限制普遍性。由于该研究的观察性质,证据强度中等。

papers.title: Beyond Croup: A Phenotype-Based Perspective on Parainfluenza Virus Types in Children.
papers.abstract: Human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) caused an estimated 18.8 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 725 000 hospitalizations, and 34 400 deaths among children under 5 in 2018, ranking second only to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) and their role in causing respiratory infections in children, with an emphasis on the distinct clinical and epidemiological characteristics of PIV types. The central question is whether PIVs should be considered as a single disease entity or as separate pathogens with unique impacts on pediatric health.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis of existing literature, with no explicit mention of systematic search methods, databases, or meta-analysis. papers.title_zh: 超越哮吼:基于表型的儿童副流感病毒类型视角。
papers.source_body_en: Human parainfluenza viruses (PIVs) caused an estimated 18.8 million acute lower respiratory infection episodes, 725 000 hospitalizations, and 34 400 deaths among children under 5 in 2018, ranking second only to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). Despite this burden, clinical attention has historically focused on croup, leading to the common perception that parainfluenza is a single disease entity. However, the 4 types differ substantially in taxonomy, tropism, clinical syndrome, and severity. PIV-1, the most common cause of croup, drives biennial epidemics in toddlers, whereas PIV-2 is less frequent but can cause severe disease, particularly in children with underlying conditions. PIV-3 predominates in young infants, causing bronchiolitis and pneumonia clinically like RSV infection, reflecting its early postnatal susceptibility, which may relate to earlier and more frequent viral exposure. PIV-4, historically underrecognized due to culture limitations, usually does not cause croup but is linked to lower respiratory tract disease, hypoxemia, and occasional neurologic complications. PIV infections are most severe in infants, immunocompromised children, and those in low-resource settings. Seasonal patterns vary by type and geography. Advances in multiplex molecular diagnostics now allow rapid type-specific detection, improving clinical interpretation and management. No vaccine or antiviral is licensed. Emerging therapeutics include sialidase-based antivirals with Food and Drug Administration Breakthrough designation; monoclonal antibodies capable of cross-neutralizing PIV-1, PIV-3, RSV, and human metapneumovirus; and messenger RNA vaccines showing early immunogenicity in children. Recognizing the distinct epidemiology, clinical features, and immune responses of each type is critical for informed pediatric care and the development of targeted preventive and therapeutic strategies.

papers.title: Generative AI-Designed Immunoglobulin Domain Antibodies (IgDAbs) Against the Fusion Protein as a Neutralizing Agent for Respiratory Syncytial Virus.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to rationally design, screen, and experimentally validate novel immunoglobulin domain antibodies (IgDAbs) targeting the site II epitope of the respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) fusion (F) protein using generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) driven tools. METHOD: A generative AI tool was employed to generate 250 novel IgDAb sequences optimized for RSV-F site II binding. Candidates were screened computationally using molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations to select hit candidates. The selected IgDAbs were cloned and produced using an E. coli expression system. Purified IgDAbs were characterized for target specificity via ELISA and evaluated for functional viral inhibition using in vitro microneutralization assay against RSV A2 (long strain). RESULT: Computational screening narrowed the library to 05 structurally compatible hit IgDAb with predicted binding affinity. ELISA confirmed specific binding of purified IgDAbs to the RSV-F protein. In vitro microneutralization assays demonstrated neutralization of RSV A2 (long strain), with two 'lead' IgDAbs showing EC50 of 1.3 μg/mL and 3.5 μg/mL. CONCLUSION: Combining generative AI sequence generation with an integrated in silico and in vitro screening cascade enables the rapid, cost-effective discovery of neutralizing nanobodies against RSV, offering a viable alternative to resource-intensive traditional antibody discovery workflows.

papers.title: Under pressure: lessons learnt from rapid implementation of the respiratory syncytial virus maternal vaccine and infant nirsevimab in Sydney, Australia.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.

papers.title_zh: 压力之下:从澳大利亚悉尼快速实施 呼吸道合胞病毒 孕产妇 疫苗 和婴儿 尼塞韦单抗 中吸取的经验教训。
papers.source_body_en: OBJECTIVE: To share lessons learnt from the Sydney Local Health District (SLHD) rollout of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prevention products, and present data on immunisation uptake for mothers and babies in two maternity hospitals. TYPE OF SERVICE: Rollout of the RSV maternal vaccine and the injectable, long-acting monoclonal antibody nirsevimab for newborn infants to protect them from RSV infection and hospitalisation. METHODS: Deidentified summary data from the electronic medical record on RSV immunisation status in two SLHD maternity hospitals were analysed descriptively as counts and proportions. The Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research was used as a lens to reflect on the rollout process. RESULTS: RSV vaccination coverage in women giving birth in two SLHD hospitals improved from 4% in the first month of rollout (February 2025) to a range of 70-74% from June to September 2025. As antenatal coverage improved, the number of live born babies requiring nirsevimab decreased. Among eligible newborns, 36% of families declined nirsevimab, with reason for refusal not recorded. Documentation of RSV immunisation status improved as the rollout progressed. LESSONS LEARNT: Engaging multidisciplinary leaders and clinicians is critical for a coordinated response and program rollout success. Leveraging existing education structures, staff meetings and using online prerecording can optimise clinician education. New programs take time to embed into routine clinical practice, and programs that involve delivering multiple immunisation products for distinct groups require clear messaging and systemic safeguards to prevent errors. Integrating immunisation into medical record workflows as standard practice can support program adoption and uptake.
papers.abstract_zh: 目标:分享悉尼地方卫生区 (SLHD) 推出 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 预防产品的经验教训,并提供两家妇产医院母亲和婴儿的免疫接种数据。服务类型:推出 RSV 母体 疫苗 和用于新生儿的可注射长效单克隆抗体 尼塞韦单抗,以保护他们免受 RSV 感染和住院治疗。方法:以计数和比例的形式对两家 SLHD 妇产医院的 RSV 免疫状况电子病历中的去识别化汇总数据进行描述性分析。实施研究综合框架被用作反思推出过程的镜头。结果:两家 SLHD 医院分娩妇女的 RSV 疫苗接种 覆盖率从推出第一个月(2025 年 2 月)的 4% 提高到 2025 年 6 月至 9 月的 70-74%。随着产前覆盖率的提高,需要 尼塞韦单抗 的活产婴儿数量减少。在符合条件的新生儿中,36%的家庭拒绝了尼塞韦单抗,但没有记录拒绝的原因。随着推广的进展,RSV 免疫状态的记录得到改善。经验教训:多学科领导者和临床医生的参与对于协调应对和计划成功推出至关重要。利用现有的教育结构、员工会议和使用在线预录音可以优化临床医生教育。新计划需要时间才能融入常规临床实践,而涉及为不同群体提供多种免疫产品的计划需要明确的信息传递和系统保障措施以防止错误。将免疫接种作为标准做法纳入医疗记录工作流程可以支持计划的采用和采用。

papers.title: Dissolving microneedle patches for needle-free and thermostable respiratory syncytial virus vaccination.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of acute lower respiratory tract disease, yet current prefusion F (preF)-based RSV vaccines depend on intramuscular injection and cold-chain distribution, limiting broad deployment. Dissolving microneedle array patches (MAPs) offer a minimally invasive, needle-free, and potentially thermostable alternative to conventional vaccine delivery. Here, we developed dissolving microneedle array patches loaded with an engineered prefusion-stabilized RSV F antigen (CL073A) and evaluated their potential as a needle-free, thermostable, and potent RSV vaccination platform. Following formulation screening, two lead CL073A-loaded MAPs (MAPs-CL073A) were identified that preserved antigenicity and mechanical performance and showed prolonged local antigen retention relative to intramuscular injection. In mice, MAPs-CL073A elicited markedly enhanced and durable humoral immunity, inducing approximately five-fold higher neutralizing antibody titers than intramuscular immunization at a ten-fold lower antigen dose, demonstrating a pronounced dose-sparing effect. In cotton rats, MAPs-CL073A conferred robust protection against RSV challenge by reducing lung viral burden and pulmonary pathology, with the 10 μg regimen (F2-MAP) achieving near-complete protection. Furthermore, the patches fully retained antigen bioactivity and in vivo immunogenicity after 6 months of room-temperature storage. Our findings establish that antigen delivery is a critical dimension of RSV vaccine performance and support dissolving microneedle delivery as a versatile strategy to enhance both the efficacy and deployability of RSV vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop a dissolving microneedle array patch (MAP) as a needle-free and thermostable platform for RSV vaccination. The researchers formulated and tested MAPs loaded with an engineered prefusion-stabilized RSV F antigen (CL073A) in mice and cotton rats. The results showed that the MAPs-CL073A formulation preserved antigenicity and mechanical performance, with prolonged local antigen retention compared to intramuscular injection. In cotton rats, the 10 μg regimen (F2-MAP) provided near-complete protection against RSV challenge by reducing lung viral burden and pulmonary pathology. The patches retained antigen bioactivity and immunogenicity after six months of room-temperature storage. These findings highlight the potential of dissolving microneedle delivery to enhance the efficacy and deployability of RSV vaccines. The study's evidence is strong, as it directly evaluated the performance of the MAPs-CL073A formulation in relevant animal models, supporting its use as a promising vaccination strategy.

papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 仍然是急性下呼吸道疾病的主要原因,但目前基于预灌注 F (preF) 的 RSV 疫苗 依赖于肌肉注射和冷链分布,限制了广泛部署。溶解微针阵列贴片 (MAP) 为传统 疫苗 输送提供了一种微创、无针且潜在耐热的替代方案。在这里,我们开发了装载有工程化预融合 RSV F 抗原 (CL073A) 的可溶性微针阵列贴片,并评估了它们作为无针、热稳定和有效的 RSV 疫苗接种 平台的潜力。经过配方筛选,鉴定出两种负载 CL073A 的先导 MAP (MAP-CL073A),它们保留了抗原性和机械性能,并显示出相对于肌内注射延长的局部抗原保留时间。在小鼠中,MAPs-CL073A 引发显着增强且持久的体液免疫,在低十倍的抗原剂量下诱导出比肌内免疫高约五倍的中和抗体滴度,表现出显着的剂量节约效应。在棉鼠中,MAPs-CL073A 通过减少肺部病毒负荷和肺部病理,提供针对 RSV 攻击的强大保护,其中 10 μg 方案 (F2-MAP) 实现了近乎完全的保护。此外,室温保存6个月后,贴剂完全保留了抗原生物活性和体内免疫原性。我们的研究结果表明,抗原递送是 RSV 疫苗 性能的一个关键维度,并支持溶解微针递送作为增强 RSV 疫苗 的功效和可部署性的通用策略。

papers.title: Predicting prolonged hospital stay in children hospitalised with respiratory syncytial virus infection: model development, internal validation and a calendar-year transportability assessment
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is the commonest cause of lower respiratory tract infection in young children, and length of stay dominates cost. Published RSV models mostly predict intensive-care outcomes from variables unavailable on a ward. We developed a model for prolonged stay from routine admission data and examined its transport across years. Retrospective cohort of children under 5 years admitted to general paediatric wards in Chengdu, China, with RSV confirmed by multiplex polymerase chain reaction, 2023–2025. Prolonged stay was 7 days or more. Fifteen admission variables were ranked by least absolute shrinkage and selection operator regression with 300 bootstrap resamples; retention required 95% selection frequency and stability across four specifications. Discrimination was assessed with 500-resample optimism correction, calibration by slope, intercept and Brier score against a constant-risk benchmark, and utility by decision curves. The primary model was refitted in 2023–2024 and applied unchanged to 2025. Of 494 admissions, 476 were analysed (median age 20.0 months; 57.6% boys); 106 (22.3%) stayed ≥ 7 days. Age (odds ratio 0.49 per 16.7 months, 95% CI 0.38–0.64), co-detection (1.73, 1.07–2.79) and lactate dehydrogenase (0.66 per 66.6 U/L, 0.51–0.86) were retained; AUC 0.708 (0.653–0.760), optimism-corrected 0.687, slope 1.00, Brier 0.158. Prolonged stay fell from 32.1% (62/193) to 15.5% (44/283) (p < 0.001). On transport discrimination was preserved (AUC 0.701, 0.623–0.772; slope 1.07) but risk was overestimated (intercept −0.82; predicted 28.3% vs observed 15.5%), and the Brier score (0.142) exceeded the constant-risk benchmark (0.131) until recalibrated (0.124). At a 20% threshold, 33.9% of 2025 admissions were low risk (negative predictive value 95.8%; 14 events missed per 1000). Prolonged stay fell from 32.1% (62/193) to 15.5% (44/283) (p < 0.001). At a 20% threshold, 33.9% of 2025 admissions were low risk (negative predictive value 95.8%; 14 events missed per 1000). Three routine admission variables predicted prolonged RSV stay with moderate discrimination, preserved across calendar years, whereas absolute risk was not and needs recalibration before use. The model suits ruling out a long stay, not escalation.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在开发一个模型来预测 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染儿童的住院时间延长,并评估其跨日历年的可运输性。RSV 是幼儿下呼吸道感染的最常见原因,住院时间长短是费用的主要因素。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项回顾性 队列研究 研究对 2023 年至 2025 年中国成都普通儿科病房收治的 5 岁以下儿童进行,通过多重聚合酶链式反应证实有 RSV。该研究纳入了 494 名入院儿童,其中 476 名进行了分析(中位年龄 20.0 个月;57.6% 是男孩);106 人 (22.3%) 停留 ≥ 7 天。

analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该模型确定了三个常规入院变量,这些变量预测 RSV 停留时间较长,并具有适度的歧视,并在历年中保留。然而,绝对风险并未保留,需要在使用前重新校准。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为开发工具提供信息,以排除 RSV 感染儿童长期住院的情况,从而有助于资源分配和临床决策。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究的证据因其回顾性设计和潜在的偏倚而受到限制。该模型的风险估计在应用于 2025 年数据时被高估,并且 Brier 评分在重新校准之前超过了恒定风险基准,表明证据强度中等。

papers.title: Incidence, shedding, and transmission of common respiratory viruses: data from a prospective, longitudinal, household cohort study in the Gambia from March 2021-June 2022.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings. We aimed to compare the epidemiology of multiple respiratory viruses within households in the Gambia. METHODS: We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year. Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables. FINDINGS: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03). We found evidence for reductions in incidence risk with increasing age for HRV, RSV, seasonal coronaviruses, and parainfluenza viruses, with no difference for SARS-CoV-2. Among 719 index infections, the mean household SARs for all viruses combined was 6.7%. Infection with prolonged shedding (p = 0.002), specific viral species (p < 0.0001) and a lower Ct value were associated with increased transmission. INTERPRETATION: A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species. FUNDING: This study was funded through a UK Research and Innovation grant.

A prospective household cohort study was conducted in a peri-urban region, enrolling households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, and following them for one year. Weekly upper respiratory tract swabs were collected and tested by RT-PCR for various viruses, including respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). However, the study's findings are limited by its single-location setting and lack of experimental controls, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title_zh: 常见呼吸道病毒的 发病率、脱落和 传播:数据来自 2021 年 3 月至 2022 年 6 月在冈比亚进行的一项前瞻性、纵向、家庭 队列研究 研究。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Respiratory viruses are a major cause of morbidity in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs), yet little is known about their incidence, risk factors, and transmission dynamics in community settings. We aimed to compare the epidemiology of multiple respiratory viruses within households in the Gambia. METHODS: We conducted a prospective household cohort study in a peri-urban region of the Gambia. Households with ≥5 members, including at least one adult and one child, were enrolled and followed for one year. Upper respiratory tract swabs were collected weekly, regardless of symptoms, and tested by RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, seasonal coronaviruses, human rhinovirus (HRV), influenza A/B, RSV A/B, parainfluenza viruses 1-4, human metapneumovirus, and adenovirus. We estimated incidence, symptomatic fraction, shedding duration, and household secondary attack rates (SARs), and explored associations with virus type and demographic variables. FINDINGS: From 2 March 2021 to 13 June 2022, 349 participants from 52 households completed 14,421 scheduled and 129 unscheduled visits. Respiratory viruses were detected in 11.1% of visits (n = 1611), representing 1423 infection episodes. HRV was most common, infecting 86.5% of participants (2.4 infections per person-year). Children aged <5 and 5-17 years shed virus for longer than adults (p = 0.0005), with longer shedding durations seen for HRV and SARS-CoV-2. Overall, 88.4% of infections were asymptomatic, with the highest symptomatic proportions for SARS-CoV-2 (16.3%) and RSV (17.7%) (p = 0.03). We found evidence for reductions in incidence risk with increasing age for HRV, RSV, seasonal coronaviruses, and parainfluenza viruses, with no difference for SARS-CoV-2. Among 719 index infections, the mean household SARs for all viruses combined was 6.7%. Infection with prolonged shedding (p = 0.002), specific viral species (p < 0.0001) and a lower Ct value were associated with increased transmission. INTERPRETATION: A large burden of asymptomatic infections underlies the circulation of respiratory viruses within households, with key differences in incidence, shedding and transmission across viral species. FUNDING: This study was funded through a UK Research and Innovation grant.

papers.title: Subtype-specific differences in susceptibility to monoclonal antibodies and vaccines among contemporary RSV-A and RSV-B isolates
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continues to circulate at high levels despite the introduction of new monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and vaccines targeting the pre-fusion F (pre-F) protein. We analyzed the viral genome sequences of 133 RSV clinical samples collected during the 2022–2023 and 2023–2024 seasons and selected representative isolates for phenotypic testing. We selected four RSV-A and four RSV-B replication-competent, sequence-verified stocks and then assessed them for replication kinetics in vitro and neutralization sensitivity with a panel of F-targeting mAbs and polyclonal sera using a rabbit vaccination model. Isolates retained sensitivity to all mAbs tested. We detected no mutations in mAb binding sites in the isolates tested. RSV-A isolates were slightly less susceptible to multiple mAbs than RSV-B isolates. Antigenic cartography revealed a separation of antibody responses by subtype: RSV-A isolates clustered together and aligned with lower neutralization by antibodies such as MPE8 and 101F, whereas RSV-B isolates formed a distinct cluster associated with higher mAb susceptibility. In a rabbit vaccination model, RSV-A-only sera efficiently neutralized all RSV-A isolates and the RSV-B1 reference strain but showed diminished activity against contemporary RSV-B isolates. RSV-B-only sera displayed balanced neutralization across both subtypes. Combined RSV-A + RSV-B immunization produced uniformly strong responses to all isolates, suggesting that multivalent exposure may overcome subtype-specific antibody polarization. Collectively, our results demonstrate consistent antigenic divergence of RSV subtypes and underscore the importance of using contemporary isolates, rather than legacy reference strains, to guide F-directed immunoprophylaxis and vaccine design. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of lower respiratory tract infections. Although new monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and vaccines have been approved in recent years, the impact of circulating genetic diversity on these therapeutics is incompletely understood. In this study, we demonstrate how recent RSV isolates respond to a panel of mAbs and whether sera from rabbits vaccinated with mRNA vaccines effectively neutralize these isolates. We observe that RSV-A isolates are slightly more resistant to neutralization by mAbs than RSV-B isolates and that a bivalent vaccine elicits broader neutralizing responses than the monovalent vaccine. This study provides insights into how viral diversity may influence antibody-mediated protection and suggests that recent RSV-B isolates may respond differently from the laboratory-adapted strains commonly used in research, an important consideration for the design of next-generation vaccines and antibody therapeutics.

elements_en.research_question_and_background: IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of lower respiratory tract infections.
elements_en.study_design_and_population: We analyzed the viral genome sequences of 133 RSV clinical samples collected during the 2022–2023 and 2023–2024 seasons and selected representative isolates for phenotypic testing.
elements_en.methods: We selected four RSV-A and four RSV-B replication-competent, sequence-verified stocks and then assessed them for replication kinetics in vitro and neutralization sensitivity with a panel of F-targeting mAbs and polyclonal sera using a rabbit vaccination model.
elements_en.main_results: In a rabbit vaccination model, RSV-A-only sera efficiently neutralized all RSV-A isolates and the RSV-B1 reference strain but showed diminished activity against contemporary RSV-B isolates.
elements_en.interpretation_and_novelty: Antigenic cartography revealed a separation of antibody responses by subtype: RSV-A isolates clustered together and aligned with lower neutralization by antibodies such as MPE8 and 101F, whereas RSV-B isolates formed a distinct cluster associated with higher mAb susceptibility.
elements_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: We observe that RSV-A isolates are slightly more resistant to neutralization by mAbs than RSV-B isolates and that a bivalent vaccine elicits broader neutralizing responses than the monovalent vaccine.
elements_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: This study provides insights into how viral diversity may influence antibody-mediated protection and suggests that recent RSV-B isolates may respond differently from the laboratory-adapted strains commonly used in research, an important consideration for the design of next-generation vaccines and antibody therapeutics.

papers.title_zh: 当代RSV-A和RSV-B分离株对单克隆抗体和疫苗的亚型特异性易感性差异
papers.source_body_en: ABSTRACT Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continues to circulate at high levels despite the introduction of new monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and vaccines targeting the pre-fusion F (pre-F) protein. We analyzed the viral genome sequences of 133 RSV clinical samples collected during the 2022–2023 and 2023–2024 seasons and selected representative isolates for phenotypic testing. We selected four RSV-A and four RSV-B replication-competent, sequence-verified stocks and then assessed them for replication kinetics in vitro and neutralization sensitivity with a panel of F-targeting mAbs and polyclonal sera using a rabbit vaccination model. Isolates retained sensitivity to all mAbs tested. We detected no mutations in mAb binding sites in the isolates tested. RSV-A isolates were slightly less susceptible to multiple mAbs than RSV-B isolates. Antigenic cartography revealed a separation of antibody responses by subtype: RSV-A isolates clustered together and aligned with lower neutralization by antibodies such as MPE8 and 101F, whereas RSV-B isolates formed a distinct cluster associated with higher mAb susceptibility. In a rabbit vaccination model, RSV-A-only sera efficiently neutralized all RSV-A isolates and the RSV-B1 reference strain but showed diminished activity against contemporary RSV-B isolates. RSV-B-only sera displayed balanced neutralization across both subtypes. Combined RSV-A + RSV-B immunization produced uniformly strong responses to all isolates, suggesting that multivalent exposure may overcome subtype-specific antibody polarization. Collectively, our results demonstrate consistent antigenic divergence of RSV subtypes and underscore the importance of using contemporary isolates, rather than legacy reference strains, to guide F-directed immunoprophylaxis and vaccine design. IMPORTANCE Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) remains a major cause of lower respiratory tract infections. Although new monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) and vaccines have been approved in recent years, the impact of circulating genetic diversity on these therapeutics is incompletely understood. In this study, we demonstrate how recent RSV isolates respond to a panel of mAbs and whether sera from rabbits vaccinated with mRNA vaccines effectively neutralize these isolates. We observe that RSV-A isolates are slightly more resistant to neutralization by mAbs than RSV-B isolates and that a bivalent vaccine elicits broader neutralizing responses than the monovalent vaccine. This study provides insights into how viral diversity may influence antibody-mediated protection and suggests that recent RSV-B isolates may respond differently from the laboratory-adapted strains commonly used in research, an important consideration for the design of next-generation vaccines and antibody therapeutics.
papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)尽管引入了新的单克隆抗体(mAbs)和疫苗,仍持续在高水平流行。我们分析了2022–2023和2023–2024季节收集的133份RSV临床样本的病毒基因组序列,并选择了代表性的分离株进行表型测试。我们选择了四种RSV-A和四种RSV-B具有复制能力且序列验证的株系,然后使用兔疫苗接种模型评估了它们的体外复制动力学和对F靶向单克隆抗体和多克隆血清的中和敏感性。所有测试的分离株均保留了对所有mAbs的敏感性。我们在测试的分离株中未检测到mAb结合位点的突变。RSV-A分离株对多种mAbs的中和敏感性略低于RSV-B分离株。抗原图谱显示了抗体反应的亚型分离:RSV-A分离株聚类在一起,并与如MPE8和101F等抗体的中和能力较低相一致,而RSV-B分离株则形成一个与较高mAb敏感性相关的独特聚类。在兔疫苗接种模型中,RSV-A-only血清能够有效中和所有RSV-A分离株和RSV-B1参考株,但对当代RSV-B分离株的中和活性有所减弱。RSV-B-only血清在两种亚型之间表现出平衡的中和能力。RSV-A + RSV-B联合免疫产生了对所有分离株一致的强反应,这表明多价暴露可能克服亚型特异性抗体极化。总体而言,我们的结果展示了RSV亚型之间一致的抗原差异,并强调了使用当代分离株而非传统参考株来指导F靶向免疫预防和疫苗设计的重要性。重要性 呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)仍然是下呼吸道感染的主要原因。尽管近年来批准了新的单克隆抗体(mAbs)和疫苗,但这些治疗药物对流行遗传多样性的影响仍不完全清楚。本研究探讨了近期RSV分离株对一组mAbs的反应情况,以及使用mRNA 疫苗免疫的兔血清是否能有效中和这些分离株。我们观察到RSV-A分离株对mAbs的中和能力略低于RSV-B分离株,并且双价疫苗比单价疫苗诱导更广泛的中和反应。本研究提供了关于病毒多样性如何影响抗体介导保护的见解,并表明近期RSV-B分离株可能与常用于研究的实验室适应株产生不同的反应,这对下一代疫苗和抗体治疗药物的设计具有重要意义。

papers.title: Forecasting Respiratory Syncytial Virus Activity Using Seasonal ARIMA Models: Evidence from CDC Weekly Surveillance Data
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) imposes seasonal operational pressure on paediatric care and hospital healthcare systems. This study evaluates whether weekly RSV test percent positivity data from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) can support short-term forecasting of RSV transmission activity. The national weekly surveillance dataset spanning 3 January 2015 to 27 June 2020 was analyzed with four forecasting approaches: seasonal autoreggressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), non-seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), and a seasonal naive benchmark model. Model predictive performance was validated via a 52-week chronological holdout sample and rolling-origin forecasts for 1–4 week ahead horizons. Multiple evaluation metrics were adopted, including root mean square error (RMSE), mean absolute error (MAE), symmetric mean absolute percentage error (sMAPE), directional accuracy, and peak-timing error. Exploratory time-series analyses verified prominent annual seasonality and short-term serial dependence embedded in RSV percent positivity time series. Among all candidate models, SARIMA yielded the smallest RMSE and MAE on the holdout dataset, and exhibited relatively robust performance as the forecast window extended. The overall findings demonstrate that surveillance-driven SARIMA forecasting can facilitate early epidemic warning and advance healthcare resource planning. Nevertheless, further external validation using post-pandemic and regional RSV surveillance datasets is required, as the sample only covers the pre-pandemic and early coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19 ) period.
papers.journal: International Journal of Biology and Life Sciences

analysis.summary_en: This study investigates the potential of using weekly RSV test percent positivity data from the CDC National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System (NREVSS) to forecast RSV transmission activity. The researchers analyzed four forecasting models: seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (SARIMA), non-seasonal autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA), exponential smoothing (ETS), and a seasonal naive benchmark model. They validated the models using a 52-week chronological holdout sample and rolling-origin forecasts for 1–4 week ahead horizons. The results showed that SARIMA performed best, with the smallest root mean square error (RMSE) and mean absolute error (MAE) on the holdout dataset, and maintained relatively robust performance as the forecast window extended. The study highlights the potential of surveillance-driven SARIMA forecasting to support early epidemic warning and healthcare resource planning. However, the authors note that further external validation using post-pandemic and regional RSV surveillance datasets is needed, as the current sample only covers the pre-pandemic and early coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) period. The findings suggest that SARIMA models could be valuable tools for predicting RSV activity, which may help in managing healthcare resources during seasonal outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 给儿科护理和医院医疗保健系统带来季节性运营压力。本研究评估来自疾病控制和预防中心 (CDC) 国家呼吸道和肠道病毒 监测 系统 (NREVSS) 的每周 RSV 检测阳性百分比数据是否可以支持 RSV 传播 活动的短期预测。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用四种预测方法对2015年1月3日至2020年6月27日的全国每周监测数据集进行了分析:季节性自回归综合移动平均线(SARIMA)、非季节性自回归综合移动平均线(ARIMA)、指数平滑(ETS)和季节性朴素基准模型。
elements_zh.methods: 模型的预测性能通过 52 周的时间保留样本和未来 1-4 周的滚动源预测进行了验证。采用多种评估指标,包括均方根误差(RMSE)、平均绝对误差(MAE)、对称平均绝对百分比误差(sMAPE)、方向精度和峰值时序误差。
elements_zh.main_results: 探索性时间序列分析验证了 RSV 阳性率时间序列中嵌入的显着的年度季节性和短期序列依赖性。在所有候选模型中,SARIMA 在保留数据集上产生了最小的 RMSE 和 MAE,并且随着预测窗口的扩展表现出相对稳健的性能。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 总体研究结果表明,监测 驱动的 SARIMA 预测可以促进早期流行病预警并推进医疗资源规划。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究提供的证据表明 SARIMA 模型可用于预测 RSV 活动,从而为季节性 暴发 的医疗资源规划和早期预警系统提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 尽管如此,仍需要使用大流行后和区域 RSV 监测 数据集进行进一步的外部验证,因为样本仅涵盖大流行前和早期的 2019 年冠状病毒病 (COVID-19) 时期。

papers.title: Respiratory syncytial virus in adults in Moscow (2024–2025) - a case series
papers.abstract: The role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the development of severe infections and decompensation of chronic diseases in adults is often underestimated. In the Russian Federation, data on the clinical course of RSV infection in adults are extremely limited. The article presents three clinical cases of RSV infection in adult patients identified during a prospective study of RSV prevalence among 1,544 patients with acute respiratory infection in Moscow (epidemic season 2024–2025). The first case is a severe exacerbation of asthma in a 73-year-old woman with obesity and hypertension, requiring hospitalization. The second case is RSV-associated pneumonia in a 39-year-old man without comorbidities, complicated by myocardial infarction on the second day of hospitalization; co-infection with coronavirus HKU-1. The third case is a prolonged course of RSV infection (acute tracheitis progressing to bronchitis) in a 75-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities, leading to decompensation of arterial hypertension. The presented cases illustrate various patterns of RSV infection in adults, highlighting the role of RSV as a trigger for exacerbation of chronic diseases and vascular events, as well as the challenges of differential diagnosis and management of such patients in real-world clinical practice. RSV infection in adults often remains overlooked by clinicians, despite its ability to cause severe outcomes even in patients without underlying risk factors. The heterogeneity of manifestations and the absence of pathognomonic symptoms necessitate the improvement of epidemiological surveillance and an in-depth study of the RSV burden to substantiate prevention strategies in vulnerable adult populations. Keywords: respiratory syncytial virus, adults, case series, comorbidity, myocardial infarction.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in the development of severe infections and decompensation of chronic diseases in adults is often underestimated. The study aimed to highlight the under-recognized impact of RSV in adult populations.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a case series presenting three clinical cases of RSV infection in adult patients identified during a prospective study of RSV prevalence among 1,544 patients with acute respiratory infection in Moscow during the epidemic season of 2024–2025.
analysis.methods: The study involved the identification of RSV cases through clinical evaluation and prospective data collection from patients with acute respiratory infection. The cases were analyzed for clinical manifestations, comorbidities, and outcomes.
analysis.main_results: The first case involved a severe exacerbation of asthma in a 73-year-old woman with obesity and hypertension, requiring hospitalization. The second case was RSV-associated pneumonia in a 39-year-old man without comorbidities, complicated by myocardial infarction on the second day of hospitalization and co-infection with coronavirus HKU-1. The third case was a prolonged course of RSV infection (acute tracheitis progressing to bronchitis) in a 75-year-old woman with multiple comorbidities, leading to decompensation of arterial hypertension.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that RSV can trigger exacerbations of chronic diseases and vascular events in adults, even in those without underlying risk factors. This case series provides novel insights into the diverse clinical presentations of RSV in adults.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings emphasize the need for improved recognition and management of RSV in adults, particularly in vulnerable populations, and suggest the importance of targeted surveillance and prevention strategies.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its case series design, which may not capture the full spectrum of RSV infection in adults. The evidence is moderate, as it is based on clinical observations rather than controlled trials.

analysis.summary_en: This case series highlights the under-recognized role of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in adults, particularly in triggering severe exacerbations of chronic diseases and vascular events. Three clinical cases from Moscow during the 2024–2025 epidemic season illustrate the varied manifestations of RSV infection, including severe asthma exacerbation, RSV-associated pneumonia with myocardial infarction, and prolonged infection leading to decompensation of arterial hypertension. The study underscores the importance of improving RSV surveillance and management in adults, especially those with comorbidities. However, the case series design limits the generalizability of the findings, and the evidence is considered moderate due to the observational nature of the study.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 在成人严重感染和慢性病失代偿中的作用常常被低估。该研究旨在强调 RSV 对成年人群的影响未被充分认识。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究是一个病例系列,介绍了 2024-2025 年流行季节莫斯科 1,544 名急性呼吸道感染患者中进行的 RSV 患病率 前瞻性研究中发现的 3 例成人 RSV 感染临床病例。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究通过临床评估和收集急性呼吸道感染患者的前瞻性数据来识别 RSV 病例。对病例的临床表现、合并症和结果进行分析。
elements_zh.main_results: The first case involved a severe exacerbation of asthma in a 73-year-old woman with obesity and hypertension,requiring hospitalization.第二例为RSV相关肺炎,患者为39岁男性,无合并症,住院第二天并发心肌梗塞,合并感染冠状病毒HKU-1。第三个病例是一名 75 岁女性,患有长期 RSV 感染(急性气管炎进展为支气管炎),患有多种合并症,导致动脉高血压失代偿。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者解释说,RSV 可以引发成人慢性疾病和血管事件的恶化,即使是那些没有潜在危险因素的人。该病例系列为成人 RSV 的不同临床表现提供了新颖的见解。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调需要改进成人尤其是弱势群体对 RSV 的认识和管理,并表明有针对性的 监测 和预防策略的重要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其病例系列设计而受到限制,可能无法涵盖成人 RSV 感染的全部谱系。证据是中等的,因为它是基于临床观察而不是对照试验。

papers.title: Sendai virus, a candidate vaccine for the prevention of respiratory virus infections in children: a review
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory viruses including human parainfluenza virus (hPIV), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and human metapneumovirus (hMPV), pose serious, potentially lethal threats to humans, particularly infants and young children. While maternal vaccines and monoclonal antibodies are advancing to provide transient protection against these viruses, licensed pediatric vaccines are not yet available. Sendai virus (SeV) is now being developed as an intranasal (I.N.) vaccine candidate for the prevention of serious respiratory viral infections in children. Methods To examine the potential of replication-competent Sendai virus and its recombinants as pediatric respiratory virus vaccines against hPIV, RSV and hMPV, we searched literature databases and evaluated both historical and contemporary published research. Results SeV and SeV recombinant vaccines have been tested pre-clinically in a variety of animal models and in Phase I clinical studies. In pre-clinical models, a single dose of SeV induced rapid and long-lasting B- and T-cell responses in the upper respiratory tract and blood. When recombinant SeV constructs were produced and formulated into cocktail vaccines, they were protective against four different respiratory pathogens simultaneously. Vaccines were successful when partnered with passively transferred antibodies; specifically, when a recombinant SeV-based RSV vaccine was tested in the presence of passively transferred monoclonal or polyclonal PIV-specific or RSV-specific antibodies in a cotton rat model, the vaccine provided durable protective immunity against RSV. In clinical trials, SeV was well-tolerated and uniformly immunogenic in PIV-seropositive 1–2 year old children. Methods have been developed for the manufacture of stable SeV-based vaccine products, compatible with wide global distribution of SeV vaccines for clinical use. Conclusion To date, results highlight SeV as an attractive pediatric vaccine candidate. Continued clinical testing of SeV may provide global relief from serious respiratory viral infections in infants and young children.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates Sendai virus (SeV) as a potential vaccine candidate for preventing serious respiratory viral infections in children, particularly against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The study highlights the pre-clinical and early clinical testing of SeV and its recombinants, demonstrating their ability to induce immune responses and offer protection against multiple pathogens. The findings suggest that SeV could be a promising vaccine for pediatric use, though the evidence is limited to early-phase studies and lacks detailed limitations or strength assessments. The review underscores the need for further clinical trials to validate SeV's efficacy and safety in this population.

Results SeV and SeV recombinant vaccines have been tested pre-clinically in a variety of animal models and in Phase I clinical studies. In pre-clinical models, a single dose of SeV induced rapid and long-lasting B- and T-cell responses in the upper respiratory tract and blood. When recombinant SeV constructs were produced and formulated into cocktail vaccines, they were protective against four different respiratory pathogens simultaneously. Vaccines were successful when partnered with passively transferred antibodies; specifically, when a recombinant SeV-based RSV vaccine was tested in the presence of passively transferred monoclonal or polyclonal PIV-specific or RSV-specific antibodies in a cotton rat model, the vaccine provided durable protective immunity against RSV. In clinical trials, SeV was well-tolerated and uniformly immunogenic in PIV-seropositive 1–2 year old children. Methods have been developed for the manufacture of stable SeV-based vaccine products, compatible with wide global distribution of SeV vaccines for clinical use. Conclusion To date, results highlight SeV as an attractive pediatric vaccine candidate. Continued clinical testing of SeV may provide global relief from serious respiratory viral infections in infants and young children.

papers.title: Temporal dynamics of respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients in Shanghai, 2019–2023: a multi-center longitudinal surveillance study
papers.abstract: COVID-19 greatly reshaped the epidemiology of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.This study explored temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic. A retrospective multi-center observational study was performed across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China (2019–2023). Hospitalized SARI patients aged ≥ 15 years were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). We stratified the study period into pre-pandemic (2019), pandemic (2020–2022), and post-pandemic (2023) phases for comparative analysis. In total, 4738 participants were enrolled. The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) ( P <0.001). A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established: (1) decline-resurgence for influenza virus (IFV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ), Bordetella pertussis ( B. pertussis ), and human bocavirus (HBoV); (2) sustained decline for human parainfluenza virus (HPIV), human coronavirus (HCoV), human adenovirus (HAdV), human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV), and Legionella pneumophila ( L. pneumophila ); (3) transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV); (4) continuous increase for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). IFV, HRV/EV, and HCoV consistently ranked top five across all periods. pneumoniae was the dominant pathogen (33.65%) in patients aged 15–44 years. Seasonal peaks of IFV and RSV were substantially reshaped in the post-pandemic period. The co-infection rate was 1.14% (54/4738), with IFV- M. pneumoniae was the most combination (20.37%). Respiratory pathogen circulation patterns changed substantially from 2019 to 2023. Persistent multi-pathogen surveillance is required to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This study aimed to explore the temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic, as the epidemiology of SARI was greatly reshaped by COVID-19, yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective multi-center observational study was conducted across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China, from 2019 to 2023, enrolling a total of 4738 hospitalized SARI patients aged ≥ 15 years.
analysis.methods: Hospitalized SARI patients were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR).
analysis.main_results: The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) (P < 0.001).
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study established a novel classification of four distinct temporal trends, including a continuous increase for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings highlight the need for persistent multi-pathogen surveillance to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the temporal dynamics of respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients in Shanghai from 2019 to 2023. A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established, with respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) showing a continuous increase. The evidence is strong due to the large sample size and comprehensive testing, but the observational design may limit the confidence in causal interpretations.

papers.title_zh: 2019-2023年上海成人SARI患者呼吸道病原体时间动态:多中心纵向监测研究
papers.source_body_en: COVID-19 greatly reshaped the epidemiology of severe acute respiratory infection (SARI), yet long-term shifts in multi-pathogen circulation remain poorly characterized.This study explored temporal patterns of common respiratory pathogens among adult SARI patients before, during, and after the pandemic. A retrospective multi-center observational study was performed across seven sentinel hospitals in Shanghai, China (2019–2023). Hospitalized SARI patients aged ≥ 15 years were tested for 12 respiratory pathogens (22 subtypes) using real-time polymerase chain reaction (RT-PCR). We stratified the study period into pre-pandemic (2019), pandemic (2020–2022), and post-pandemic (2023) phases for comparative analysis. In total, 4738 participants were enrolled. The overall pathogen detection rate decreased from 30.26% in the pre-pandemic period (2019) to 16.50% during the pandemic (2020–2022), then rebounded to 20.07% in the post-pandemic period (2023) ( P <0.001). A novel classification of four distinct temporal trends was established: (1) decline-resurgence for influenza virus (IFV), Mycoplasma pneumoniae ( M. pneumoniae ), Bordetella pertussis ( B. pertussis ), and human bocavirus (HBoV); (2) sustained decline for human parainfluenza virus (HPIV), human coronavirus (HCoV), human adenovirus (HAdV), human rhinovirus/enterovirus (HRV/EV), and Legionella pneumophila ( L. pneumophila ); (3) transient peak for human metapneumovirus (HMPV); (4) continuous increase for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). IFV, HRV/EV, and HCoV consistently ranked top five across all periods. pneumoniae was the dominant pathogen (33.65%) in patients aged 15–44 years. Seasonal peaks of IFV and RSV were substantially reshaped in the post-pandemic period. The co-infection rate was 1.14% (54/4738), with IFV- M. pneumoniae was the most combination (20.37%). Respiratory pathogen circulation patterns changed substantially from 2019 to 2023. Persistent multi-pathogen surveillance is required to guard against single-pathogen outbreaks and concurrent multi-pathogen epidemics.
papers.abstract_zh: COVID-19 极大地重塑了严重急性呼吸道感染 (SARI) 的 流行病学,但多病原体循环的长期变化仍知之甚少。本研究探讨了成人 SARI 患者在大流行之前、期间和之后常见呼吸道病原体的时间模式。对中国上海七家哨点医院(2019-2023)进行了回顾性多中心观察研究。使用实时聚合酶链反应 (RT-PCR) 对年龄≥ 15 岁的住院 SARI 患者进行了 12 种呼吸道病原体(22 种亚型)检测。我们将研究时期分为大流行前(2019年)、大流行(2020-2022年)和大流行后(2023年)三个阶段进行比较分析。总共有 4738 名参与者参加。总体病原检出率从疫情前期(2019年)的30.26%下降至疫情期间(2020-2022年)的16.50%,随后反弹至疫情后期(2023年)的20.07%( P <0.001)。建立了四种不同时间趋势的新分类:(1)流感病毒(IFV)、肺炎支原体(M.pneumoniae)、百日咳博德特氏菌(B.pertussis)和人博卡病毒(HBoV)的下降-复苏;(2)人副流感病毒(HPIV)、人冠状病毒(HCoV)、人腺病毒(HAdV)、人鼻病毒/肠道病毒(HRV/EV)、嗜肺军团菌(L. pneumophila)持续下降;(3)人偏肺病毒(HMPV)瞬时峰;(4)持续增加呼吸道合胞病毒(RSV)。IFV、HRV/EV 和 HCoV 在所有时期均排名前五。肺炎链球菌是15-44岁患者的主要病原体(33.65%)。IFV 和 RSV 的季节性峰值在大流行后时期大幅重塑。合并感染率为1.14%(54/4738),其中以IFV-肺炎支原体合并感染最多(20.37%)。从 2019 年到 2023 年,呼吸道病原体循环模式发生了很大变化。需要持续的多病原体 监测 来防范单一病原体 暴发 和并发的多病原体流行。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨成人 SARI 患者在大流行之前、期间和之后常见呼吸道病原体的时间模式,因为 SARI 的 流行病学 被 COVID-19 极大地重塑,但多病原体循环的长期变化仍知之甚少。

papers.title: AS01E-adjuvanted RSV pre-F protein vaccine in adults with lung or kidney transplant: a phase 2b randomized trial.
papers.abstract: Immunocompromised adults are at increased risk of severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease. This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01E-adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30–60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients. The authors report results from a randomized phase 2 trial showing that the adjuvanted RSVPreF3 vaccine was immunogenic and had an acceptable safety profile in lung and kidney transplant recipients, supporting a favorable benefit-risk profile.
authors: On behalf of the RSV OA=ADJ-023 Study Group
