This multicountry, open-label phase 2b trial (NCT05921903) evaluated the immunogenicity and safety of the AS01 E -adjuvanted RSV prefusion F protein vaccine (adjuvanted RSVPreF3) over 12 months in kidney or lung transplant recipients ≥18 years, randomized 1:1 to receive one (n = 131) or two doses 30-60 days apart (n = 130). A control group of non-immunocompromised adults ≥50 years (n = 125) received a single dose. The primary outcome was the mean geometric increase in RSV-A and RSV-B neutralizing titers one month following a second adjuvanted RSVPreF3 dose relative to the first dose in transplant recipients. Secondary outcomes included assessment of the safety and immunogenicity of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in transplant recipients compared with the control group. In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups. Humoral and cell-mediated immune responses remained above baseline for 12 months post-vaccination. Both doses of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 were well tolerated and had a similar and acceptable safety profile. Overall, these results support a favorable benefit-risk profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in kidney and lung transplant recipients.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 免疫功能低下的成年人患严重 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疾病的风险增加。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项多国开放标签 2b 期试验评估了 AS01E 佐剂 RSV 预融合 F 蛋白 疫苗(佐剂 RSVPreF3)在 18 岁以上肾移植或肺移植受者中为期 12 个月的免疫原性和安全性,按 1:1 随机分配接受一剂 (n = 131) 或间隔 30-60 天的两剂 (n = 130)。对照组由 50 岁以上的非免疫功能低下成年人 (n = 125) 接受单剂治疗。
elements_zh.methods: 主要结果是移植受者在接受第二次辅助 RSVPreF3 剂量一个月后,RSV-A 和 RSV-B 中和滴度相对于第一剂的平均几何增加。次要结果包括与对照组相比,移植受者中添加佐剂的 RSVPreF3 的安全性和免疫原性的评估。
elements_zh.main_results: In transplant recipients receiving two doses, neutralizing titers against RSV-A and RSV-B were numerically higher one month post-dose 2 than post-dose 1 (mean geometric increases: 1.34 [95% CI: 1.20, 1.48] for RSV-A [n = 111] and 1.26 [95% CI: 1.14, 1.40] for RSV-B [n = 111]). A single dose was immunogenic in transplant recipients, but showed slower and generally lower initial neutralizing responses than in non-immunocompromised controls, specifically in individuals receiving mycophenolate. RSVPreF3-specific CD4 + T-cell frequencies increased after vaccination versus baseline in all groups.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 两种剂量的 RSVPreF3 佐剂均具有良好的耐受性,并且具有相似且可接受的安全性。总体而言,这些结果支持在肾移植和肺移植受者中添加佐剂的 RSVPreF3 具有良好的获益-风险特征。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 免疫应答 后 12 个月内,体液和细胞介导的 免疫应答 保持高于基线。这些发现表明,佐剂 RSVPreF3 疫苗 可以为免疫功能低下的个体提供持续的保护。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 作者报告了一项随机 2 期试验的结果,显示佐剂 RSVPreF3 疫苗 具有免疫原性,并且在肺和肾移植受者中具有可接受的安全性,支持有利的获益风险概况。然而,该研究是开放标签的,样本量相对较小,这可能会限制研究结果的普遍性。

papers.title: Vaccine profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in adults: prevention of RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and emerging evidence of potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits.
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and hospitalization in older adults, individuals with certain chronic medical conditions, and immunocompromised patients. RSV can result in acute and longer-term cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity, and declines in physical functioning and quality of life. AREAS COVERED: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 was the first RSV vaccine licensed for preventing RSV-LRTD in adults, with initial approvals in 2023 in the United States and Europe. Robust clinical trial data showed an acceptable safety profile and demonstrated efficacy against RSV-LRTD, with exploratory post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in RSV-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)/asthma exacerbations. These findings are reinforced by real-world evidence showing effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations, COPD/asthma exacerbations, and cardiovascular events. EXPERT OPINION: This emerging evidence supports a broader role of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 beyond preventing RSV-LRTD alone to preserve cardiovascular and respiratory health. RSV vaccination should be considered within an integrated routine care and preventive management strategy for older adults and individuals with chronic conditions, alongside other adult immunizations and health interventions. Addressing implementation barriers for adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and emphasizing its role in maintaining health and independence will be critical to enable widespread uptake and help protect patient health.

papers.title_original: Vaccine profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in adults: prevention of RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and emerging evidence of potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits.

analysis.scope_and_question: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and hospitalization in older adults, individuals with certain chronic medical conditions, and immunocompromised patients. The review focuses on the vaccine profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in adults, specifically its prevention of RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease and emerging evidence of potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on clinical trial data and real-world evidence. Robust clinical trial data showed an acceptable safety profile and demonstrated efficacy against RSV-LRTD, with exploratory post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in RSV-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)/asthma exacerbations. These findings are reinforced by real-world evidence showing effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations, COPD/asthma exacerbations, and cardiovascular events.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 was the first RSV vaccine licensed for preventing RSV-LRTD in adults, with initial approvals in 2023 in the United States and Europe. The vaccine has shown efficacy against RSV-LRTD and has emerging evidence suggesting potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits, including reductions in COPD/asthma exacerbations and effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations and cardiovascular events.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review notes that while the clinical trial data supports the safety and efficacy of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 against RSV-LRTD, the exploratory post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in COPD/asthma exacerbations and cardiovascular events are not definitive. The evidence for these broader benefits is still emerging and requires further validation.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: RSV vaccination should be considered within an integrated routine care and preventive management strategy for older adults and individuals with chronic conditions, alongside other adult immunizations and health interventions. Addressing implementation barriers for adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and emphasizing its role in maintaining health and independence will be critical to enable widespread uptake and help protect patient health.

analysis.summary_en: This review evaluates the vaccine profile of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 in adults, focusing on its prevention of RSV-related lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and emerging evidence of potential cardiovascular and respiratory benefits. RSV is a significant cause of LRTD and hospitalization in older adults, individuals with chronic conditions, and immunocompromised patients. Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 was the first RSV vaccine licensed for preventing RSV-LRTD in adults, with initial approvals in 2023 in the United States and Europe. Clinical trial data demonstrated an acceptable safety profile and efficacy against RSV-LRTD, with post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in COPD/asthma exacerbations. Real-world evidence further supports its effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations and cardiovascular events. While the findings are promising, the evidence for broader benefits remains emerging and requires further validation. The review emphasizes the importance of integrating RSV vaccination into routine care and preventive strategies for high-risk populations, alongside addressing implementation barriers to promote widespread uptake.

papers.title_zh: 成人中添加佐剂的 RSVPreF3 的 疫苗 概况:预防 RSV 相关的下呼吸道疾病以及潜在心血管和呼吸系统益处的新证据。
papers.source_body_en: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is an important cause of lower respiratory tract disease (LRTD) and hospitalization in older adults, individuals with certain chronic medical conditions, and immunocompromised patients. RSV can result in acute and longer-term cardiovascular and respiratory morbidity, and declines in physical functioning and quality of life. AREAS COVERED: Adjuvanted RSVPreF3 was the first RSV vaccine licensed for preventing RSV-LRTD in adults, with initial approvals in 2023 in the United States and Europe. Robust clinical trial data showed an acceptable safety profile and demonstrated efficacy against RSV-LRTD, with exploratory post-hoc analyses suggesting reductions in RSV-related chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)/asthma exacerbations. These findings are reinforced by real-world evidence showing effectiveness against RSV-related hospitalizations, COPD/asthma exacerbations, and cardiovascular events. EXPERT OPINION: This emerging evidence supports a broader role of adjuvanted RSVPreF3 beyond preventing RSV-LRTD alone to preserve cardiovascular and respiratory health. RSV vaccination should be considered within an integrated routine care and preventive management strategy for older adults and individuals with chronic conditions, alongside other adult immunizations and health interventions. Addressing implementation barriers for adjuvanted RSVPreF3 and emphasizing its role in maintaining health and independence will be critical to enable widespread uptake and help protect patient health.

papers.title: The "ever-vaccinated" stock-flow bias in adult RSV vaccine policy evaluation: A methodological caution and a flow-based remedy.
papers.abstract: ABSTRACT Adult respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines are recommended as a single dose without routine revaccination; cumulative “ever-vaccinated” coverage is therefore a stock variable rising mechanically each season. Prior guidance implies this stock–flow distinction, yet no study has provided a portable, instrument-agnostic remedy or quantified this decomposition for the 2025–26 season. Using weekly 2025–26 U.S. National Immunization Survey data, we decomposed cumulative coverage into a prior-season stock and current-season flow, approximating the stock by the season-opening estimate. As of the latest available 2025–26 data (week ending 2026–02-21; mid-season snapshot), 84.9% of coverage among adults 75+ (43.2%) and 82.9% among high-risk adults 50–74 (32.8%) was attributable to prior-season stock – only 15–17% reflected current-season behavior; this stock share is an empirical approximation, not an exact decomposition. In two exploratory region-level quasi-experiments, the flow metric showed no sustained uptake acceleration (all primary tests p ≥ .19; a transient early-season gap, p = .008 post hoc, did not persist); these underpowered analyses are illustrative only, not identified for the policy effect. To our knowledge, this is the first portable flow-metric operationalization for survey and registry data, released as open code. Registry data exploratorily show the stock metric can obscure equity monitoring (Gini 0.210→0.202; range 39.7→43.5 pp; not significant). As a mid-season snapshot, these figures are an upper bound on the end-of-season value; the conclusion that coverage is dominated by prior-season stock holds through the season. RSV policy evaluation should pre-specify current-season flow as the primary outcome and report the stock share as a strongly recommended diagnostic.

Prior guidance implies this stock–flow distinction, yet no study has provided a portable, instrument-agnostic remedy or quantified this decomposition for the 2025–26 season. Using weekly 2025–26 U.S. National Immunization Survey data, we decomposed cumulative coverage into a prior-season stock and current-season flow, approximating the stock by the season-opening estimate. As of the latest available 2025–26 data (week ending 2026–02-21; mid-season snapshot), 84.9% of coverage among adults 75+ (43.2%) and 82.9% among high-risk adults 50–74 (32.8%) was attributable to prior-season stock – only 15–17% reflected current-season behavior; this stock share is an empirical approximation, not an exact decomposition. In two exploratory region-level quasi-experiments, the flow metric showed no sustained uptake acceleration (all primary tests p ≥ .19; a transient early-season gap, p = .008 post hoc, did not persist); these underpowered analyses are illustrative only, not identified for the policy effect. To our knowledge, this is the first portable flow-metric operationalization for survey and registry data, released as open code. Registry data exploratorily show the stock metric can obscure equity monitoring (Gini 0.210→0.202; range 39.7→43.5 pp; not significant). As a mid-season snapshot, these figures are an upper bound on the end-of-season value; the conclusion that coverage is dominated by prior-season stock holds through the season. RSV policy evaluation should pre-specify current-season flow as the primary outcome and report the stock share as a strongly recommended diagnostic.
papers.title_original: The "ever-vaccinated" stock-flow bias in adult RSV vaccine policy evaluation: A methodological caution and a flow-based remedy.

papers.title: Respiratory Infections at Mass Gatherings: A Travel-Medicine Review with Hajj and Umrah as a Longitudinal Case Study.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mass gatherings combine international mobility with dense, repeated contact and can amplify respiratory infections across travel corridors. Hajj, Umrah and Kumbh Mela, offer a uniquely recurrent case study, while other religious or sporting mega-events, and music or cultural festivals provide contrasting exposure systems. METHODS: A focused narrative review was conducted of peer-reviewed studies, systematic and scoping reviews, and authoritative public-health guidance. Searches and project evidence synthesis prioritized publications from January 2021 to August 2026, with selected foundational sources. We examined respiratory symptoms, laboratory detections, clinical disease, vaccination, antimicrobial use and resistance, surveillance, environmental modifiers, and pre-, during-, and post-travel practice. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias scoring was undertaken. RESULTS: Respiratory risk is determined less by attendance alone than by contact intensity, duration, ventilation, vocalization, shared accommodation, traveler susceptibility, and pathogen circulation. Recent Hajj evidence confirms a substantial burden of respiratory symptoms and clinical consultations, but estimates vary because denominators range from volunteers and tested samples to healthcare encounters. Rhinovirus, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and bacterial pneumonia remain important. There is continued abuse of antibiotics for predominantly viral syndromes and acquisition of resistant organisms link individual care to global antimicrobial resistance. Syndromic, laboratory, event-based, genomic, and wastewater surveillance are complementary, not interchangeable. Heat, dust, air quality, fatigue, and differential access to protective infrastructure modify respiratory symptoms, severity, and care seeking. Comparative events share mechanisms but not directly transferable rates. CONCLUSIONS: Travel-medicine practice should treat mass gatherings as longitudinal exposure systems spanning preparation, transport, the event, and return. Layered vaccination, risk-based masking, ventilation and crowd-flow measures, prompt diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and explicit travel histories, can reduce respiratory morbidity while preserving denominator discipline and access to protective infrastructure.

papers.title_zh: 大型集会中的呼吸道感染:以朝觐和副朝为纵向案例研究的旅行医学回顾。
papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Mass gatherings combine international mobility with dense, repeated contact and can amplify respiratory infections across travel corridors. Hajj, Umrah and Kumbh Mela, offer a uniquely recurrent case study, while other religious or sporting mega-events, and music or cultural festivals provide contrasting exposure systems. METHODS: A focused narrative review was conducted of peer-reviewed studies, systematic and scoping reviews, and authoritative public-health guidance. Searches and project evidence synthesis prioritized publications from January 2021 to August 2026, with selected foundational sources. We examined respiratory symptoms, laboratory detections, clinical disease, vaccination, antimicrobial use and resistance, surveillance, environmental modifiers, and pre-, during-, and post-travel practice. No meta-analysis or formal risk-of-bias scoring was undertaken. RESULTS: Respiratory risk is determined less by attendance alone than by contact intensity, duration, ventilation, vocalization, shared accommodation, traveler susceptibility, and pathogen circulation. Recent Hajj evidence confirms a substantial burden of respiratory symptoms and clinical consultations, but estimates vary because denominators range from volunteers and tested samples to healthcare encounters. Rhinovirus, influenza, SARS-CoV-2, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and bacterial pneumonia remain important. There is continued abuse of antibiotics for predominantly viral syndromes and acquisition of resistant organisms link individual care to global antimicrobial resistance. Syndromic, laboratory, event-based, genomic, and wastewater surveillance are complementary, not interchangeable. Heat, dust, air quality, fatigue, and differential access to protective infrastructure modify respiratory symptoms, severity, and care seeking. Comparative events share mechanisms but not directly transferable rates. CONCLUSIONS: Travel-medicine practice should treat mass gatherings as longitudinal exposure systems spanning preparation, transport, the event, and return. Layered vaccination, risk-based masking, ventilation and crowd-flow measures, prompt diagnostics, antimicrobial stewardship, and explicit travel histories, can reduce respiratory morbidity while preserving denominator discipline and access to protective infrastructure.
papers.abstract_zh: 背景:大型集会将国际流动性与密集、反复接触结合在一起,可能会加剧旅行走廊中的呼吸道感染。朝觐、副朝和大壶节提供了独特的循环案例研究,而其他宗教或体育大型活动以及音乐或文化节则提供了对比鲜明的曝光系统。方法:对同行评审的研究、系统性和范围界定的评审以及权威的公共卫生指导进行重点叙述性评审。搜索和项目证据综合优先考虑 2021 年 1 月至 2026 年 8 月的出版物,并选择基础来源。我们检查了呼吸道症状、实验室检测、临床疾病、疫苗接种、抗菌药物的使用和耐药性、监测、环境调节剂以及旅行前、旅行期间和旅行后的实践。没有进行荟萃分析或正式的偏倚风险评分。结果:呼吸风险不仅仅取决于出勤率,还取决于接触强度、持续时间、通风、发声、共用住宿、旅行者易感性和病原体循环。最近的朝觐证据证实了呼吸道症状和临床咨询的巨大负担,但估计有所不同,因为分母范围从志愿者和测试样本到医疗保健遭遇。鼻病毒、流感、SARS-CoV-2、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和细菌性肺炎仍然很重要。主要针对病毒性综合症的抗生素持续滥用,耐药微生物的获得将个人护理与全球抗菌素耐药性联系起来。综合征、实验室、基于事件、基因组和废水 监测 是互补的,不可互换。高温、灰尘、空气质量、疲劳和防护基础设施的差异会改变呼吸道症状、严重程度和寻求护理的情况。比较事件共享机制,但不直接转移速率。结论:旅行医学实践应将群众集会视为涵盖准备、运输、活动和返回的纵向暴露系统。分层的 疫苗接种、基于风险的掩蔽、通风和人群流动措施、及时诊断、抗菌药物管理和明确的旅行史,可以减少呼吸道疾病发病率,同时保持分母纪律和保护性基础设施的使用。

papers.title: Surveillance of adverse events following immunisation in Australia, 2024.
papers.abstract: This report summarises Australia's spontaneous surveillance data for adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) for all vaccines administered in 2024, reported to the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA). An adverse event(s) following immunisation is defined as any untoward medical occurrence which follows immunisation but does not necessarily have a causal relationship with use of the vaccine. Analyses of AEFI data are done continuously and also annually to detect new potential safety issues or changes to known safety issues. Overall, there were 6,232 AEFI reports for vaccines administered in 2024. This represents an annual AEFI reporting rate of 22.9 per 100,000 population and 25.7 per 100,000 vaccine doses, compared with 20.8 per 100,000 population and 24.1 per 100,000 doses in 2023. The slight increase in the AEFI reporting rates observed in 2024 was likely driven by the introduction of a new recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) which replaced the live attenuated zoster vaccine (ZLV, Zostavax) on the National Immunisation Program (NIP) from November 2023, along with the expansion of the eligible population for zoster vaccination. In 2024, RZV (Shingrix) was associated with the highest number of reported AEFIs. The most frequently reported adverse events following immunisation were medication errors; hypersensitivity; gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms; pyrexia; and injection site reaction. Among vaccines newly introduced in 2024, the most commonly reported adverse events were medication errors and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for COVID-19 vaccines (Comirnaty XBB.1.5 and Spikevax XBB.1.5); hypersensitivity and pyrexia for the DTPa-HepB-IPV-Hib vaccine (Vaxelis); medication errors and exposure during pregnancy for the adjuvanted recombinant respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) pre-fusion F protein vaccine (Arexvy); and hypersensitivity and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms for RZV (Shingrix). Fewer deaths were reported following vaccination in 2024 (28 reports) than in 2023 (34 reports). None of the 28 reported deaths in 2024 indicated an emerging safety signal.

analysis.research_question_and_background: This report addresses the need to monitor adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) to ensure vaccine safety, particularly for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccines. The study aimed to evaluate the safety profile of vaccines administered in 2024, with a focus on RSV-related adverse events.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study is a national surveillance report conducted in Australia during 2024, encompassing all vaccines administered in the country. It includes data from the Therapeutic Goods Administration (TGA) on adverse events reported across the population.
analysis.methods: AEFI data were collected through spontaneous reporting to the TGA and analysed continuously and annually to identify new safety concerns or changes in known safety issues. The analyses focused on the frequency and types of adverse events associated with vaccines, including RSV vaccines.
analysis.main_results: In 2024, there were 6,232 AEFI reports for vaccines administered, with RZV (Shingrix) associated with the highest number of reported AEFIs. The most frequently reported adverse events were medication errors, hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal nonspecific symptoms, pyrexia, and injection site reactions.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret that the slight increase in AEFI reporting rates in 2024 was likely due to the introduction of the new recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV) and the expansion of the eligible population for zoster vaccination. This finding highlights the importance of monitoring new vaccines for safety signals.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings inform the ongoing surveillance of vaccine safety, particularly for RSV vaccines, and support the need for continued monitoring of adverse events to ensure public health safety and improve vaccine programs.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is based on spontaneous reporting, which may introduce bias and underreporting. The evidence is moderate as it relies on observational data rather than controlled experiments, and the interpretation is grounded in the observed trends.

analysis.summary_en: This study reports on adverse events following immunisation (AEFI) in Australia for all vaccines administered in 2024. It highlights that RZV (Shingrix) was associated with the highest number of AEFI reports, with medication errors, hypersensitivity, gastrointestinal symptoms, pyrexia, and injection site reactions being the most frequently reported. The authors suggest that the slight increase in AEFI rates compared to 2023 may be attributed to the introduction of RZV and the expanded eligible population for zoster vaccination. The findings underscore the importance of continuous vaccine safety monitoring and provide insights into the safety profile of RSV vaccines. However, the study's reliance on spontaneous reporting introduces potential biases, and the evidence is considered moderate in strength.

papers.title: Immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain and efforts to shield it.
papers.abstract: Protein subunit and mRNA vaccines encoding viral glycoprotein antigens fused to the bacteriophage T4 fibritintrimerization domain are increasingly being tested in human clinical trials. AREXVY and ABRYSVO®, subunit vaccines composed of respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) prefusion F glycoprotein(s) fused to Foldon, are now FDA-approved and regularly administered. However, administration of vaccine antigens containing the Foldon domain has the potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. Here, we demonstrate that protein subunit vaccine antigens RSV F Foldon and influenza hemagglutinin (HA) Foldon elicit antibodies against the Foldon domain. To dampen Foldon-induced antibody responses, we engineered influenza computationally optimized broadly reactive antigen (COBRA) HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations at three different sites in Foldon. Mass spectrometry analyses confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of the three intended sites. Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens demonstrated reduced binding by anti-Foldon monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies compared to the wild-type COBRA HA Foldon. However, mice immunized with the COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens did not have a significant reduction in the elicitation of anti-Foldon antibodies. Further analysis suggested that some of the observed differences in antibody binding to mutant Foldon antigens can be attributed to differences in protein sequence alone. Altogether, these data suggest that while the N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon from reactive antibodies, this shielding does not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. Importantly, these data highlight that the Foldon trimerization domain is immunogenic, which should be considered during clinical trials of vaccines that contain Foldon.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the potential immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain in vaccines and its impact on eliciting off-target antibody responses.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved engineered influenza HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations in the Foldon domain and evaluated their immunogenicity in mice.
analysis.methods: The researchers used mass spectrometry to analyze N-glycosylation modifications and assessed antibody binding using monoclonal and polyclonal antibodies against the Foldon domain.
analysis.main_results: Two of the three COBRA HA Foldon mutant antigens showed reduced binding by anti-Foldon antibodies, but mice immunized with these mutants did not have a significant reduction in anti-Foldon antibody elicitation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that while N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield the Foldon domain, they do not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These results should inform the design of clinical trials for vaccines containing Foldon, highlighting the need to consider its immunogenicity.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited to mice and does not account for human immune responses, which may differ. The evidence is moderate in strength due to these limitations.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immunogenicity of the Foldon trimerization domain in vaccines, focusing on its potential to elicit off-target antibody responses. The researchers engineered influenza HA proteins with N-glycosylation motif mutations in Foldon and evaluated their immunogenicity in mice. Mass spectrometry confirmed partial occupancy of N-glycosylation modifications at two of three intended sites, and antibody binding was assessed. Two of the three mutant antigens showed reduced binding by anti-Foldon antibodies, but mice immunized with these mutants did not have a significant reduction in anti-Foldon antibody elicitation. The results suggest that while N-glycosylation modifications may partially shield Foldon, they do not significantly reduce its immunogenicity in a naïve setting. These findings highlight the importance of considering Foldon's immunogenicity during vaccine development and clinical trials. The study is limited to mice and does not account for human immune responses, which may differ, resulting in moderate evidence strength.

papers.title: Genomic diversity of respiratory pathogens in clinical versus community surveillance: a comparative analysis of SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza viruses in Washington State
papers.abstract: BackgroundGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses typically relies on sequences from individuals seeking health care, and whether these sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community is not well-characterized. We aimed to compare the diversity, proportion, and dynamics of influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and SARS-CoV-2 between clinical and community samples. MethodsIn this retrospective comparative genomic analysis, we used whole-genome sequences from community-based surveillance studies in the Seattle area, and clinical sequences from the Washington State Department of Health. We compared clade proportions and dynamics, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values between clinical and community samples. FindingsWe analyzed 538 RSV sequences collected between 2019 and 2021 (278 community, 260 clinical), 1506 influenza sequences (260 community, 1246 clinical) between 2019 and 2020, and 8660 SARS-CoV-2 sequences (5923 community, 2737 clinical) from 2020 to 2022. Clade proportions did not differ between clinical and community samples for RSV or influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2: clades 21J (Delta) and 21K (Omicron BA.1) were more frequent in community samples and clade 22B (Omicron BA.5) in clinical samples. SARS-CoV-2 clinical sequence clusters were more diverse than community clusters, whereas RSV and influenza showed no significant difference. Several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples for SARS-CoV-2. Ct values were lower in clinical samples for multiple SARS-CoV-2, RSV, and influenza clades. InterpretationSeasonal respiratory viruses had similar dynamics and diversity in clinical and community samples, whereas pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differed between settings. Genomic surveillance programs should combine clinical and community sampling, particularly during pandemics in order to better capture viral diversity. FundingThis analysis was funded by the Washington State Department of Health Northwest Pathogen Genomics Center of Excellence (WA DOH contract number HED29377-1, federal grant number NU50CK000630 to University of Washington). The underlying studies were funded by Gates Ventures. RESEARCH IN CONTEXTO_ST_ABSEvidence before this studyC_ST_ABSGenomic surveillance of respiratory viruses expanded substantially during the COVID-19 pandemic and has since been extended to respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and influenza, but most sequences come from people who sought medical care. We searched PubMed for studies published in English up to September 2026 using combinations of terms "genomic surveillance", "community surveillance", "respiratory syncytial virus", "influenza", "SARS-CoV-2", "whole genome sequencing", and included studies that sequenced respiratory viruses from defined clinical or community populations. Previous work has sampled hospitalized patients, sequenced random positive specimens, or sequenced wastewater, and has shown that such data can track variant emergence, clade replacement, and nosocomial transmission. However, few studies compared clinical and community sampling for the same virus in the same population and period, so it remains unclear whether clinically derived sequences represent the viruses circulating in the community. Added value of this studyTo our knowledge, this is the first study to compare viral diversity between clinical and community sampling for three respiratory viruses in the same region and overlapping time periods. Using more than 10,000 whole genomes from community-based surveillance studies and state clinical surveillance in Washington State, we found that clade proportions and dynamics were similar between sources for RSV and influenza, but differed for SARS-CoV-2. At finer genetic resolution, clinical SARS-CoV-2 sequences formed more diverse clusters than community sequences, and several spike mutations associated with monoclonal antibody resistance were more prevalent in community samples. Implications of all the available evidenceFor seasonal respiratory viruses, sampling people who seek care appears to capture much of the diversity circulating in the community, which may allow surveillance programs with limited resources to rely on clinical specimens. In contrast with seasonal circulation in a population with some pre-existing immunity, during pandemic-level transmission, when very large numbers of people in a largely susceptible population are infected over a short period, clinical and community samples are not interchangeable, and programs that sequence only clinical specimens risk missing variants circulating in the community, including mutations relevant to antiviral and monoclonal antibody resistance. These differences may partly reflect the much larger number of SARS-CoV-2 genomes available, as well as heterogeneous mixing and co-circulation of multiple variants during the pandemic. Surveillance programs should therefore combine clinical and community sampling, and future studies should test whether these patterns hold in other regions, seasons, and pathogens.

analysis.summary_en: This study compares the genomic diversity of respiratory viruses between clinical and community samples in Washington State, focusing on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and SARS-CoV-2. The research question addresses the gap in understanding whether clinical sequences accurately represent community viral circulation. The study design involves a retrospective comparative genomic analysis using sequences from both clinical and community sources. Whole-genome sequencing was employed to assess clade proportions, sequence-cluster diversity, non-synonymous mutations, and Ct values. The main results show that RSV and influenza had similar clade proportions and diversity in both settings, while SARS-CoV-2 showed differences, with community samples having more frequent clades 21J and 21K, and clinical samples showing more diversity in sequence clusters. The authors interpret these findings as indicating that seasonal respiratory viruses have comparable dynamics in clinical and community settings, but pandemic SARS-CoV-2 differs significantly. The study suggests that genomic surveillance programs should integrate both clinical and community sampling, especially during pandemics, to capture full viral diversity. The evidence strength is moderate, as the study is based on abstract-only data and does not report specific limitations.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景呼吸道病毒的基因组监测通常依赖于寻求医疗保健的个体的序列,并且这些序列是否代表社区中传播的病毒尚不清楚。我们的目的是比较临床和社区样本之间流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和 SARS-CoV-2 的多样性、比例和动态。方法在这项回顾性比较基因组分析中,我们使用了来自西雅图地区基于社区的 基因组 研究的全 基因组 序列,以及来自华盛顿州卫生部的临床序列。我们比较了临床和社区样本之间的进化枝比例和动态、序列簇多样性、非同义 突变 以及 Ct 值。研究结果我们分析了 2019 年至 2021 年收集的 538 个 RSV 序列(278 个社区,260 个临床),2019 年至 2020 年收集的 1506 个流感序列(260 个社区,1246 个临床),以及 2020 年至 2022 年收集的 8660 个 SARS-CoV-2 序列(5923 个社区,2737 个临床)。进化枝比例没有差异RSV 或流感的临床样本和社区样本之间存在差异,但 SARS-CoV-2 存在差异:社区样本中的进化枝 21J (Delta) 和 21K (Omicron BA.1) 更为常见,而临床样本中的进化枝 22B (Omicron BA.5) 则更为常见。SARS-CoV-2 临床序列簇比社区簇更加多样化,而 RSV 和流感则没有显着差异。与单克隆抗体耐药性相关的几个尖峰 突变 在 SARS-CoV-2 社区样本中更为普遍。多个 SARS-CoV-2、RSV 和流感分支的临床样本中的 Ct 值较低。解释季节性呼吸道病毒在临床和社区样本中具有相似的动态和多样性,而大流行的 SARS-CoV-2 在不同环境中则不同。基因组监测 计划应结合临床和社区采样,特别是在大流行期间,以便更好地捕获病毒多样性。资助本分析由华盛顿州卫生部西北病原体基因组学卓越中心资助(华盛顿州卫生部合同号 HED29377-1,华盛顿大学联邦拨款号 NU50CK000630)。基础研究由盖茨风险投资公司资助。CONTEXTO_ST_ABS 研究之前的证据 C_ST_ABS 呼吸道病毒的基因组 监测 在 COVID-19 大流行期间大幅扩展,此后已扩展到 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和流感,但大多数序列来自寻求医疗护理的人。我们使用术语“基因组监测”、“社区 监测”、“呼吸道合胞病毒”、“流感”、“SARS-CoV-2”、“整个 基因组 测序”的组合检索了 PubMed 中截至 2026 年 9 月以英文发表的研究,并纳入了对来自特定临床或社区人群的呼吸道病毒进行测序的研究。之前的工作对住院患者进行了采样,对随机阳性样本进行了测序,或对废水进行了测序,并表明这些数据可以跟踪变异的出现、进化枝替换和医院 传播。然而,很少有研究比较同一人群和时期内同一病毒的临床和社区采样,因此尚不清楚临床衍生的序列是否代表社区中传播的病毒。这项研究的附加值据我们所知,这是第一项比较同一地区和重叠时间段内三种呼吸道病毒的临床和社区采样之间的病毒多样性的研究。使用来自华盛顿州社区 监测 研究和州临床 监测 的 10,000 多个完整 基因组,我们发现 RSV 和流感来源之间的进化枝比例和动态相似,但 SARS-CoV-2 不同。在更精细的遗传分辨率下,临床 SARS-CoV-2 序列比群落序列形成更多样化的簇,并且与单克隆抗体耐药性相关的几个尖峰 突变 在群落样本中更为普遍。所有可用证据的含义对于季节性呼吸道病毒,对寻求护理的人进行采样似乎可以捕获社区中传播的大部分多样性,这可能使资源有限的 监测 项目能够依赖临床标本。与具有一定免疫力的人群中的季节性循环相反,在大流行水平的传播期间,当很大程度上易感人群中的大量人在短时间内被感染时,临床和社区样本不可互换,并且仅对临床样本进行测序的程序存在缺失社区中传播的变异的风险,包括与抗病毒药物和单克隆抗体耐药性相关的突变。这些差异可能部分反映了可用的 SARS-CoV-2 基因组 数量大得多,以及大流行期间多种变体的异质混合和共同循环。因此,监测 计划应结合临床和社区抽样,未来的研究应测试这些模式是否适用于其他地区、季节和病原体。

papers.title: An enhanced electrochemiluminescence immunosensor based on PtCo/UiO-66-NH2@luminol for highly sensitive detection of recombinant RSV F protein.
papers.abstract: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. The development of sensitive and reliable methods for the detection of RSV proteins is therefore of great significance for disease prevention and control. In this study, a sandwich-type electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor was developed for the highly sensitive detection of recombinant RSV F protein. A glassy carbon electrode (GCE) was modified with gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) to leverage their excellent conductivity and biocompatibility. The Au NPs not only facilitated electron transfer at the electrode interface but also provided a stable platform for immobilizing the capture antibody (Ab 1 ). The immunosensor was fabricated by sequentially assembling chitosan and Ab 1 on the Au NPs/GCE, blocking with BSA, capturing RSV F protein, and introducing an Ab 2 /PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 @luminol probe, with Ab 1 immobilized by physical adsorption. A multifunctional PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 nanocomposite was further designed, with PtCo providing peroxidase-like catalytic activity and UiO-66-NH 2 supplying abundant adsorption sites and amino functional groups. This composite enabled efficient stepwise loading of luminol molecules and detection antibodies (Ab 2 ), thereby achieving cascaded amplification of ECL signals in an H 2 O 2 coreactant system. In the presence of recombinant RSV F protein, a stable "electrode-Ab 1 -RSV F protein-Ab 2 -probe" sandwich complex was formed. Under optimized conditions, the ECL intensity showed a good linear relationship with recombinant RSV F protein concentration in the range of 0.1 pg mL -1 to 10 ng mL -1 , with a calculated detection limit of 0.025 pg mL -1 , experimentally verified at this concentration (n = 6). The proposed biosensor exhibited excellent stability, specificity, and reproducibility, providing a sensitive and reliable proof-of-concept platform for the detection of recombinant RSV F protein, which may serve as a foundation for future clinical validation.

papers.title_zh: 基于 PtCo/UiO-66-NH2@luminol 的增强型电化学发光免疫传感器,用于高灵敏度检测重组 RSV F 蛋白。
papers.source_body_en: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes severe lower respiratory tract infections in infants and young children. The development of sensitive and reliable methods for the detection of RSV proteins is therefore of great significance for disease prevention and control. In this study, a sandwich-type electrochemiluminescence (ECL) biosensor was developed for the highly sensitive detection of recombinant RSV F protein. A glassy carbon electrode (GCE) was modified with gold nanoparticles (Au NPs) to leverage their excellent conductivity and biocompatibility. The Au NPs not only facilitated electron transfer at the electrode interface but also provided a stable platform for immobilizing the capture antibody (Ab 1 ). The immunosensor was fabricated by sequentially assembling chitosan and Ab 1 on the Au NPs/GCE, blocking with BSA, capturing RSV F protein, and introducing an Ab 2 /PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 @luminol probe, with Ab 1 immobilized by physical adsorption. A multifunctional PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 nanocomposite was further designed, with PtCo providing peroxidase-like catalytic activity and UiO-66-NH 2 supplying abundant adsorption sites and amino functional groups. This composite enabled efficient stepwise loading of luminol molecules and detection antibodies (Ab 2 ), thereby achieving cascaded amplification of ECL signals in an H 2 O 2 coreactant system. In the presence of recombinant RSV F protein, a stable "electrode-Ab 1 -RSV F protein-Ab 2 -probe" sandwich complex was formed. Under optimized conditions, the ECL intensity showed a good linear relationship with recombinant RSV F protein concentration in the range of 0.1 pg mL -1 to 10 ng mL -1 , with a calculated detection limit of 0.025 pg mL -1 , experimentally verified at this concentration (n = 6). The proposed biosensor exhibited excellent stability, specificity, and reproducibility, providing a sensitive and reliable proof-of-concept platform for the detection of recombinant RSV F protein, which may serve as a foundation for future clinical validation.
papers.abstract_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 会导致婴儿和幼儿严重的下呼吸道感染。因此,开发灵敏、可靠的RSV蛋白检测方法对于疾病预防和控制具有重要意义。在本研究中,开发了一种夹心型电化学发光(ECL)生物传感器,用于高灵敏度检测重组RSV F蛋白。用金纳米粒子 (Au NP) 修饰玻碳电极 (GCE),以利用其优异的导电性和生物相容性。Au NP 不仅促进了电极界面上的电子转移,而且还为固定捕获抗体 (Ab 1 ) 提供了稳定的平台。该免疫传感器的制备方法是将壳聚糖和 Ab 1 依次组装在 Au NPs/GCE 上,用 BSA 封闭,捕获 RSV F 蛋白,并引入 Ab 2 /PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 @luminol 探针,并通过物理吸附固定 Ab 1。进一步设计了多功能PtCo/UiO-66-NH 2 纳米复合材料,其中PtCo提供类似过氧化物酶的催化活性,UiO-66-NH 2 提供丰富的吸附位点和氨基官能团。该复合材料能够有效地逐步加载鲁米诺分子和检测抗体(Ab 2 ),从而在H 2 O 2 共反应体系中实现ECL信号的级联放大。在重组RSV F蛋白存在下,形成稳定的“电极-Ab 1 -RSV F蛋白-Ab 2 -探针”夹心复合物。在优化条件下,ECL强度与重组RSV F蛋白浓度在0.1 pg mL -1 至10 ng mL -1 范围内表现出良好的线性关系,计算检测限为0.025 pg mL -1,经该浓度实验验证(n = 6)。所提出的生物传感器表现出优异的稳定性、特异性和重现性,为重组RSV F蛋白的检测提供了灵敏且可靠的概念验证平台,可作为未来临床验证的基础。

papers.title: Hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of respiratory viral infections in Spain: A population-based study using hospital data (2019-2023).
papers.abstract: INTRODUCTION: Respiratory viral infections are a major cause of hospitalization, morbidity, mortality, and healthcare resource use in Spain. Although influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) account for most of the healthcare burden, the contribution of other respiratory viruses has been less studied. This study aimed to analyze the hospital burden, clinical severity, and economic impact of these infections during the 2019-2023 period. METHODS: A retrospective population-based study was conducted using the Spanish Minimum Basic Data Set (CMBD), including hospitalizations with a diagnosis of respiratory viral infection between 2019 and 2023. Influenza, RSV, adenovirus, metapneumovirus, parainfluenza, and rhinovirus were analyzed. RESULTS: A total of 154,753 hospitalizations were included (mean age: 39 years; 48.6% female). Influenza and RSV accounted for most hospitalizations and total costs. A marked reduction in hospitalizations was observed in 2021, followed by recovery in 2022-2023. RSV, metapneumovirus, rhinovirus, and adenovirus predominantly affected the pediatric population, whereas influenza and parainfluenza had a greater impact on older adults. Overall, 6.5% of patients required ICU admission and in-hospital mortality was 2.7%, highest for influenza (4.2%). Metapneumovirus and rhinovirus showed the highest ICU admission rates. Mean hospital stay was 6.1 days (7.4 days in ICU). Although influenza and RSV generated the highest total costs, other viruses showed higher costs per episode. CONCLUSIONS: Respiratory viral infections impose a substantial healthcare and economic burden, with variable impact according to virus type and age group, highlighting the need for integrated surveillance, prevention, and healthcare planning strategies.

papers.title: Three-Year Polymerase Chain Reaction-Based Surveillance of Respiratory Tract Infections in Adults and Seasonal Patterns.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the aetiological composition, seasonal variation and risk factors of adult respiratory tract infections in Ganzhou, Jiangxi Province, during 2023-2025. METHODS: A total of 8,493 adults (≥18 years) with respiratory symptoms were enrolled from a tertiary hospital during 2023-2025. Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter-spring (December-March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78-3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89-3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24-2.01) were independent risk factors. CONCLUSION: Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter-spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance - with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter-spring months - and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.

Oropharyngeal and nasopharyngeal swabs were tested using multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction (PCR) panels targeting six categories of seven respiratory pathogens: influenza A and B viruses, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), parainfluenza virus types I and III, adenovirus and Mycoplasma pneumoniae. Mixed infections (two or more pathogens) were reported separately. Data were analysed by univariate analysis and multivariate logistic regression. Results The overall pathogen detection rate was 4.14% (352/8,493), comprising 325 single infections (92.33%) and 27 mixed infections (7.67%). Among single infections, M. pneumoniae (39.69%), influenza A virus (28.00%) and RSV (16.00%) predominated. Infections peaked in winter-spring (December-March). Age ≥65 years (OR = 2.35, 95% CI: 1.78-3.09), underlying diseases (OR = 2.41, 95% CI: 1.89-3.08) and emergency department admission (OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.24-2.01) were independent risk factors. Conclusion Adult respiratory infections in Ganzhou show clear winter-spring seasonality, with M. pneumoniae, influenza A virus and RSV as leading pathogens. These findings support seasonally targeted surveillance - with enhanced monitoring for M. pneumoniae and influenza during winter-spring months - and prioritised vaccination, expanded diagnostic panels and early PCR-based diagnosis for adults aged ≥65 years and those with underlying diseases, thereby strengthening local respiratory infection prevention and control strategies.

papers.title: Viral Infections and Dysregulation of Neurotrophin Signaling: Potential impact in the Central Nervous System.
papers.abstract: Viral infections can perturb neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system, with important consequences for neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, and long-term cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, and neurotrophin-4, mediate their actions primarily through tropomyosin receptor kinases (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC) and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR), activating intracellular pathways such as PI3K-AKT, MAPK-ERK, and PLC-γ. Growing evidence suggests that both neurotropic/neuroinvasive and non-classically neurotropic viruses can interfere with these pathways through multiple mechanisms, including those elicited by direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking required for sustained Trk signaling, and inflammation-driven alterations in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. This review summarizes current knowledge on how selected viruses affect neurotrophin availability and downstream signaling in experimental models and clinical settings. Specifically, the review focuses on: 1) viruses capable of establishing life-long latent or persistent infection such as i) herpesviruses (herpes simplex virus-1; Epstein Barr virus; human cytomegalovirus), and ii) human immunodeficiency virus; 2) other neurotropic viruses driving peculiar neuropathological profiles, such West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Zika virus, and Borna disease virus 1; 3) respiratory viruses, such as influenza A virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. For each virus group, we discuss convergent pathogenic mechanisms and receptor-level interference with neurotrophin signaling. We further highlight some gaps in current knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the underexplored role of viral co-infections and reactivations, and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation.

source_records.abstract: Viral infections can perturb neurotrophin signaling in the central nervous system, with important consequences for neuronal survival, synaptic plasticity, neurodevelopment, and long-term cognitive and neuropsychiatric outcomes. Neurotrophins, including nerve growth factor, brain-derived neurotrophic factor, neurotrophin-3, and neurotrophin-4, mediate their actions primarily through tropomyosin receptor kinases (TrkA, TrkB and TrkC) and the p75 neurotrophin receptor (p75NTR), activating intracellular pathways such as PI3K-AKT, MAPK-ERK, and PLC-γ. Growing evidence suggests that both neurotropic/neuroinvasive and non-classically neurotropic viruses can interfere with these pathways through multiple mechanisms, including those elicited by direct infection of neural and glial cells, interference with endosomal trafficking required for sustained Trk signaling, and inflammation-driven alterations in neurotrophin expression and receptor balance. This review summarizes current knowledge on how selected viruses affect neurotrophin availability and downstream signaling in experimental models and clinical settings. Specifically, the review focuses on: 1) viruses capable of establishing life-long latent or persistent infection such as i) herpesviruses (herpes simplex virus-1; Epstein Barr virus; human cytomegalovirus), and ii) human immunodeficiency virus; 2) other neurotropic viruses driving peculiar neuropathological profiles, such West Nile virus, Japanese encephalitis virus, Zika virus, and Borna disease virus 1; 3) respiratory viruses, such as influenza A virus, human respiratory syncytial virus, and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2. For each virus group, we discuss convergent pathogenic mechanisms and receptor-level interference with neurotrophin signaling. We further highlight some gaps in current knowledge, including limited longitudinal human data and the underexplored role of viral co-infections and reactivations, and the unclear causal directionality of neurotrophin dysregulation.

papers.abstract_zh: 病毒感染会扰乱中枢神经系统中的神经营养素信号传导,对神经元存活、突触可塑性、神经发育以及长期认知和神经精神结果产生重要影响。神经营养蛋白,包括神经生长因子、脑源性神经营养因子、神经营养蛋白-3 和神经营养蛋白-4,主要通过原肌球蛋白受体激酶(TrkA、TrkB 和 TrkC)和 p75 神经营养蛋白受体 (p75NTR) 介导其作用,激活细胞内通路,例如 PI3K-AKT、MAPK-ERK 和 PLC-γ。越来越多的证据表明,嗜神经/神经侵袭性病毒和非经典嗜神经病毒都可以通过多种机制干扰这些途径,包括直接感染神经和胶质细胞引起的机制、干扰持续 Trk 信号传导所需的内体运输以及炎症驱动的神经营养蛋白表达和受体平衡的改变。这篇综述总结了有关选定病毒如何影响实验模型和临床环境中神经营养蛋白可用性和下游信号传导的当前知识。具体而言,该审查重点关注:1)能够建立终生潜伏或持续感染的病毒,例如i)疱疹病毒(单纯疱疹病毒-1;Epstein Barr病毒;人类巨细胞病毒)和ii)人类免疫缺陷病毒;2)其他导致特殊神经病理学特征的嗜神经病毒,例如西尼罗河病毒、日本脑炎病毒、寨卡病毒和博尔纳病病毒1;3)呼吸道病毒,例如甲型流感病毒、人类呼吸道合胞病毒和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒2。对于每个病毒组,我们讨论了趋同的致病机制和受体水平对神经营养蛋白信号传导的干扰。我们进一步强调了当前知识中的一些差距,包括有限的纵向人类数据和病毒共同感染和再激活的作用尚未充分探索,以及神经营养蛋白失调的因果方向性尚不清楚。

papers.title: Nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV hospitalizations in children 8-23 months at risk of severe RSV
papers.abstract: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. Objective: We evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. Design: This retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. Setting: Enrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. Participants: Children eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. Exposures: Receipt of nirsevimab before or during the second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measures: RSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. Results: One hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). Conclusions: This analysis provides real-world estimates of substantial nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations for high-risk U.S. children in their second RSV season These data support recommendations for nirsevimab as a preventive strategy in this population.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是高危幼儿在第二个 RSV 季节住院的主要原因。我们评估了 尼塞韦单抗 在第二个 RSV 季节期间有资格接受 尼塞韦单抗 的幼儿对 RSV 相关住院治疗的有效性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项采用测试阴性设计的回顾性病例对照研究是在 2024-2025 和 2025-2026 RSV 季节进行的。招募对象为 24 名美国 26 家医院,其中包括在第二个 RSV 季节(按照 2023 年 8 月的建议)符合 尼塞韦单抗 条件的儿童。
elements_zh.methods: 我们使用多变量逻辑回归估计了 尼塞韦单抗 的有效性,并根据年龄、住院月份和年份、人口普查地区和性别进行了调整,比较了病例和对照患者中接受第二季 尼塞韦单抗 的几率。
elements_zh.main_results: 分析了106例病例患者和125例对照患者。总体而言,21例(19.8%)病例患者和53例(42.4%)对照患者接受了尼塞韦单抗。调整后的尼塞韦单抗对RSV相关住院的有效性为78.1%(95%置信区间,55.2%-89.3%);从接受尼塞韦单抗到症状出现的中位时间间隔为66.5天(四分位距为30-96天)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该分析提供了 尼塞韦单抗 对美国高危儿童在第二个 RSV 季节因 RSV 相关住院治疗的有效性的实际估计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些数据支持将 尼塞韦单抗 作为该人群预防策略的建议。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 大多数病例和对照患者因早产儿慢性肺病而符合 尼塞韦单抗 的条件(分别为 84.0% 和 69.6%)。所提供的证据并未报告研究设计的具体局限性。

papers.title_zh: 尼塞韦单抗 对有严重 RSV 风险的 8-23 个月儿童 RSV 住院治疗的有效性
papers.source_body_en: Importance: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a leading cause of hospitalization in high-risk young children during their second RSV season. Nirsevimab, a long-acting monoclonal antibody against RSV, is recommended for some children who are at increased risk for severe RSV and entering their second RSV season to prevent severe RSV disease. Because of limited eligibility criteria for second season nirsevimab, estimating its effectiveness is challenging. Objective: We evaluated nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations among young children eligible to receive nirsevimab during their second RSV season. Design: This retrospective case control study with a test-negative design was conducted during the 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 RSV seasons. Setting: Enrollment was in 26 hospitals across 24 U.S. Participants: Children eligible for nirsevimab during their second RSV season (as recommended in August 2023) were included. Nirsevimab-eligible children 8-23 months old hospitalized with respiratory symptoms were enrolled. Case-patients tested positive for RSV; control-patients tested negative for RSV. Exposures: Receipt of nirsevimab before or during the second RSV season and at least 7 days before symptom onset. Outcomes and measures: RSV-associated hospitalization. We estimated nirsevimab effectiveness using multivariable logistic regression adjusted for age, month and year of hospitalization, census region, and sex comparing the odds of second season nirsevimab receipt among case- and control-patients. Results: One hundred six case-patients and 125 control-patients were analyzed. Distributions of age, sex, race and ethnicity, and region were similar in case- and control-patients. Most case- and control-patients were eligible for nirsevimab because of chronic lung disease of prematurity (84.0% and 69.6%, respectively). Overall, 21 (19.8%) of case-patients and 53 (42.4%) of control-patients received nirsevimab. Adjusted nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations was 78.1% (95% CI, 55.2%-89.3%); the median interval from nirsevimab receipt to symptom onset was 66.5 days (IQR = 30-96 days). Effectiveness was estimated to be higher if nirsevimab was received 8-59 days before symptom onset (88.5%, 95% CI, 63.4%-96.4%). Conclusions: This analysis provides real-world estimates of substantial nirsevimab effectiveness against RSV-associated hospitalizations for high-risk U.S. children in their second RSV season These data support recommendations for nirsevimab as a preventive strategy in this population.
papers.abstract_zh: 重要性:尼塞韦单抗(呼吸道合胞病毒,RSV)是高风险婴幼儿在第二次RSV流行季期间住院的主要原因之一。尼塞韦单抗是一种长效单克隆抗体,针对RSV,推荐用于某些在第二次RSV流行季期间面临严重RSV风险的儿童,以预防严重RSV疾病。由于第二次流行季尼塞韦单抗的适用条件有限,评估其有效性具有挑战性。目的:我们评估了尼塞韦单抗在第二次RSV流行季期间,适用于接受尼塞韦单抗的高风险婴幼儿中,针对RSV相关住院的有效性。设计:这项回顾性病例对照研究采用测试阴性设计,于2024-2025和2025-2026年RSV流行季期间进行。背景:研究对象来自美国24个州的26家医院。参与者:在第二次RSV流行季期间符合接受尼塞韦单抗条件(根据2023年8月的推荐)的婴幼儿被纳入研究。年龄在8至23个月之间的尼塞韦单抗适用儿童,因呼吸道症状住院。病例患者RSV检测呈阳性,对照患者RSV检测呈阴性。暴露因素:在第二次RSV流行季之前或期间以及症状出现前至少7天接受尼塞韦单抗。结果和测量:RSV相关住院。我们使用多变量逻辑回归分析,调整年龄、住院月份和年份、人口普查地区和性别,比较病例和对照患者中第二次流行季尼塞韦单抗接受率的比值,以估计尼塞韦单抗的有效性。结果:分析了106例病例患者和125例对照患者。病例和对照患者在年龄、性别、种族和民族以及地区分布上相似。大多数病例和对照患者因早产慢性肺病而符合尼塞韦单抗的适用条件(分别为84.0%和69.6%)。总体而言,21例(19.8%)病例患者和53例(42.4%)对照患者接受了尼塞韦单抗。调整后的尼塞韦单抗对RSV相关住院的有效性为78.1%(95%置信区间,55.2%-89.3%);从接受尼塞韦单抗到症状出现的中位时间间隔为66.5天(四分位距为30-96天)。如果尼塞韦单抗在症状出现前8至59天接受,其有效性估计为88.5%(95%置信区间,63.4%-96.4%)。结论:本分析提供了真实世界中尼塞韦单抗对美国高风险儿童在第二次RSV流行季期间RSV相关住院的显著有效性估计。这些数据支持将尼塞韦单抗作为该人群预防策略的推荐。

papers.title: Influenza A/B, RSV and SARS-CoV-2 Co-Detection Among Adults with Acute Respiratory Illness in Zimbabwe, 2022–2023: A Sub-Study of a COVID-19 Vaccine Effectiveness Study
papers.abstract: Background: /Objectives: Influenza, respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2) cause overlapping respiratory illness, but Zimbabwean adult multipathogen data remain limited. We described influenza and RSV detection and co-detection with SARS-CoV-2 among adults enrolled in the ZIMCOVVAR study. Methods: This retrospective sub-study included nasopharyngeal specimens from adults with acute respiratory illness recruited in six Zimbabwean provinces during 2022-2023. Following exclusion of duplicate and unlinked records, 1,429 participants were analyzed. Influenza A, influenza B, and RSV were tested by multiplex real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR); recorded target cycle thresholds (Ct) ≤30 were provisionally classified as signals. Valid target-specific denominators remained unresolved. Proportions, confidence intervals, monthly patterns, and associations with SARS-CoV-2 status were examined. Results: The analytic cohort comprised 281 SARS-CoV-2-positive and 1,148 negative participants; median age was 35 years and 68.2% were female. Ct-defined influenza A, RSV, and influenza B signals occurred in 191/1,429 (13.4%), 53/1,429 (3.7%), and 2/1,429 (0.1%), respectively. Influenza A was recorded in 68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2-positive versus 123/1,148 (10.7%) negative participants. RSV was recorded in 3/281 (1.1%) versus 50/1,148 (4.4%), respectively. These are provisional signals per linked record, not valid-result positivity estimates; testing-group exclusion reversed the adjusted association. Conclusions: The selected adult cohort showed recorded influenza and RSV detections alongside SARS-CoV-2, supporting continued investigation of multiple respiratory pathogens in symptomatic adults. The findings require cautious interpretation because of nonrepresentative sampling and unresolved testing-group effects; quality-assured, multi-season surveillance is needed to inform local prevention planning.

analysis.summary_en: This study analyzed co-detection of influenza A, influenza B, and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) with SARS-CoV-2 among adults with acute respiratory illness in Zimbabwe during 2022–2023. The research aimed to address limited data on multipathogen respiratory illnesses in the region. Using multiplex real-time reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction (PCR), the study found that RSV was detected in 3.7% of specimens, with a higher proportion in SARS-CoV-2-positive participants. The results suggest potential co-circulation of these viruses, but the findings are provisional due to unresolved testing-group effects and nonrepresentative sampling. The study highlights the need for quality-assured, multi-season surveillance to better understand the epidemiology of respiratory pathogens and inform local prevention strategies.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 我们描述了参加 ZIMCOVVAR 研究的成年人中流感和 RSV 的检测以及与 SARS-CoV-2 的共同检测。这项回顾性子研究包括 2022 年至 2023 年在津巴布韦六个省份招募的患有急性呼吸道疾病的成年人的鼻咽标本。
elements_zh.methods: 通过多重实时逆转录聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测甲型流感、乙型流感和 RSV;记录的目标周期阈值(Ct)≤30 暂时归类为信号。检查了比例、置信区间、每月模式以及与 SARS-CoV-2 状态的关联。
elements_zh.main_results: 分析 队列研究 包括 281 名 SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者和 1,148 名阴性参与者;中位年龄为 35 岁,其中 68.2% 为女性。Ct 定义的甲型流感、RSV 和乙型流感信号分别出现在 191/1,429 (13.4%)、53/1,429 (3.7%) 和 2/1,429 (0.1%) 中。68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者记录了甲型流感,而 123/1,148 (10.7%) 阴性参与者记录了甲型流感。RSV 记录分别为 3/281 (1.1%) 和 50/1,148 (4.4%)。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 选定的成人 队列研究 显示记录的流感和 RSV 检测以及 SARS-CoV-2,支持对有症状成人的多种呼吸道病原体的持续研究。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 由于抽样不具代表性且测试组效应尚未解决,研究结果需要谨慎解释;需要有质量保证的多季节 监测 来为当地预防规划提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 这些是每个链接记录的临时信号,不是有效结果的积极性估计;测试组排除逆转了调整后的关联。

papers.abstract_zh: 背景:/目标:流感、呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 和严重急性呼吸综合征冠状病毒 2 (SARS-CoV-2) 会引起重叠的呼吸道疾病,但津巴布韦成人多病原体数据仍然有限。我们描述了参加 ZIMCOVVAR 研究的成年人中流感和 RSV 的检测以及与 SARS-CoV-2 的共同检测。方法:这项回顾性子研究包括 2022 年至 2023 年在津巴布韦六个省份招募的患有急性呼吸道疾病的成年人的鼻咽标本。排除重复和未关联的记录后,对 1,429 名参与者进行了分析。通过多重实时逆转录聚合酶链反应 (PCR) 检测甲型流感、乙型流感和 RSV;记录的目标周期阈值(Ct)≤30 暂时归类为信号。有效的特定目标分母仍未解决。检查了比例、置信区间、每月模式以及与 SARS-CoV-2 状态的关联。结果:分析 队列研究 包括 281 名 SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者和 1,148 名阴性参与者;中位年龄为 35 岁,其中 68.2% 为女性。Ct 定义的甲型流感、RSV 和乙型流感信号分别出现在 191/1,429 (13.4%)、53/1,429 (3.7%) 和 2/1,429 (0.1%) 中。68/281 (24.2%) SARS-CoV-2 阳性参与者记录了甲型流感,而 123/1,148 (10.7%) 阴性参与者记录了甲型流感。RSV 记录分别为 3/281 (1.1%) 和 50/1,148 (4.4%)。这些是每个链接记录的临时信号,不是有效结果的积极性估计;测试组排除逆转了调整后的关联。结论:选定的成人 队列研究 显示记录的流感和 RSV 检测以及 SARS-CoV-2,支持对有症状成人中的多种呼吸道病原体的继续研究。由于抽样不具代表性且测试组效应尚未解决,研究结果需要谨慎解释;需要有质量保证的多季节 监测 来为当地预防规划提供信息。

papers.title: Comparison of Dissemination of Aerosol and Splatter during Ultrasonic Scaling using Different Masks: A Pilot Study with Relevance to Respiratory Infection Transmission
papers.abstract: Abstract Background: Dentists are routinely exposed to a high amount of micro-organism load due to primarily being responsible for the treatment of the structures if the mouth – which is a well-known source of huge bacterial loads. Also, as COVID-19 recently affected the entire world, masks thus were considered to act as a comprehensive strategy of measures to suppress transmission. However, the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control extends beyond COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza viruses such as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, commonly referred to as swine flu, influenza A(H3N2), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and other respiratory viruses continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles. Aim: To compare the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. Method: In this study we evaluated the dissemination of four masks that is N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask by calculating the surface are of filter paper with the help of a previously marked scale which was divided into one-centimeter squares. Results: Best protection was seen to be offered by the combined use of the double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by N-95 mask alone and then the surgical mask.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for effective infection control measures in dental settings, where dentists are routinely exposed to high microbial loads. The background highlights the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control beyond the context of COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This pilot study evaluated the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. The study was conducted in a dental setting, and the participants were dentists involved in the procedure.
analysis.methods: The study compared the effectiveness of four masks: N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask. The surface area of filter paper was calculated using a previously marked scale divided into one-centimeter squares to assess the dissemination of aerosol and splatter.
analysis.main_results: The results indicated that the best protection was provided by the combined use of double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by the N-95 mask alone, and then the surgical mask.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that double masking offers superior protection against aerosol dissemination during dental procedures. This is a novel approach to infection control in settings where respiratory pathogens are a concern.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have specific implications for improving infection control strategies in dental environments, particularly in reducing the transmission of respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a pilot study, which limits the generalizability of the results. The evidence is based on a single method of assessing aerosol dissemination, which may not fully capture the complexity of pathogen transmission in real-world scenarios.

analysis.summary_en: This pilot study aimed to evaluate the effectiveness of different masks in preventing aerosol and splatter dissemination during ultrasonic scaling in dental settings. The study highlighted the importance of infection control measures, particularly in environments where respiratory pathogens like RSV are prevalent. The results showed that combining an N-95 mask without a filter with a cloth mask provided the best protection. The authors interpreted these findings as a novel approach to reducing pathogen transmission in dental procedures. The study's implications for public health include the potential for improved infection control strategies in dental practices. However, the study's limitations include its small scale and reliance on a single method of assessment, which may affect the strength of the evidence.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在解决牙科环境中有效感染控制措施的需求,因为牙医经常暴露在高微生物负荷下。背景强调了在 COVID-19 背景下气溶胶和呼吸道感染控制的相关性,因为 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 等呼吸道病原体继续循环,并可能通过呼吸道颗粒传播。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该试点研究评估了使用不同面罩进行超声洁牙期间气溶胶和飞溅的传播情况。该研究是在牙科环境中进行的,参与者是参与该手术的牙医。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究比较了四种口罩的有效性:带呼吸器的 N-95、不带呼吸器的 N-95、布口罩和不带呼吸器的 N-95 的组合以及普通外科口罩。使用先前标记的一厘米见方的刻度来计算滤纸的表面积,以评估气溶胶和飞溅的传播。
elements_zh.main_results: 结果表明,双重口罩的组合使用提供了最好的保护——无过滤器的N-95加布口罩,其次是单独的N-95口罩,然后是外科口罩。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证据,表明双重遮蔽在牙科手术过程中提供了针对气溶胶传播的卓越保护。这是一种在呼吸道病原体存在问题的环境中控制感染的新方法。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现对于改善牙科环境中的感染控制策略具有具体意义,特别是在减少 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 等呼吸道病原体的 传播 方面。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是一项试点研究,限制了结果的普遍性。该证据基于评估气溶胶传播的单一方法,该方法可能无法完全捕捉现实场景中病原体 传播 的复杂性。

analysis_en.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the need for effective infection control measures in dental settings, where dentists are routinely exposed to high microbial loads. The background highlights the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control beyond the context of COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles.
analysis_en.study_design_and_population: This pilot study evaluated the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. The study was conducted in a dental setting, and the participants were dentists involved in the procedure.
analysis_en.methods: The study compared the effectiveness of four masks: N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask. The surface area of filter paper was calculated using a previously marked scale divided into one-centimeter squares to assess the dissemination of aerosol and splatter.
analysis_en.main_results: The results indicated that the best protection was provided by the combined use of double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by the N-95 mask alone, and then the surgical mask.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as evidence that double masking offers superior protection against aerosol dissemination during dental procedures. This is a novel approach to infection control in settings where respiratory pathogens are a concern.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings have specific implications for improving infection control strategies in dental environments, particularly in reducing the transmission of respiratory pathogens such as respiratory syncytial virus (RSV).
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is a pilot study, which limits the generalizability of the results. The evidence is based on a single method of assessing aerosol dissemination, which may not fully capture the complexity of pathogen transmission in real-world scenarios.

papers.title_zh: 使用不同口罩进行超声洁牙期间气溶胶和飞溅传播的比较:与呼吸道感染相关的初步研究 传播
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background: Dentists are routinely exposed to a high amount of micro-organism load due to primarily being responsible for the treatment of the structures if the mouth – which is a well-known source of huge bacterial loads. Also, as COVID-19 recently affected the entire world, masks thus were considered to act as a comprehensive strategy of measures to suppress transmission. However, the relevance of aerosol and respiratory infection control extends beyond COVID-19, as respiratory pathogens including seasonal influenza viruses such as influenza A(H1N1)pdm09, commonly referred to as swine flu, influenza A(H3N2), respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), and other respiratory viruses continue to circulate and may be transmitted through respiratory particles. Aim: To compare the dissemination of aerosol and splatter during ultrasonic scaling using different masks. Method: In this study we evaluated the dissemination of four masks that is N-95 with respirator, N-95 without respirator, a combination of cloth mask and N-95 without respirator, and normal surgical mask by calculating the surface are of filter paper with the help of a previously marked scale which was divided into one-centimeter squares. Results: Best protection was seen to be offered by the combined use of the double masking – N-95 without filter plus cloth mask, followed by N-95 mask alone and then the surgical mask.

papers.title: mRNA-Lipid Nanoparticle Vaccines for Infectious Diseases: Mechanisms of Action and Translational Progress
papers.abstract: Six years after the first emergency use authorizations, mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines have gone from a platform without a licensed product to one that supplies a large share of the world's COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine doses and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. Their performance depends on mechanisms that are being resolved with unusual speed at the level of individual cell types, receptors and molecular interactions, and several textbook assumptions have had to be revised in the process. This review follows the vaccine from the formulation vial to the germinal centre. We first describe how the RNA is engineered for efficient translation and for partial escape from cytosolic and endosomal RNA sensors, and why N1-methylpseudouridine is neither immunologically silent nor translationally neutral. We then examine how the ionizable lipid, the helper phospholipid, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid determine particle behaviour, cell uptake and endosomal release, and how the lipid and RNA components act as separable adjuvant signals. Evidence from mouse models and from human lymph node sampling is compared, with attention to the substantial species differences in innate cytokine control that limit extrapolation from mice to people. The clinical section summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for COVID-19, RSV and influenza vaccines, and the preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against cytomegalovirus, mpox, HIV, malaria, Nipah virus and Clostridioides difficile. Safety data are discussed in absolute terms rather than as signals alone. We close with the questions that currently block rational improvement: the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the design of antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), including their mechanisms of action, translational progress, and clinical applications. The central question is how these vaccines function and their potential for broader use in preventing RSV infections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on evidence from mouse models and human lymph node sampling. It discusses the performance of mRNA-LNP vaccines, emphasizing the need to account for species differences in innate cytokine control when extrapolating findings from mice to humans. The review also outlines the clinical section that summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for RSV vaccines and includes preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against other pathogens.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mRNA-LNP vaccines have transitioned from a platform without a licensed product to one that is widely used for RSV and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. It highlights the importance of understanding the molecular mechanisms of vaccine performance, particularly the role of lipid and RNA components in particle behavior, cell uptake, and endosomal release.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies several controversies and evidence gaps, including the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the challenges in designing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on resolving the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, improving the separation of immunogenicity from reactogenicity, quantifying endosomal escape mechanisms, and developing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen. These efforts are critical for the rational improvement of mRNA-LNP vaccines.

analysis.summary_en: This review explores the development and mechanisms of mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), highlighting their transition from an unlicensed platform to a major contributor in RSV and influenza vaccine production. The review emphasizes the importance of understanding the molecular interactions between lipid and RNA components, as well as the challenges in translating findings from mouse models to humans due to differences in innate cytokine control. It also outlines key controversies, such as the molecular identity of the lipid sensor and the difficulty of distinguishing immunogenicity from reactogenicity. The review concludes with research and practice implications, suggesting that future efforts should focus on resolving these gaps to improve vaccine design and efficacy for RSV and other pathogens.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述重点关注 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 (mRNA-LNP) 疫苗,包括其作用机制、转化进展和临床应用。核心问题是这些 疫苗 如何发挥作用以及它们在预防 RSV 感染方面更广泛应用的潜力。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查基于小鼠模型和人类淋巴结采样的证据。它讨论了 mRNA-LNP 疫苗 的性能,强调在将小鼠的研究结果外推到人类时,需要考虑先天细胞因子控制的物种差异。该综述还概述了临床部分,总结了 RSV 疫苗 的功效和免疫原性数据,并包括候选药物针对其他病原体的临床前和早期临床状态。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,mRNA-LNP 疫苗 已从一个没有许可产品的平台转变为广泛用于 RSV 的平台,并已完成季节性流感的 3 期试验。它强调了了解 疫苗 性能的分子机制的重要性,特别是脂质和 RNA 成分在颗粒行为、细胞摄取和内体释放中的作用。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述指出了一些争议和证据差距,包括脂质传感器的分子身份、区分免疫原性和反应原性的困难、缺乏内体逃逸的定量描述,以及为不耐受单一固定免疫原的病原体设计抗原的挑战。
