analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), including their mechanisms of action, translational progress, and clinical applications. The central question is how these vaccines function and their potential for broader use in preventing RSV infections.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is based on evidence from mouse models and human lymph node sampling. It discusses the performance of mRNA-LNP vaccines, emphasizing the need to account for species differences in innate cytokine control when extrapolating findings from mice to humans. The review also outlines the clinical section that summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for RSV vaccines and includes preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against other pathogens.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that mRNA-LNP vaccines have transitioned from a platform without a licensed product to one that is widely used for RSV and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. It highlights the importance of understanding the molecular mechanisms of vaccine performance, particularly the role of lipid and RNA components in particle behavior, cell uptake, and endosomal release.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies several controversies and evidence gaps, including the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the challenges in designing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: The review suggests that future research should focus on resolving the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, improving the separation of immunogenicity from reactogenicity, quantifying endosomal escape mechanisms, and developing antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen. papers.title_zh: 用于传染病的 mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 疫苗:作用机制和转化进展
papers.source_body_en: Six years after the first emergency use authorizations, mRNA-lipid nanoparticle (mRNA-LNP) vaccines have gone from a platform without a licensed product to one that supplies a large share of the world's COVID-19 and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) vaccine doses and has completed phase 3 trials for seasonal influenza. Their performance depends on mechanisms that are being resolved with unusual speed at the level of individual cell types, receptors and molecular interactions, and several textbook assumptions have had to be revised in the process. This review follows the vaccine from the formulation vial to the germinal centre. We first describe how the RNA is engineered for efficient translation and for partial escape from cytosolic and endosomal RNA sensors, and why N1-methylpseudouridine is neither immunologically silent nor translationally neutral. We then examine how the ionizable lipid, the helper phospholipid, cholesterol and the PEG-lipid determine particle behaviour, cell uptake and endosomal release, and how the lipid and RNA components act as separable adjuvant signals. Evidence from mouse models and from human lymph node sampling is compared, with attention to the substantial species differences in innate cytokine control that limit extrapolation from mice to people. The clinical section summarizes efficacy and immunogenicity data for COVID-19, RSV and influenza vaccines, and the preclinical and early clinical status of candidates against cytomegalovirus, mpox, HIV, malaria, Nipah virus and Clostridioides difficile. Safety data are discussed in absolute terms rather than as signals alone. We close with the questions that currently block rational improvement: the molecular identity of the lipid sensor, the difficulty of separating immunogenicity from reactogenicity, the absence of a quantitative description of endosomal escape, and the design of antigens for pathogens that do not tolerate a single fixed immunogen.
papers.abstract_zh: 在首次获得紧急使用授权六年后,mRNA-脂质纳米颗粒 (mRNA-LNP) 疫苗 已从一个没有许可产品的平台转变为供应全球大部分 COVID-19 和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 疫苗 剂量的平台,并已完成季节性流感的 3 期试验。它们的性能取决于在个体细胞类型、受体和分子相互作用水平上以异常速度解决的机制,并且在此过程中必须修改一些教科书的假设。本次审查遵循 疫苗 从配方瓶到生发中心的整个过程。我们首先描述了如何设计 RNA 以实现有效翻译并部分逃离胞质和内体 RNA 传感器,以及为什么 N1-甲基假尿苷既不是免疫沉默也不是翻译中性。然后,我们研究可电离脂质、辅助磷脂、胆固醇和 PEG-脂质如何决定颗粒行为、细胞摄取和内体释放,以及脂质和 RNA 成分如何充当可分离的佐剂信号。比较了来自小鼠模型和人类淋巴结采样的证据,并注意先天细胞因子控制方面的巨大物种差异,这限制了从小鼠到人类的外推。临床部分总结了 COVID-19、RSV 和流感 疫苗 的功效和免疫原性数据,以及针对巨细胞病毒、mpox、HIV、疟疾、尼帕病毒和艰难梭菌的候选药物的临床前和早期临床状态。安全数据以绝对术语而不是单独作为信号来讨论。我们以目前阻碍合理改进的问题作为结束语:脂质传感器的分子特性、将免疫原性与反应原性分开的困难、缺乏内体逃逸的定量描述以及不耐受单一固定免疫原的病原体的抗原设计。

papers.title: Lagged environmental effects on multi-pathogen respiratory positivity: a distributed-lag nonlinear analysis of seven Sichuan sentinel hospitals, China
papers.abstract: Abstract Acute respiratory infections (ARI) impose a large global burden and show marked seasonality that implicates environmental drivers, yet the lagged effects of these exposures on pathogen-specific positivity remain poorly characterised. Using case-level data from seven sentinel hospitals in Sichuan, China (2024–2026) aggregated to a weekly panel of 23 014 ARI cases, we applied quasi-Poisson distributed-lag non-linear models (cross-basis, 6-week lag; trend spline; city effects; log offset) to estimate cumulative relative risks (90th versus 10th percentile) for temperature, relative humidity and six air pollutants, with within-pathogen false-discovery-rate control. At least one pathogen was detected in 51.9% of cases and co-detection in 18.2%; Haemophilus influenzae and influenza predominated. Relative humidity gave the most stable single-exposure association with respiratory syncytial virus positivity ( RR 2.01, 95% CI 1.06–3.82); it failed FDR control (adjusted P = 0.130 ) and was nullified by temperature co-adjustment ( RR 1.05). influenzae rose with temperature and ozone and fell with PM2.5; SARS-CoV-2 tracked carbon monoxide. Twelve of 40 estimates survived FDR control. The humidity–RSV signal is robust to model specification yet fragile under co-varying exposures — the cautionary lesson — and the reusable output is a transparent screening framework that exposes such fragility, serving exposure science and environmental epidemiology.

papers.title: Current Approaches to Geriatric Immunizat?on: A Narrative Mini-Review
papers.abstract: As the global population ages, the implementation of a "life-course immunization" approach has become a critical pillar for maintaining functional capacity and ensuring healthy aging. Current 2025-2026 guidelines emphasize a strategic transition to trivalent influenza vaccines and the routine administration of novel Respiratory Syncytial Virus vaccines for high-risk geriatric cohorts. Furthermore, clinical protocols prioritize high-dose or adjuvanted formulations to overcome immunosenescence and provide robust protection against invasive pneumococcal disease, herpes zoster, and COVID-19 subvariants. Despite these advancements, significant disparities in vaccine access and public awareness persist, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Strengthening national immunization schedules through the integration of these next-generation vaccines is essential to alleviate the burden on healthcare systems and reduce preventable mortality. Ultimately, the shift toward personalized immunization strategies aims to ensure that every older adult achieves optimal seroprotection and a higher quality of life.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 目前的指南建议对高危老年人群进行向三价流感 疫苗 的战略过渡,并常规施用新型 RSV 疫苗。临床方案优先考虑高剂量或佐剂制剂,以增强对 RSV 相关疾病(如 毛细支气管炎 和侵袭性肺炎球菌疾病)的保护。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该审查强调了 疫苗 的获取和公众意识方面的显着差异,特别是在低收入和中等收入国家。这些差异代表了一个关键的证据差距,因为它们影响 RSV 免疫策略的公平实施。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 通过整合下一代 RSV 疫苗 来加强国家免疫计划对于减少可预防的 死亡率 和减轻医疗保健系统的负担至关重要。向个性化免疫策略的转变旨在确保老年人获得最佳的血清保护和生活质量。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review focuses on respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) and its impact on geriatric immunization, particularly in the context of vaccine development and administration strategies for older adults. The central question is how to optimize immunization approaches for RSV to improve health outcomes in aging populations.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative mini-review, not a systematic or meta-analytic study. It does not report specific databases, search dates, or eligibility criteria. The evidence is derived from current guidelines and clinical protocols, with an emphasis on vaccine formulations and their application in geriatric cohorts.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Current guidelines recommend a strategic transition to trivalent influenza vaccines and the routine administration of novel RSV vaccines for high-risk geriatric populations. Clinical protocols prioritize high-dose or adjuvanted formulations to enhance protection against RSV-related diseases such as bronchiolitis and invasive pneumococcal disease.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review highlights significant disparities in vaccine access and public awareness, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. These disparities represent a critical evidence gap, as they affect the equitable implementation of RSV immunization strategies.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Strengthening national immunization schedules through the integration of next-generation RSV vaccines is essential to reduce preventable mortality and alleviate healthcare system burdens. The shift toward personalized immunization strategies aims to ensure optimal seroprotection and quality of life for older adults.

papers.title_zh: 当前的老年免疫方法:叙述性迷你评论
papers.source_body_en: As the global population ages, the implementation of a "life-course immunization" approach has become a critical pillar for maintaining functional capacity and ensuring healthy aging. Current 2025-2026 guidelines emphasize a strategic transition to trivalent influenza vaccines and the routine administration of novel Respiratory Syncytial Virus vaccines for high-risk geriatric cohorts. Furthermore, clinical protocols prioritize high-dose or adjuvanted formulations to overcome immunosenescence and provide robust protection against invasive pneumococcal disease, herpes zoster, and COVID-19 subvariants. Despite these advancements, significant disparities in vaccine access and public awareness persist, particularly in low- and middle-income countries. Strengthening national immunization schedules through the integration of these next-generation vaccines is essential to alleviate the burden on healthcare systems and reduce preventable mortality. Ultimately, the shift toward personalized immunization strategies aims to ensure that every older adult achieves optimal seroprotection and a higher quality of life.

papers.title: Adaptive forecasting and alert evaluation for pediatric RSV and influenza hospitalization burden using public U.S. surveillance data: a time-series study
papers.abstract: Pediatric influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalization surges strain hospitals and public health agencies. Post-pandemic changes in seasonality and surveillance practice have weakened fixed seasonal baselines. We evaluated whether public surveillance signals can support transparent warning evaluation for pediatric influenza and RSV hospitalization burden. We conducted a retrospective ecological time-series study using aggregated U.S. RESP-NET hospitalization surveillance and related public signal streams from October 2018 through March 2026. Outcomes were weekly pediatric hospitalization rates for influenza and RSV among children aged 0–4 and 5–17 years. We compared a prior-year same-week seasonal naïve baseline with expanding-window ridge models using seasonal/autoregressive terms and feasible public signals, including emergency department (ED) percent-visit indicators. Forecasts were evaluated by rolling-origin validation, with a finalized-data sensitivity excluding the most recent 4 weeks. We summarized mean absolute error (MAE), alert utility, onset lead time, and expected loss under training-quantile alert thresholds. For RSV among children aged 0–4 years, an ED-feasible ridge model improved matched-week forecasts versus the seasonal naïve baseline at horizon 1 under the finalized-data sensitivity (paired MAE improvement 3.49; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.59 to 5.69; paired n = 104). Influenza gains were smaller and uncertain (ages 0–4 years, horizon 1: paired MAE improvement 0.60; 95% CI -0.24 to 1.24; paired n = 51). Direct matched comparisons of autoregressive/seasonal ridge models with versus without ED terms did not show a stable independent ED point-error gain. At a fixed 90th training-quantile alert threshold and miss: false-alarm cost ratio of 2.0, expected-loss ratios relative to the seasonal baseline were 0.280 for RSV ages 0–4 years and 0.545 for influenza ages 0–4 years. These findings support pathogen-specific, locally calibrated strategies for pediatric respiratory-virus hospitalization warning. Adaptive ridge models improved RSV warning metrics relative to a fixed prior-year baseline, whereas ED terms did not improve matched point-error accuracy beyond AR+season terms. ED signals are therefore a feasible syndromic layer for alert-policy evaluation, not evidence of an independent forecasting gain.

papers.title_zh: 使用美国 监测 公开数据对儿科 RSV 和流感住院负担进行自适应预测和警报评估:一项时间序列研究
papers.source_body_en: Pediatric influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) hospitalization surges strain hospitals and public health agencies. Post-pandemic changes in seasonality and surveillance practice have weakened fixed seasonal baselines. We evaluated whether public surveillance signals can support transparent warning evaluation for pediatric influenza and RSV hospitalization burden. We conducted a retrospective ecological time-series study using aggregated U.S. RESP-NET hospitalization surveillance and related public signal streams from October 2018 through March 2026. Outcomes were weekly pediatric hospitalization rates for influenza and RSV among children aged 0–4 and 5–17 years. We compared a prior-year same-week seasonal naïve baseline with expanding-window ridge models using seasonal/autoregressive terms and feasible public signals, including emergency department (ED) percent-visit indicators. Forecasts were evaluated by rolling-origin validation, with a finalized-data sensitivity excluding the most recent 4 weeks. We summarized mean absolute error (MAE), alert utility, onset lead time, and expected loss under training-quantile alert thresholds. For RSV among children aged 0–4 years, an ED-feasible ridge model improved matched-week forecasts versus the seasonal naïve baseline at horizon 1 under the finalized-data sensitivity (paired MAE improvement 3.49; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.59 to 5.69; paired n = 104). Influenza gains were smaller and uncertain (ages 0–4 years, horizon 1: paired MAE improvement 0.60; 95% CI -0.24 to 1.24; paired n = 51). Direct matched comparisons of autoregressive/seasonal ridge models with versus without ED terms did not show a stable independent ED point-error gain. At a fixed 90th training-quantile alert threshold and miss: false-alarm cost ratio of 2.0, expected-loss ratios relative to the seasonal baseline were 0.280 for RSV ages 0–4 years and 0.545 for influenza ages 0–4 years. These findings support pathogen-specific, locally calibrated strategies for pediatric respiratory-virus hospitalization warning. Adaptive ridge models improved RSV warning metrics relative to a fixed prior-year baseline, whereas ED terms did not improve matched point-error accuracy beyond AR+season terms. ED signals are therefore a feasible syndromic layer for alert-policy evaluation, not evidence of an independent forecasting gain.

papers.title: Does the Effectiveness of the Nirsevimab Immunization Programs Decline from One RSV Season to the Next? Real-World Evidence from Northeastern Italy
papers.abstract: Background: Nirsevimab has demonstrated high effectiveness in preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease in infants. However, real-world evidence from subsequent seasonal immunization campaigns remains limited. We evaluated the effectiveness of universal infant immunization during a second RSV season and assessed protection during the following season after immunization in the previous year. Methods: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study in the Province of Udine, Italy, using linked anonymized regional healthcare databases. All infants born between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 were included in the analysis of the 2025–2026 RSV season. RSV-related hospitalizations were identified from hospital discharge diagnoses. Effectiveness was estimated using multivariable logistic regression and a Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying immunization status. We also assessed RSV-related hospitalizations during the subsequent season among infants who had received nirsevimab during the previous campaign. Seasonal hospitalization risks for RSV and other respiratory viral infections were compared across pre- and post-implementation seasons. Results: Of 2620 infants born during the second campaign, 2293 (87.5%) received nirsevimab. Twenty infants were hospitalized for RSV-related conditions, including 13/2293 (5.67 per 1000) immunized and 7/327 (21.41 per 1000) non-immunized infants (p = 0.008). Adjusted analyses showed significantly lower odds and hazard of RSV-related hospitalization among immunized infants (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09–0.57; HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11–0.69), corresponding to estimated effectiveness of 78% and 73%, respectively. During the following RSV season, six infants from the previous birth cohort were hospitalized with RSV-related conditions, all of whom had received nirsevimab during the preceding campaign (cohort coverage: 78.5%). Hospitalization rates for non-RSV respiratory viruses were lower in the two post-implementation seasons than in the preceding seasons, although this ecological analysis was not designed to establish causality. Conclusions: Universal infant immunization with nirsevimab remained highly effective in preventing RSV-related hospitalization during the second seasonal campaign, achieving high population coverage. No evidence of residual protection was observed during the subsequent RSV season after immunization in the previous year. Continued real-world surveillance is warranted to monitor nirsevimab effectiveness and the broader epidemiology of respiratory viral infections following widespread implementation.

source_records.abstract: Background: Nirsevimab has demonstrated high effectiveness in preventing severe respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) disease in infants. However, real-world evidence from subsequent seasonal immunization campaigns remains limited. We evaluated the effectiveness of universal infant immunization during a second RSV season and assessed protection during the following season after immunization in the previous year. Methods: We conducted a population-based retrospective cohort study in the Province of Udine, Italy, using linked anonymized regional healthcare databases. All infants born between 1 April 2025 and 31 March 2026 were included in the analysis of the 2025–2026 RSV season. RSV-related hospitalizations were identified from hospital discharge diagnoses. Effectiveness was estimated using multivariable logistic regression and a Cox proportional hazards model with time-varying immunization status. We also assessed RSV-related hospitalizations during the subsequent season among infants who had received nirsevimab during the previous campaign. Seasonal hospitalization risks for RSV and other respiratory viral infections were compared across pre- and post-implementation seasons. Results: Of 2620 infants born during the second campaign, 2293 (87.5%) received nirsevimab. Twenty infants were hospitalized for RSV-related conditions, including 13/2293 (5.67 per 1000) immunized and 7/327 (21.41 per 1000) non-immunized infants (p = 0.008). Adjusted analyses showed significantly lower odds and hazard of RSV-related hospitalization among immunized infants (OR 0.22, 95% CI 0.09–0.57; HR 0.27, 95% CI 0.11–0.69), corresponding to estimated effectiveness of 78% and 73%, respectively. During the following RSV season, six infants from the previous birth cohort were hospitalized with RSV-related conditions, all of whom had received nirsevimab during the preceding campaign (cohort coverage: 78.5%). Hospitalization rates for non-RSV respiratory viruses were lower in the two post-implementation seasons than in the preceding seasons, although this ecological analysis was not designed to establish causality. Conclusions: Universal infant immunization with nirsevimab remained highly effective in preventing RSV-related hospitalization during the second seasonal campaign, achieving high population coverage. No evidence of residual protection was observed during the subsequent RSV season after immunization in the previous year. Continued real-world surveillance is warranted to monitor nirsevimab effectiveness and the broader epidemiology of respiratory viral infections following widespread implementation.

papers.title: Impact of expanding nirsevimab immunoprophylaxis, extended window and catch-up, on RSV hospitalizations in infants: a three-season, multicentre, population-based study in Emilia-Romagna, Italy
papers.abstract: Background Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) is a major cause of hospitalization in infancy, particularly during the first months of life. Nirsevimab has substantially reduced RSV-related hospitalizations in early real-world studies, but the incremental population-level benefit of expanding an established seasonal programme to broader birth cohorts remains uncertain. In Emilia-Romagna, Italy, nirsevimab was introduced for the 2024–25 RSV season as seasonal at-birth immunoprophylaxis and expanded in 2025–26 to include at-birth immunoprophylaxis for infants born from August 2025 through March 2026 and catch-up immunization for infants born from April through July 2025. We assessed whether this expanded strategy provided an additional reduction in RSV-compatible hospitalizations. Methods We conducted a multicentre, population-based observational before–after study using hospital discharge records from eleven centres, covering approximately 69% of hospitalizations among infants aged <12 months. RSV-compatible hospitalizations were compared across three seasons: Pre-Nirsevimab (2023–24), Seasonal (2024–25), and Extended seasonal + catch-up (2025–26). Incidence rate ratios (IRRs) were estimated by negative binomial regression adjusted for sex and age. Net avoided hospitalizations were also calculated. Results Age-standardized RSV-compatible hospitalization rates declined from 21.9 per 100, 000 person-days in 2023–24 to 10.1 in 2024–25 and 7.8 in 2025–26. Compared with the Seasonal strategy, the Extended seasonal + catch-up strategy was associated with a further 22% reduction in hospitalization risk (IRR 0.78; 95% CI 0.69–0.88; p<0.001) and a 64% reduction versus Pre-Nirsevimab (IRR 0.36; 95% CI 0.31–0.42). An estimated 103.3 additional hospitalizations were avoided versus 2024–25 and 677.8 versus Pre-Nirsevimab, corresponding to approximately 52 and 339 avoided hospitalizations per 10, 000 infants, respectively. Findings were consistent in infants aged 0–180 days. Conclusions Expanding nirsevimab immunoprophylaxis was associated with a further significant reduction in RSV-compatible hospitalizations beyond that achieved with seasonal-only administration. Given the observational design, causal inference should remain cautious.

The findings are relevant for informing future vaccination strategies and surveillance efforts for RSV in infants.

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是婴儿期住院的主要原因,尤其是在生命的最初几个月。在早期的现实世界研究中,尼塞韦单抗 已大大减少了与 RSV 相关的住院治疗,但将已建立的季节性计划扩大到更广泛的出生 队列研究 所带来的增量人口水平效益仍不确定。

papers.title: Pathogen spectrum and its association with hospital length of stay in 112 pathogen-tested children with bronchiolitis: a retrospective study from a cohort of 132 hospitalized cases in Hebei Children's Hospital
papers.abstract: Objective To investigate the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological characteristics of hospitalized children with bronchiolitis admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital, and to analyze the relationship between different pathogens or mixed infections and clinical recovery speed, providing a clinical reference for the prevention and treatment of infant bronchiolitis in northern China. Methods Based on the electronic medical record system, the clinical data of 132 children hospitalized with bronchiolitis at Hebei Children's Hospital from September 2022 to February 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Sputum or nasopharyngeal secretion specimens were collected within 24 h of admission, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed to detect common respiratory pathogens. Patients were divided into a pathogen-tested group (112 cases) and a pathogen-untested group (20 cases). The tested group comprised a positive subgroup of 99 cases (77 single infections and 22 mixed infections) and a negative subgroup of 13 cases. Clinical recovery evaluation: clinical recovery speed was evaluated using the hospital length of stay (LOS); patients were categorized into a rapid-recovery group (LOS ≤ 5 days) and a delayed-recovery group (LOS > 5 days). To avoid selection bias arising from missing pathogen data, all analyses examining the association between pathogen profile and LOS were restricted to the 112 pathogen-tested patients; descriptive demographic characteristics (Section 3.1 ) were based on the full cohort of 132 patients. A subsequent sensitivity analysis (Section 3.1.1 ) found no statistically significant differences between the 20 untested and 112 tested patients in sex, age, LOS, or rapid-/delayed-recovery group composition, suggesting a limited risk of residual selection bias from this approach. Results Among the 132 children with bronchiolitis, the median age was 6.6 months and the median LOS was 6.0 days. In the tested group (112 cases), the overall positive rate was 88.4% (99/112), with single infection accounting for 68.8% (77/112), mixed infection accounting for 19.6% (22/112), and negative results accounting for 11.6% (13/112). The top three detected pathogens were respiratory syncytial virus (RSV, 54.5%), human rhinovirus (HRV, 31.3%), and parainfluenza virus (PIV, 6.3%), with RSV/HRV (11 cases) being the most common mixed infection. RSV and mixed infections exhibited a bimodal epidemic feature during the study period: in addition to the traditional winter-spring heating season (November to March of the following year), an atypical off-season epidemic peak emerged in May, with a single-month RSV detection rate of 82.1% (23/28). In contrast, hospitalized cases were relatively sparse in other months of the summer-autumn season (June to October). Because case ascertainment was not a complete census in every year and sample sizes were limited, the year-to-year stability of this off-season peak was not confirmed; see Section 2.4 and the Discussion. Within the 112 pathogen-tested patients (rapid-recovery group, n = 52; delayed-recovery group, n = 60), infants < 6 months accounted for 55.8% (29/52) of the rapid-recovery group versus 41.7% (25/60) of the delayed-recovery group ( P = 0.1363); RSV positivity was 50.0% (26/52) vs. 58.3% (35/60) ( P = 0.3771), HRV positivity was 30.8% (16/52) vs. 31.7% (19/60) ( P = 0.9186), and mixed-infection rate was 13.5% (7/52) vs. 25.0% (15/60) ( P = 0.1253); none of these differences reached statistical significance. Conclusion RSV and HRV are the core dominant pathogens of hospitalized bronchiolitis in this region. In addition to the traditional winter-spring heating-season peak, an atypical off-season epidemic peak occurred in May, although its year-to-year stability requires further confirmation.

source_records.title: Pathogen spectrum and its association with hospital length of stay in 112 pathogen-tested children with bronchiolitis: a retrospective study from a cohort of 132 hospitalized cases in Hebei Children's Hospital
source_records.abstract: Objective To investigate the pathogen spectrum and epidemiological characteristics of hospitalized children with bronchiolitis admitted to Hebei Children's Hospital, and to analyze the relationship between different pathogens or mixed infections and clinical recovery speed, providing a clinical reference for the prevention and treatment of infant bronchiolitis in northern China. Methods Based on the electronic medical record system, the clinical data of 132 children hospitalized with bronchiolitis at Hebei Children's Hospital from September 2022 to February 2025 were retrospectively analyzed. Sputum or nasopharyngeal secretion specimens were collected within 24 h of admission, and multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) was performed to detect common respiratory pathogens. Patients were divided into a pathogen-tested group (112 cases) and a pathogen-untested group (20 cases). The tested group comprised a positive subgroup of 99 cases (77 single infections and 22 mixed infections) and a negative subgroup of 13 cases. Clinical recovery evaluation: clinical recovery speed was evaluated using the hospital length of stay (LOS); patients were categorized into a rapid-recovery group (LOS ≤ 5 days) and a delayed-recovery group (LOS > 5 days). To avoid selection bias arising from missing pathogen data, all analyses examining the association between pathogen profile and LOS were restricted to the 112 pathogen-tested patients; descriptive demographic characteristics (Section 3.1 ) were based on the full cohort of 132 patients. A subsequent sensitivity analysis (Section 3.1.1 ) found no statistically significant differences between the 20 untested and 112 tested patients in sex, age, LOS, or rapid-/delayed-recovery group composition, suggesting a limited risk of residual selection bias from this approach. analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed the pathogen spectrum and clinical recovery speed in 112 hospitalized children with bronchiolitis at Hebei Children's Hospital, using data from a larger cohort of 132 cases. Multiplex PCR was used to detect respiratory pathogens, and patients were categorized into rapid- and delayed-recovery groups based on LOS. The results showed that RSV and HRV were the most common pathogens, with RSV/HRV being the most frequent mixed infection. papers.title: Improving respiratory virus forecasts by capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission
papers.abstract: Respiratory viruses impose a substantial burden of morbidity and mortality globally, and models that forecast this burden are widely used to support public health decision-making. However, the public health utility of these forecasts can be limited by poor predictive accuracy. In this work, we show how capturing the effects of school holidays, public holidays and seasonal changes in transmission can improve respiratory virus forecasting performance. We construct a Bayesian renewal model where the effective reproduction number R(t) is composed of log-additive components including school and public holiday effects and an annually-periodic Gaussian process. The model also allows for the relative rate of reporting to vary with school and public holidays. We use this model to forecast respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza and SARS-CoV-2 case incidence across a 28-day horizon over five jurisdictions in Australia. Applied to the 2025 winter season, our forecasts outperform a random-walk baseline forecast across all settings. We find that the inclusion of holiday and seasonal transmission effects improved forecasting performance across the three pathogens. We show that the school holidays are associated with population-wide reductions in R(t) on the order of 5-15% but are generally not associated with changes in reporting. Collectively, our results provide support for the inclusion of holiday and seasonal effects in future respiratory virus forecasting models.

analysis.summary_en: This study demonstrates how incorporating school holidays, public holidays, and seasonal changes in transmission can improve respiratory virus forecasting. Using a Bayesian renewal model, the researchers forecasted RSV, influenza, and SARS-CoV-2 case incidence across five Australian jurisdictions during the 2025 winter season. Their forecasts outperformed a random-walk baseline, showing that holiday and seasonal effects significantly enhance predictive accuracy. The model also accounts for variations in reporting rates during these periods. These results support the integration of such factors into future forecasting models, which could improve public health preparedness. However, the study is limited to a single season and region, and the evidence is based on a single dataset. The findings are cautiously significant for refining respiratory virus surveillance and prediction strategies.

papers.title: A New Homogeneous Surrogate Virus Neutralization Test Format Based on Liposomes and the Complement System
papers.abstract: Abstract Neutralizing antibodies are key mediators of protection against common viral infections such as SARS-CoV-2, influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), making them an important target for diagnostic assays assessing immune status and vaccine efficacy. Here we present a novel platform technology that specifically detects SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies in a simple homogeneous no-wash format as a surrogate virus neutralization test (sVNT). Liposomes loaded with a quenched fluorophore were modified with the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor, the main receptor for SARS-CoV-2 entry. Virus surrogates based on the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein were developed that bind to ACE2-liposomes and contain a trigger moiety, which activates the complement system leading to liposome lysis. Neutralizing antibodies inhibit this binding event and thus prevent the generation of a fluorescent signal. The proof-of-principle was demonstrated using SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pooled human serum, generating IC50 values that can be compared to other assay formats. Testing of 20 SARS-CoV-2 antibody negative sera and 24 sera from individuals with SARS-CoV-2 infection and/or vaccination history, resulted in a specificity of 95%, sensitivity of 96% and a strong correlation (Spearman r = 0.78, Pearson r = 0.77) with antibody titers determined in a pseudovirus neutralization test. The assay platform can be readily adapted to other targets, offering a rapid and straightforward approach to serological immunodiagnostics and in general other competitive assay formats. The simplicity of the assay, the avoidance of washing and immobilization steps renders this format ideally suited for high-throughput screening and point-of-care settings.

Here we present a novel platform technology that specifically detects SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies in a simple homogeneous no-wash format as a surrogate virus neutralization test (sVNT). Liposomes loaded with a quenched fluorophore were modified with the angiotensin-converting enzyme 2 (ACE2) receptor, the main receptor for SARS-CoV-2 entry. Virus surrogates based on the receptor binding domain (RBD) of the SARS-CoV-2 spike protein were developed that bind to ACE2-liposomes and contain a trigger moiety, which activates the complement system leading to liposome lysis. Neutralizing antibodies inhibit this binding event and thus prevent the generation of a fluorescent signal. The proof-of-principle was demonstrated using SARS-CoV-2 neutralizing antibodies and pooled human serum, generating IC50 values that can be compared to other assay formats. Testing of 20 SARS-CoV-2 antibody negative sera and 24 sera from individuals with SARS-CoV-2 infection and/or vaccination history, resulted in a specificity of 95%, sensitivity of 96% and a strong correlation (Spearman r = 0.78, Pearson r = 0.77) with antibody titers determined in a pseudovirus neutralization test. The assay platform can be readily adapted to other targets, offering a rapid and straightforward approach to serological immunodiagnostics and in general other competitive assay formats. The simplicity of the assay, the avoidance of washing and immobilization steps renders this format ideally suited for high-throughput screening and point-of-care settings.

papers.abstract_zh: 摘要 中和抗体是预防 SARS-CoV-2、流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 等常见病毒感染的关键介质,使其成为评估免疫状态和 疫苗 功效的诊断测定的重要目标。在这里,我们提出了一种新颖的平台技术,以简单的均质免洗形式专门检测 SARS-CoV-2 中和抗体,作为替代病毒中和测试 (sVNT)。装载有猝灭荧光团的脂质体用血管紧张素转换酶 2 (ACE2) 受体进行修饰,血管紧张素转换酶 2 (ACE2) 受体是 SARS-CoV-2 进入的主要受体。基于 SARS-CoV-2 刺突蛋白受体结合域 (RBD) 的病毒替代物被开发出来,它与 ACE2 脂质体结合,并含有触发部分,可激活补体系统,导致脂质体裂解。中和抗体抑制这种结合事件,从而防止荧光信号的产生。使用 SARS-CoV-2 中和抗体和混合人血清进行了原理验证,生成可与其他检测形式进行比较的 IC50 值。对 20 份 SARS-CoV-2 抗体阴性血清和 24 份来自有 SARS-CoV-2 感染和/或 疫苗接种 病史的个体的血清进行检测,结果特异性为 95%,敏感性为 96%,并且与假病毒中和试验中确定的抗体滴度具有很强的相关性(Spearman r = 0.78,Pearson r = 0.77)。该检测平台可以轻松适应其他目标,为血清学免疫诊断和其他竞争性检测格式提供快速、直接的方法。测定的简单性、避免洗涤和固定步骤使得这种形式非常适合高通量筛选和护理点设置。

papers.title: RSM01, an extended half-life RSV monoclonal antibody with a high barrier to in vitro resistance
papers.abstract: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). RSM01 is a long-acting RSV monoclonal antibody (mAb) in development for LMICs. In vitro generation of RSM01 resistant mutants has previously been unsuccessful. We systematically assessed the in vitro resistance barrier of RSM01 and the susceptibility of a panel of global contemporary strains to RSM01. Monoclonal antibody resistant mutants (MARMs) were generated by serially passaging triple plaque-purified RSV-A2 and RSV-B1 using HEp-2 cells under pressure from RSM01, nirsevimab, or palivizumab, followed by phenotypic and genotypic characterisation. Moderate resistance was defined as > 3-fold and high resistance as > 30-fold increase in IC 50 compared with parental virus. The susceptibility of contemporary global clinical strains to RSM01 was tested in a neutralisation assay. RSV-A and B strains developed high resistance to palivizumab and nirsevimab, while RSM01 pressure induced moderate resistance. No MARMs demonstrated a fitness advantage. RSM01 neutralised global contemporary strains. In conclusion, in vitro RSM01 resistance was infrequent and moderate and RSM01 had broad activity against circulating strains. The confirmation of the high barrier to resistance of RSM01 is encouraging and provides an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

papers.title_zh: RSM01,一种半衰期延长的 RSV 单克隆抗体,具有高体外耐药屏障
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) causes substantial infant morbidity and mortality, particularly in low- and middle-income countries (LMICs). RSM01 is a long-acting RSV monoclonal antibody (mAb) in development for LMICs. In vitro generation of RSM01 resistant mutants has previously been unsuccessful. We systematically assessed the in vitro resistance barrier of RSM01 and the susceptibility of a panel of global contemporary strains to RSM01. Monoclonal antibody resistant mutants (MARMs) were generated by serially passaging triple plaque-purified RSV-A2 and RSV-B1 using HEp-2 cells under pressure from RSM01, nirsevimab, or palivizumab, followed by phenotypic and genotypic characterisation. Moderate resistance was defined as > 3-fold and high resistance as > 30-fold increase in IC 50 compared with parental virus. The susceptibility of contemporary global clinical strains to RSM01 was tested in a neutralisation assay. RSV-A and B strains developed high resistance to palivizumab and nirsevimab, while RSM01 pressure induced moderate resistance. No MARMs demonstrated a fitness advantage. RSM01 neutralised global contemporary strains. In conclusion, in vitro RSM01 resistance was infrequent and moderate and RSM01 had broad activity against circulating strains. The confirmation of the high barrier to resistance of RSM01 is encouraging and provides an alternative should resistance emerge with widespread use of current licensed anti-RSV mAbs.

papers.title: Respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, 2021 to 2023: a retrospective study of virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics
papers.abstract: Abstract Background Data on respiratory viruses in western Saudi Arabia after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mitigation period are limited. We described the viruses detected, their distribution over time and by age, clinical features, pre-existing conditions, and outcomes in a hospital-based series of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-positive episodes at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH), Jeddah. Methods We retrospectively reviewed episodes in which at least one respiratory virus was detected by real-time PCR, primarily with a multiplex panel, in nasopharyngeal specimens tested clinically between January 2021 and December 2023; testing denominators were not available. Analyses used exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Results We analyzed 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients; no records were available for December 2021, January to September 2022, or January 2023. Median age was 9.0 months (interquartile range 3.0 to 29.0; unknown for 32 episodes). Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) was detected in 40.9% and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) in 34.2% of episodes; 16.8% had co-detections. Among episodes with known age, 70.2% of those in infants younger than 6 months were hRSV-positive (q = 0.005); at least 33 of all 61 hRSV episodes occurred in this age group. hRSV and hRV/hEV proportions differed between years, including within October and November, while testing sites also changed. No association between documented symptoms and virus detection remained significant after correction. Pre-existing conditions were documented in 46.3% of episodes and were nominally less frequent with hRSV (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.64), but not after correction (q = 0.057). Specimens were collected in an intensive care unit in 22.4% of episodes; 9 of 143 patients (6.3%) had a recorded death at data extraction. Conclusions In this single-center series of PCR-positive episodes, hRSV and hRV/hEV were the most frequently detected viruses, and, among episodes with known age, hRSV was concentrated in young infants, most without documented pre-existing conditions. Without testing denominators, these data describe the composition of positive detections, not incidence or seasonality; they provide local hospital reference data from before infant hRSV immunization, whose impact will require denominator-based surveillance. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

analysis.scope_and_question: The study aimed to analyze respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, from 2021 to 2023, with a focus on human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV). The central question was to determine the virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics of these detections.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study was a retrospective analysis of PCR-positive episodes at KAUH, using real-time PCR with a multiplex panel on nasopharyngeal specimens. The analyses included exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Testing denominators were not available, and the study included 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients, though no records were available for certain periods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) were the most frequently detected viruses, with hRSV accounting for 40.9% and hRV/hEV for 34.2% of episodes. Co-detections were observed in 16.8% of cases. Among episodes with known age, hRSV was predominantly found in infants younger than 6 months, with 70.2% of these cases being hRSV-positive. However, no significant association was found between documented symptoms and virus detection after correction for multiple testing.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that without testing denominators, the data describe the composition of positive detections rather than incidence or seasonality. Additionally, the analysis of pre-existing conditions showed a nominal association with hRSV, but this was not significant after correction. The study also highlights that testing sites changed over time, which may affect the interpretation of viral distribution patterns.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for denominator-based surveillance to better understand the incidence and seasonality of hRSV and hRV/hEV. They also provide local hospital reference data from before the introduction of infant hRSV immunization, which could inform future public health strategies and vaccine implementation.

analysis.summary_en: This retrospective study analyzed respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital in Jeddah from 2021 to 2023. The primary focus was on human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV). The study found that hRSV and hRV/hEV were the most frequently detected viruses, with hRSV predominantly affecting infants under six months. However, no significant association was found between symptoms and virus detection after correction. The data, while descriptive, highlight the need for denominator-based surveillance to assess true incidence and seasonality, especially in the context of upcoming hRSV immunization programs.

elements_en.scope_and_question: The study aimed to analyze respiratory viruses detected by real-time PCR at King Abdulaziz University Hospital, Jeddah, from 2021 to 2023, with a focus on human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV). The central question was to determine the virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics of these detections.
elements_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: The study was a retrospective analysis of PCR-positive episodes at KAUH, using real-time PCR with a multiplex panel on nasopharyngeal specimens. The analyses included exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Testing denominators were not available, and the study included 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients, though no records were available for certain periods.
elements_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) were the most frequently detected viruses, with hRSV accounting for 40.9% and hRV/hEV for 34.2% of episodes. Co-detections were observed in 16.8% of cases. Among episodes with known age, hRSV was predominantly found in infants younger than 6 months, with 70.2% of these cases being hRSV-positive. However, no significant association was found between documented symptoms and virus detection after correction for multiple testing.
elements_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The study notes that without testing denominators, the data describe the composition of positive detections rather than incidence or seasonality. Additionally, the analysis of pre-existing conditions showed a nominal association with hRSV, but this was not significant after correction. The study also highlights that testing sites changed over time, which may affect the interpretation of viral distribution patterns.
elements_en.research_and_practice_implications: The findings suggest the need for denominator-based surveillance to better understand the incidence and seasonality of hRSV and hRV/hEV. They also provide local hospital reference data from before the introduction of infant hRSV immunization, which could inform future public health strategies and vaccine implementation.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 该研究旨在分析 2021 年至 2023 年吉达阿卜杜勒阿齐兹国王大学医院实时 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病毒,重点是人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (hRSV) 和人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒 (hRV/hEV)。核心问题是确定这些检测的病毒学、年龄相关和临床特征。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该研究是对 KAUH 的 PCR 阳性事件进行回顾性分析,使用实时 PCR 和多重面板对鼻咽标本进行分析。分析包括精确检验、95% 置信区间 (CI) 的比值比 (OR)、Benjamini-Hochberg 校正和 Firth 逻辑回归。测试分母不可用,该研究包括 143 名患者的 149 次 PCR 阳性事件,但没有特定时期的记录。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (hRSV) 和人类鼻病毒/肠道病毒 (hRV/hEV) 是最常检测到的病毒,其中 hRSV 占 40.9%,hRV/hEV 占 34.2%。16.8% 的病例中观察到了共同检测。在已知年龄的病例中,hRSV 主要见于 6 个月以下的婴儿,其中 70.2% 的病例为 hRSV 阳性。然而,经过多次检测校正后,没有发现记录的症状和病毒检测之间存在显着关联。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该研究指出,在不测试分母的情况下,数据描述的是阳性检测的组成,而不是 发病率 或季节性。此外,对已有病症的分析显示与 hRSV 存在名义上的关联,但在校正后并不显着。该研究还强调,检测地点随着时间的推移而变化,这可能会影响对病毒分布模式的解释。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 研究结果表明,需要基于分母的 发病率 来更好地理解 发病率 以及 hRSV 和 hRV/hEV 的季节性。他们还提供了引入婴儿 hRSV 免疫之前当地医院的参考数据,这可以为未来的公共卫生策略和 疫苗 的实施提供信息。

papers.title_zh: 2021 年至 2023 年吉达阿卜杜勒阿齐兹国王大学医院实时 PCR 检测到的呼吸道病毒:病毒学、年龄相关和临床特征的回顾性研究
papers.source_body_en: Abstract Background Data on respiratory viruses in western Saudi Arabia after the coronavirus disease 2019 (COVID-19) mitigation period are limited. We described the viruses detected, their distribution over time and by age, clinical features, pre-existing conditions, and outcomes in a hospital-based series of polymerase chain reaction (PCR)-positive episodes at King Abdulaziz University Hospital (KAUH), Jeddah. Methods We retrospectively reviewed episodes in which at least one respiratory virus was detected by real-time PCR, primarily with a multiplex panel, in nasopharyngeal specimens tested clinically between January 2021 and December 2023; testing denominators were not available. Analyses used exact tests, odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI), Benjamini-Hochberg correction, and Firth logistic regression. Results We analyzed 149 PCR-positive episodes in 143 patients; no records were available for December 2021, January to September 2022, or January 2023. Median age was 9.0 months (interquartile range 3.0 to 29.0; unknown for 32 episodes). Human respiratory syncytial virus (hRSV) was detected in 40.9% and human rhinovirus/enterovirus (hRV/hEV) in 34.2% of episodes; 16.8% had co-detections. Among episodes with known age, 70.2% of those in infants younger than 6 months were hRSV-positive (q = 0.005); at least 33 of all 61 hRSV episodes occurred in this age group. hRSV and hRV/hEV proportions differed between years, including within October and November, while testing sites also changed. No association between documented symptoms and virus detection remained significant after correction. Pre-existing conditions were documented in 46.3% of episodes and were nominally less frequent with hRSV (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.14 to 0.64), but not after correction (q = 0.057). Specimens were collected in an intensive care unit in 22.4% of episodes; 9 of 143 patients (6.3%) had a recorded death at data extraction. Conclusions In this single-center series of PCR-positive episodes, hRSV and hRV/hEV were the most frequently detected viruses, and, among episodes with known age, hRSV was concentrated in young infants, most without documented pre-existing conditions. Without testing denominators, these data describe the composition of positive detections, not incidence or seasonality; they provide local hospital reference data from before infant hRSV immunization, whose impact will require denominator-based surveillance. Clinical trial number Not applicable.

The target entities are human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), RSV-A, RSV-B, and related subtypes such as HRSV-A and HRSV-B. The central question is about the comparative effectiveness and safety of these interventions in neonates, infants, and young children.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a protocol for a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis. It is registered retrospectively, as indicated in the protocol section 1.4. The evidence base includes studies comparing the interventions to each other and to placebo, with a focus on preventing RSV lower respiratory tract infection in children under 24 months.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review protocol outlines a method to evaluate the efficacy and safety of RSV immunoprophylaxis options. However, no substantive conclusions or pooled estimates are provided in the supplied evidence. The review is in the planning stage and does not yet report findings.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The supplied evidence does not report any controversies or evidence gaps. The review is a protocol and does not include results or interpretations at this stage.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review protocol does not provide specific research or practice implications. It is focused on establishing the methodology for a future systematic review and network meta-analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This review protocol outlines a systematic review and Bayesian network meta-analysis to compare the efficacy and safety of RSV immunoprophylaxis options, including clesrovimab, nirsevimab, palivizumab, maternal RSV vaccination, and other RSV monoclonal antibodies, against each other and placebo for preventing medically attended RSV lower respiratory tract infection in children under 24 months. The target entities are human respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), RSV-A, RSV-B, and related subtypes. The review is in the planning stage and does not yet report findings, controversies, or implications. The methodology includes a retrospective registration and focuses on comparative effectiveness and safety of interventions.

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述旨在比较 RSV 免疫预防方案(clesrovimab、尼塞韦单抗、帕利珠单抗、母体 RSV 疫苗接种 和其他 RSV 单克隆抗体)与安慰剂之间的疗效和安全性,以预防 24 个月以下儿童就医的 RSV 下呼吸道感染。目标实体是人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、RSV-A、RSV-B 以及相关亚型,例如 HRSV-A 和 HRSV-B。核心问题是这些干预措施对新生儿、婴儿和幼儿的相对有效性和安全性。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该审查是系统审查和贝叶斯网络荟萃分析的协议。如协议第 1.4 节所示,它是追溯注册的。证据基础包括对干预措施之间以及与安慰剂进行比较的研究,重点是预防 24 个月以下儿童的 RSV 下呼吸道感染。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 该审查方案概述了评估 RSV 免疫预防方案的有效性和安全性的方法。然而,所提供的证据中没有提供实质性结论或汇总估计。审查处于规划阶段,尚未报告调查结果。
analysis_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 所提供的证据没有报告任何争议或证据差距。该审查是一项协议,不包括现阶段的结果或解释。
analysis_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 审查方案不提供具体的研究或实践影响。它的重点是建立未来系统评价和网络荟萃分析的方法。

papers.title: Post-marketing safety signals of the ROCK2 inhibitor Belumosudil for chronic graft-versus-host disease: a real-world disproportionality analysis based on the FAERS database
papers.abstract: Objective To characterize the real-world post-marketing safety profile, evidence hierarchy, and demographic vulnerabilities of the selective ROCK2 inhibitor Belumosudil in chronic graft-versus-host disease (cGVHD) using FAERS. Methods Adverse event reports (Q3 2021–Q4 2025) were extracted from FAERS. To control indication confounding, primary disproportionality analysis was anchored to a disease-restricted cGVHD and hematopoietic stem cell transplantation background ( n = 921 , 529 ) using four consensus algorithms (ROR, PRR, BCPNN, MGPS) with False Discovery Rate (FDR) validation. Signals were filtered via a prespecified clinical protocol and stratified into a three-tier evidence framework. Subgroup vulnerabilities (prognostic mortality, age, sex) were evaluated using Fisher’s exact tests. Dual sensitivity analyses evaluated polypharmacy (monotherapy cohort with standardized mean difference [SMD] balance) and denominator stability (whole-database comparator). Results Among 1,797 primary suspect Belumosudil reports (6,056 adverse events), initial screening identified 61 consensus-positive Preferred Terms (PTs); 60 maintained FDR significance ( q < 0.05 ). After systematically excluding 16 confounded administrative and indication-synonymous terms, 45 core PTs were retained across three tiers (Tier 1 trial verification, n = 6 ; Tier 2 novel mechanistic signals, n = 6 ; Tier 3 clinical confounders, n = 33 ). Pharmacological toxicities clustered into three dimensions: musculoskeletal symptoms (muscle tightness, ROR = 10.25; skin swelling, ROR = 19.32), mucosal/viral infections (respiratory syncytial virus, ROR = 4.02; viral gastroenteritis, ROR = 4.81), and laboratory abnormalities (hepatic enzyme increased, ROR = 5.64; blood immunoglobulin G decreased, ROR = 5.75). Subgroup stratification identified distinct clinical vulnerabilities: fatal cases were enriched for obliterative bronchiolitis and muscle atrophy; elderly patients ( ≥ 65 years) exhibited predilection for joint stiffness and lip pain ( P < 0.05 ); and females displayed heightened susceptibility to transaminase elevation, skin atrophy, and oral mucosal blistering ( P < 0.05 ). Monotherapy sensitivity analysis ( N = 1 , 255 ; almost all baseline SMDs < 0.10 ) and whole-database comparison confirmed signal robustness. Conclusion Belumosudil’s real-world safety landscape is dominated by musculoskeletal tightness and edema, mucosal and viral infections, and transaminase/immunoglobulin fluctuations, without novel systemic organ toxicities. Findings underscore the necessity of tailored clinical surveillance: monitoring pulmonary decline in severe disease, joint stiffness in elderly recipients, and hepatic transaminases in females.

The research aimed to identify safety signals, demographic vulnerabilities, and adverse event patterns. Adverse event reports from Q3 2021 to Q4 2025 were extracted and filtered using four consensus algorithms with FDR validation. The main results showed 61 consensus-positive Preferred Terms (PTs), with 60 maintaining FDR significance. After excluding confounded terms, 45 core PTs were retained, categorized into three tiers. elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在利用 FAERS 数据库描述选择性 ROCK2 抑制剂 Belumosudil 在慢性移植物抗 宿主 疾病 (cGVHD) 中的真实上市后安全性特征,满足了解其在临床实践中安全性的需要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 使用 FAERS 数据库中 2021 年第三季度至 2025 年第四季度的不良事件报告进行了现实世界的不成比例分析,重点关注疾病限制性 cGVHD 和造血干细胞移植背景,有 921,529 条记录。
elements_zh.methods: 不良事件报告从 FAERS 中提取,并通过预先指定的临床方案进行过滤。使用具有错误发现率 (FDR) 验证的四种共识算法(ROR、PRR、BCPNN、MGPS)来识别信号,并使用 Fisher 精确检验评估子组漏洞。
elements_zh.main_results: 在 1,797 份主要可疑贝鲁莫舒地尔报告(6,056 起不良事件)中,初步筛选确定了 61 项共识积极的首选术语 (PT);60 保持 FDR 显着性 (q < 0.05)。经过系统排除后,三层中保留了 45 个核心 PT。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果表明,贝鲁莫舒地尔的安全性主要表现为肌肉骨骼紧张和水肿、粘膜和病毒感染以及转氨酶/免疫球蛋白波动,没有新的全身器官毒性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 结果强调了定制临床 监测 的必要性,特别是监测严重疾病中的肺功能衰退、老年接受者的关节僵硬以及女性的肝转氨酶。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 双重敏感性分析证实了信号的稳健性,但该研究仅限于上市后安全信号,不包括直接的临床结果或因果机制。

papers.title: Epidemiological characteristics of 11 respiratory pathogens among 19,382 hospitalized children in Putian city
papers.abstract: Objective To analyze the epidemiological characteristics of common respiratory pathogens among children hospitalized with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) in Putian city with the aim of providing a scientific basis for regional pediatric respiratory infection prevention. Methods A retrospective analysis was conducted on clinical data from 19,382 children hospitalized at the Affiliated Hospital of Putian University between January 1, 2023, and December 30, 2025. Multiplex polymerase chain reaction (PCR) combined with capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis was employed to detect 11 common respiratory pathogens. Results A total of 19,382 hospitalized children were enrolled, with an overall respiratory pathogen positivity rate of 69.40%. The positivity rate was highest among preschool-aged children and lowest among adolescents. Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) exhibited the highest detection rate in school-aged children (38.57%), while human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) demonstrated the highest detection rate in infants and toddlers (19.53%). The pathogen positivity rate was 70.24% in males and 68.20% in females, with a statistically significant difference between sexes. Among the 19,382 children with ARTIs, single-pathogen detection predominated, accounting for 58.89%; dual-pathogen detection accounted for 9.93%, and multiple-pathogen detection accounted for 0.57%. Respiratory pathogen positivity rates showed seasonal fluctuations, peaking in winter 2023 (73.98%), spring 2024 (77.85%), and autumn 2025 (74.17%). In addition, the positivity rates of influenza A virus (InfA), influenza B virus (InfB) decreased with increasing temperature, whereas those of HRSV, human coronavirus (HCOV) increased with increasing temperature. A total of 15,601 pathogen detection events were recorded; the three most frequently detected pathogens were human rhinovirus (HRV; 24.66%), Mp (23.68%), and HRSV (14.52%). Conclusion The overall positivity rate of respiratory pathogens among children hospitalized with ARTIs in Putian was high (69.40%), with distinct age-related and seasonal characteristics. Mp predominated in school-aged children, whereas HRSV predominated in infants and toddlers. Pathogen detection peaked in autumn–winter 2023, spring 2024, and autumn 2025. HRV, Mp, and HRSV were the three dominant pathogens. The dual- and multiple-detection groups had median hospital stays of 6 days, compared with 5 days in the pathogen-negative and single-detection groups. These findings provide a scientific basis for optimizing clinical diagnosis and treatment of pediatric respiratory infections in this region.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the epidemiological characteristics of 11 respiratory pathogens among 19,382 hospitalized children in Putian city with acute respiratory tract infections (ARTIs) between 2023 and 2025. Using multiplex PCR and capillary electrophoresis fragment analysis, the researchers found that the overall positivity rate of respiratory pathogens was 69.40%, with the highest rates observed in preschool-aged children and the lowest in adolescents. Human respiratory syncytial virus (HRSV) had the highest detection rate in infants and toddlers (19.53%), while Mycoplasma pneumoniae (Mp) was most prevalent in school-aged children (38.57%). The positivity rates showed seasonal fluctuations, peaking in winter 2023, spring 2024, and autumn 2025. The study provides insights into the age-related and seasonal patterns of respiratory pathogens, which could inform regional strategies for the prevention and management of pediatric respiratory infections. However, the findings are based on retrospective data, which may limit their generalizability and confidence.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 对2023年1月1日至2025年12月30日莆田学院附属医院住院的19382名儿童的临床资料进行回顾性分析。

papers.abstract_zh: 目的分析莆田市急性呼吸道感染(ARTI)住院儿童常见呼吸道病原体的流行病学特征,为区域小儿呼吸道感染的预防提供科学依据。方法 回顾性分析2023年1月1日至2025年12月30日莆田学院附属医院住院的19 382例儿童的临床资料,采用多重聚合酶链式反应(PCR)结合毛细管电泳片段分析法检测11种常见呼吸道病原菌。结果共纳入住院儿童19382例,呼吸道病原总体阳性率为69.40%。学龄前儿童的阳性率最高,青少年最低。肺炎支原体(Mp)在学龄儿童中检出率最高(38.57%),而人呼吸道合胞病毒(HRSV)在婴幼儿中检出率最高(19.53%)。男性病原体阳性率为70.24%,女性病原体阳性率为68.20%,性别间差异有统计学意义。19382例ARTI儿童中,单一病原检测为主,占58.89%;双病原检测占9.93%,多病原检测占0.57%。呼吸道病原体阳性率呈现季节性波动,峰值出现在2023年冬季(73.98%)、2024年春季(77.85%)和2025年秋季(74.17%)。此外,甲型流感病毒(InfA)、乙型流感病毒(InfB)的阳性率随温度升高而降低,而HRSV、人类冠状病毒(HCOV)的阳性率随温度升高而升高。共记录病原体检测事件15601起;三种最常见的病原体是人鼻病毒(HRV;24.66%)、Mp(23.68%)和HRSV(14.52%)。结论 莆田市ARTIs住院儿童呼吸道病原体总体阳性率较高(69.40%),且具有明显的年龄和季节特征。Mp 在学龄儿童中占主导地位,而 HRSV 在婴儿和幼儿中占主导地位。病原体检测高峰期为2023年秋冬、2024年春季和2025年秋季。HRV、Mp和HRSV是三大主要病原体。双重和多重检测组的中位住院时间为 6 天,而病原体阴性和单一检测组的中位住院时间为 5 天。这些研究结果为优化该地区小儿呼吸道感染临床诊断和治疗提供了科学依据。

papers.title: KẾT QUẢ ĐIỀU TRỊ VIÊM PHỔI SƠ SINH NHIỄM VIRUS HỢP BÀO HÔ HẤP VÀ MỘT SỐ YẾU TỐ LIÊN QUAN TẠI BỆNH VIỆN NHI TRUNG ƯƠNG
papers.abstract: Mục tiêu: Nhận xét kết quả điều trị và một số yếu tố liên quan đến viêm phổi sơ sinh nhiễm virus hợp bào hô hấp (Respiratory Syncytial Virus - RSV) tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương năm 2025-2026. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả tiến cứu 202 trẻ sơ sinh viêm phổi RSV dương tính, điều trị nội trú tại Trung tâm Sơ sinh, Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ 10/2025-7/2026. Kết quả: 98,0% đỡ, giảm/khỏi; 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến; 0% tử vong, 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan hỗ trợ hô hấp: SpO2 thấp, độ tuổi, thời gian diễn biến bệnh trước nhập viện dài. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan thời gian nằm viện: bệnh kèm theo (tim bẩm sinh), CRP >= 10mg/L, độ tuổi (p < 0,05). Kết luận: Kết quả điều trị khả quan. SpO2 thấp, tuổi nhỏ, tim bẩm sinh và CRP tăng là yếu tố quan trọng trong tiên lượng.

analysis.study_design_and_population: Đây là một nghiên cứu mô tả tiến cứu được thực hiện trên 202 trẻ sơ sinh mắc viêm phổi RSV dương tính, được điều trị nội trú tại Trung tâm Sơ sinh, Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ tháng 10 năm 2025 đến tháng 7 năm 2026.
analysis.methods: Nghiên cứu sử dụng dữ liệu từ các trẻ sơ sinh được chẩn đoán viêm phổi RSV và điều trị tại bệnh viện, bao gồm theo dõi thời gian nằm viện, mức độ hỗ trợ hô hấp và các yếu tố liên quan như SpO2, độ tuổi và CRP.
analysis.main_results: 98,0% trẻ sơ sinh có triệu chứng giảm/khỏi, 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến, 0% tử vong và 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị là 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Kết quả cho thấy tỷ lệ điều trị thành công cao, nhưng thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp và thời gian nằm viện phụ thuộc vào mức độ nghiêm trọng của bệnh và các yếu tố như SpO2, độ tuổi và tình trạng bệnh kèm theo.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Kết quả cung cấp thông tin quan trọng về tiên lượng và các yếu tố nguy cơ trong điều trị viêm phổi sơ sinh do RSV, hỗ trợ trong việc lập kế hoạch chăm sóc và theo dõi bệnh nhân.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: Nghiên cứu mang tính mô tả, không có dữ liệu thống kê sâu hơn hoặc phân tích nguyên nhân cụ thể, do đó mức độ tin cậy được đánh giá là trung bình.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to evaluate treatment outcomes and related factors in neonatal pneumonia cases caused by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) at the National Children's Hospital from October 2025 to July 2026. A descriptive prospective study was conducted on 202 neonates with RSV-positive pneumonia admitted for inpatient treatment. The results showed that 98.0% of cases improved, 2.0% were transferred to another ward, and 0% resulted in mortality. Approximately 53.5% of patients required respiratory support, with a median hospitalization duration of 7.0 days. The time of respiratory support increased with the highest mode of support used. Independent factors associated with respiratory support included low SpO2, age, and prolonged disease duration before admission. Independent factors linked to hospitalization duration were congenital heart disease, CRP ≥ 10mg/L, and age (p < 0.05). The authors concluded that treatment outcomes were favorable, but low SpO2, young age, congenital heart disease, and elevated CRP were important predictors of prognosis. The study's descriptive nature and lack of detailed statistical analysis limit the confidence in its findings, resulting in a moderate evidence strength assessment.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 病毒感染者hợp bào hô hấp (RSV) gây ra tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương trong giai đoạn 2025-2026。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 这项研究是一项描述性纵向研究,对象为202例在2025年10月至2026年7月期间于首都儿科研究所新生儿中心接受住院治疗的RSV阳性新生儿肺炎患儿。
elements_zh.methods: Nghiên cứu sử dụng dữ liệu từ các trẻ sơ sinh được chẩn đoán viêm phổi RSV và điều trị tại bệnh viện,bao我建议您使用 SpO2、CRP 和 CRP。
elements_zh.main_results: 98,0% trẻ sơ sinh có triệu chứng giảm/khỏi, 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến, 0% tử vong và 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị là 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 研究结果显示治疗成功率较高,但呼吸支持时间和住院时间取决于疾病的严重程度以及SpO2水平、年龄和合并疾病等因素。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为RSV所致新生儿肺炎的预后和危险因素提供了重要信息,有助于制定患儿的护理和随访计划。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究为描述性研究,缺乏更深入的统计数据或具体原因分析,因此证据强度被评估为中等。

papers.title_zh: 2025-2026年呼吸道合胞病毒毛细支气管炎新生儿肺炎治疗结果及相关因素分析
papers.source_body_en: Mục tiêu: Nhận xét kết quả điều trị và một số yếu tố liên quan đến viêm phổi sơ sinh nhiễm virus hợp bào hô hấp (Respiratory Syncytial Virus - RSV) tại Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương năm 2025-2026. Đối tượng và phương pháp: Nghiên cứu mô tả tiến cứu 202 trẻ sơ sinh viêm phổi RSV dương tính, điều trị nội trú tại Trung tâm Sơ sinh, Bệnh viện Nhi Trung ương từ 10/2025-7/2026. Kết quả: 98,0% đỡ, giảm/khỏi; 2,0% đỡ chuyển tuyến; 0% tử vong, 53,5% cần hỗ trợ hô hấp. Thời gian nằm viện trung vị 7,0 ngày. Thời gian hỗ trợ hô hấp tăng dần theo phương thức hỗ trợ hô hấp cao nhất được dùng. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan hỗ trợ hô hấp: SpO2 thấp, độ tuổi, thời gian diễn biến bệnh trước nhập viện dài. Yếu tố độc lập liên quan thời gian nằm viện: bệnh kèm theo (tim bẩm sinh), CRP >= 10mg/L, độ tuổi (p < 0,05). Kết luận: Kết quả điều trị khả quan. SpO2 thấp, tuổi nhỏ, tim bẩm sinh và CRP tăng là yếu tố quan trọng trong tiên lượng.

papers.full_text: Abstract Background During the 2024/2025 respiratory virus season, Belgium recorded the highest incidence of general practitioner visits for influenza-like illness since the COVID-19 pandemic. The pressure on healthcare systems was driven by epidemics of influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), while SARS-CoV-2 activity remained at low levels. This exceptional situation was observed through conventional surveillance as well as via a novel wastewater-based surveillance program integrating influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 measurements. Methods The innovative program monitors over 4.5 million inhabitants, representing 38% of the Belgian population, on a weekly basis by analysing samples from 30 wastewater treatment plants. The present study aims to validate wastewater data on influenza, RSV, and SARS-CoV-2 by comparing it with conventional surveillances. Wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds were computed using a quartile method. Results Throughout the entire season, high levels of correlation were observed between wastewater data and cases confirmed by sentinel laboratories. Wastewater-based thresholds effectively monitored viruses circulation. Conclusions Wastewater-based data was assessed to provide information of added value for monitoring SARS-CoV-2 through wastewater compared to conventional surveillance, offering a large and general population coverage, a short and constant reporting time, and a feature for pandemic preparedness. Several perspectives are proposed in this work to increase the quality of RSV and influenza wastewater monitoring. Abbreviations - ARI: - Number of general practitioner consultations for symptoms other than influenza-like - GP: - General practitioner - ILI: - Number of general practitioner consultations for influenza-like symptoms - LOD: - Limits of detection - LOQ: - Limits of quantification - NH: - Number of consultations for influenza-like symptoms in nursing homes - RSV: - Respiratory syncytial virus - SARI: - Number of hospital admissions for severe acute respiratory infections - SARS-CoV-2: - Severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 Acknowledgements The contribution of all involved partners is acknowledged: SPGE, UAntwerpen, SBGE—BMWB, Aquiris, Hydria and Aquafin. In particular, the partners involved in the frequent sample collection, logistics and laboratory analysis are acknowledged. The analytical work performed by the laboratories is acknowledged (M. De Smedt, Naomi de Roeck, etc.). Funding This work was supported by the Belgian Federal Government and the regional entities: Brussels-Capital, Flanders and Wallonia. Ethics declarations Ethics approval and consent to participate The data analyses carried out in this work are among the legal tasks of Sciensano (artikel 4.4 Wet tot oprichting van Sciensano; article 4.4 Law establishment Sciensano). Article 4.4 explicitly states that Sciensano is authorized to collect, validate, analyse, report and archive data of a personal nature concerning public health. Sciensano is further authorized to make these processed data available with approval of the qualified sectoral committees. I confirm that all necessary patient/participant consent has been obtained and the appropriate institutional forms have been archived, and that any patient/participant/sample identifiers included were not known to anyone (e.g., hospital staff, patients or participants themselves) outside the research group so cannot be used to identify individuals. The study adhered to the Declaration of Helsinki.Wastewater data are anonymized as samples included in the present work cover treatment plants with a minimum of 10 000 inhabitant equivalent. analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to validate wastewater-based surveillance data for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza and SARS-CoV-2 by comparing it with conventional surveillance methods, as Belgium experienced a high incidence of influenza-like illness during the 2024/2025 winter season.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Belgium during the 2024/2025 winter season, involving wastewater samples from 30 treatment plants covering over 4.5 million inhabitants, which represents 38% of the Belgian population.
analysis.methods: Wastewater-based epidemiological thresholds were computed using a quartile method, and the data were compared with conventional surveillance data from sentinel laboratories to validate the effectiveness of the wastewater-based approach.
analysis.main_results: High levels of correlation were observed between wastewater data and cases confirmed by sentinel laboratories throughout the entire season, indicating that wastewater-based thresholds effectively monitored virus circulation.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted the findings as demonstrating that wastewater-based data provides added value for monitoring RSV, influenza and SARS-CoV-2, offering large population coverage, short reporting time, and a feature for pandemic preparedness.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The findings can inform the implementation of wastewater-based surveillance for RSV, influenza and SARS-CoV-2, enhancing public health preparedness and response to respiratory virus outbreaks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on sentinel laboratory data for comparison, and the evidence is moderate as it does not include detailed statistical analyses or long-term validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study validates the use of wastewater-based surveillance for respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), influenza, and SARS-CoV-2 in Belgium during the 2024/2025 winter season. The research highlights the effectiveness of wastewater data in monitoring virus circulation, with high correlation observed between wastewater measurements and sentinel laboratory results. The authors emphasize the added value of this approach for public health, offering broad population coverage and rapid reporting. However, the study's evidence is moderate due to its reliance on conventional surveillance data for comparison and the absence of detailed statistical analyses. The findings suggest that wastewater-based surveillance could enhance pandemic preparedness and provide a complementary tool for monitoring respiratory viruses.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在通过与传统的 监测 方法进行比较,验证基于废水的 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV)、流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的 监测 数据,因为比利时在 2024/2025 年冬季经历了 发病率 流感样疾病的高发期。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: The study was conducted in Belgium during the 2024/2025 winter season, involving wastewater samples from 30 treatment plants covering over 4.5 million inhabitants, which represents 38% of the Belgian population.
elements_zh.methods: 使用四分位法计算基于废水的流行病学阈值,并将数据与来自哨点实验室的传统 监测 数据进行比较,以验证基于废水的方法的有效性。
elements_zh.main_results: 在整个季节中,废水数据与哨点实验室确认的病例之间观察到高度相关性,这表明基于废水的阈值可以有效监测病毒传播。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将这些发现解释为证明基于废水的数据为监测 RSV、流感和 SARS-CoV-2 提供了附加值,提供了大的人口覆盖范围、短的报告时间以及大流行防范的功能。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果可为针对 RSV、流感和 SARS-CoV-2 的基于废水的 监测 的实施提供参考,从而加强公共卫生准备和对呼吸道病毒 暴发 的应对。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究由于依赖哨点实验室数据进行比较而受到限制,并且证据有限,因为它不包括详细的统计分析或长期验证。

papers.title: Rising Tuberculosis Presentations in Ontario, Canada Are Not Explained by Community SARS-CoV-2 Activity: A Population-Based Time-Series Study
papers.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis (TB) notifications have increased in several high-income countries since 2020. Proposed explanations include pandemic related disruption of treatment for latent tuberculosis, changes in population composition, and immune dysfunction following SARS CoV 2 infection. We assessed whether TB presentations increased during the pandemic era and then tested whether community SARS CoV 2 activity was followed by increased mycobacterial disease. Methods: We conducted a population-based ecological time-series study of first TB- and nontuberculous mycobacterial (NTM)-coded hospital, emergency-department and ambulatory clinic presentations in the Greater Toronto/Hamilton Area Plus (GTHA+), Ontario (2024 population approximately 11.2 million), from April 2011 through March 2024. NTM served as a comparator because it shares diagnostic pathways with TB but differs epidemiologically. Negative binomial projection and full-series models estimated pandemic-era changes under three alternative trend assumptions. Distributed lag non linear models estimated cumulative rate ratios for standardized community viral activity over 0 to 12 weeks; sensitivity analyses extended the maximum lag to 26 and 52 weeks. Influenza and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) were prespecified comparators; data for five additional viral exposures were obtained after the primary analysis was completed and analysed as exploratory comparisons. Results: We identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Across six models, estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%. No model suggested an increased in NTM. SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0 to 12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822 to 1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868 to 1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome. RSV was associated with TB and NTM; only the RSV/NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment wide threshold. Conclusions: We identified a modest pandemic era increase in TB-coded acute-care presentations in Ontario, Canada, although its estimated size depended on assumptions about underlying trends. NTM-coded presentations did not increase. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with subsequent TB or NTM presentations at lags of up to one year and did not provide a temporal explanation for the population-level TB increase. Individual-level effects cannot be excluded.
