elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究旨在评估大流行期间结核病发病是否增加,以及社区 SARS CoV 2 活动是否会导致分枝杆菌疾病增加。自 2020 年以来,一些高收入国家的结核病通知有所增加,提出的解释包括与大流行相关的 治疗 对潜伏性结核病的破坏、人口构成的变化以及 SARS CoV 2 感染后的免疫功能障碍。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 一项基于人群的生态时间序列研究在安大略省大多伦多/汉密尔顿地区扩展区(GTHA+)开展,时间为2011年4月至2024年3月,重点分析了约11.2百万人口中首次结核病(TB)和非结核分枝杆菌(NTM)编码的医院、急诊科和门诊诊所就诊情况。
elements_zh.methods: 该研究使用负二项式投影和全系列模型来估计三种替代趋势假设下大流行时代的变化。使用分布式滞后非线性模型估计了 0 至 12 周内标准化社区病毒活动的累积率比,敏感性分析将最大滞后期延长至 26 周和 52 周。流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 是预先指定的比较物,在初步分析后获得了另外五种病毒暴露的数据,并进行了探索性比较分析。
elements_zh.main_results: The study identified 3,985 first TB-coded and 5,214 first NTM-coded acute-care presentations. Estimated pandemic-era TB increases ranged from 3% to 22%, while no model suggested an increase in NTM. Community SARS-CoV-2 activity was not positively associated with TB (cumulative rate ratio per 1-SD increase over 0 to 12 weeks 0.909, 95% CI 0.822 to 1.006) or NTM (0.953, 0.868 to 1.047). No positive associations were identified in subgroup analyses or with maximum lags of 26 or 52 weeks. Influenza was not associated with either outcome, while RSV was associated with TB and NTM, but only the RSV/NTM association met the Bonferroni threshold among the prespecified comparisons, and no exploratory associations met the experiment wide threshold.
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究发现,加拿大安大略省的结核病编码急性护理报告在大流行期间略有增加,尽管其估计规模取决于对基本趋势的假设。NTM 编码的演示文稿没有增加。社区 SARS-CoV-2 活动与随后长达一年的结核病或 NTM 表现没有正相关,并且没有为人群水平结核病的增加提供时间解释。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果表明,社区 SARS-CoV-2 活动并不是加拿大安大略省人口水平结核病增加的时间解释。该研究为大流行期间推动结核病发病增加的因素提供了重要见解,并强调需要进一步研究其他潜在的解释。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究存在局限性,包括对生态时间序列数据的依赖以及可能存在未测量的混杂因素。证据强度中等,因为该研究提供了重要的见解,但不排除个人层面的影响。

papers.title: Diversification without convergence: national childhood respiratory pathogen spectra diverge as they diversify, 1990-2023
papers.abstract: Background National childhood respiratory pathogen spectra are diversifying nearly everywhere - within-country diversity rose in 203 of 204 countries between 1990 and 2023 - yet whether countries are diversifying toward a common spectrum or along divergent paths is unknown. We quantified between-country compositional distance of national pathogen spectra over the same period. Methods We built national pathogen share vectors from Global Burden of Disease Study 2023 lower respiratory infection etiologic attributions (26 pathogens, 204 countries, ages 0-19 years) at five timepoints spanning 1990-2023. Between-country distance was measured as all pairwise Jensen-Shannon divergences (JSD; primary) and Bray-Curtis dissimilarities, with Baselga and Jaccard decompositions; robustness was assessed across metrics, pathogen panels, low-count thresholds and a balanced panel of 107 countries. Results Mean pairwise JSD rose from 0.0084 in 1990 to 0.0283 in 2023 (+238%; trend p = 0.030), peaking in 2021 (+283%) with a partial 2023 pullback. Bray-Curtis dissimilarity rose +120% and the balanced panel +423%. Divergence was entirely balanced variation (share reallocation), with spectrum richness rising from 18.5 to 21.1 of 26 pathogens. Dispersion rose fastest for influenza (coefficient of variation 0.03 to 0.55) and respiratory syncytial virus (0.08 to 0.48). Within-region distance rose in every computable GBD super-region (five of seven): divergence occurs within regions, not between blocs. A country-level bootstrap confirmed the increase (+238%, 95% CI +165 to +331), and segmented trend analysis found no supported breakpoint, with divergence proceeding steadily at +4.1% per year (95% CI 2.0-6.3) rather than in stages. Conclusions National spectra are re-sorting along country-specific axes as vaccine-preventable dominance recedes at different speeds. Diversification is universal, but convergence is absent: the transition at the etiologic-spectrum level is asynchronous and path-dependent, with implications for empirical treatment policy and pathogen surveillance.

papers.abstract_zh: 背景 几乎所有国家的儿童呼吸道病原体谱系都在多样化——1990 年至 2023 年间,204 个国家中的 203 个国家的国内多样性有所增加——但各国是朝着共同谱系多样化还是沿着不同路径多样化尚不清楚。我们量化了同一时期国家病原体谱的国家间组成距离。方法 我们根据 2023 年全球疾病负担研究下呼吸道感染病因归因(26 个病原体,204 个国家,年龄 0-19 岁)在 1990 年至 2023 年的五个时间点建立了国家病原体份额 媒介。国家间距离通过所有成对的 Jensen-Shannon 散度(JSD;主要)和 Bray-Curtis 差异进行测量,并采用 Baselga 和 Jaccard 分解;稳健性通过指标、病原体小组、低计数阈值和 107 个国家的平衡小组进行了评估。结果 平均成对 JSD 从 1990 年的 0.0084 上升至 2023 年的 0.0283(+238%;趋势 p = 0.030),于 2021 年达到峰值(+283%),并于 2023 年部分回落。Bray-Curtis 差异增加了 +120%,平衡面板增加了 +423%。分歧是完全平衡的变异(份额重新分配),26 种病原体的谱丰富度从 18.5 上升到 21.1。流感(变异系数 0.03 至 0.55)和 呼吸道合胞病毒(变异系数 0.08 至 0.48)的离散度上升最快。每个可计算的 GBD 超级区域(七个中的五个)的区域内距离都增加了:分歧发生在区域内部,而不是集团之间。国家级引导程序证实了这一增长(+238%,95% CI +165 至 +331),分段趋势分析发现没有受支持的断点,分歧以每年 +4.1% 的速度稳定进行(95% CI 2.0-6.3),而不是分阶段进行。结论 随着 疫苗 可预防的主导地位以不同的速度消退,国家频谱正在沿着国家特定轴重新排序。多样化是普遍的,但缺乏趋同性:病因谱水平的转变是异步的和路径依赖的,对经验性的 治疗 政策和病原体 监测 具有影响。

news.title: RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study
news.excerpt: An age-stratified transmission model shows that human metapneumovirus seasonality is linked to viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus across ten US regions.
news.rss_summary_html: An age-stratified transmission model shows that human metapneumovirus seasonality is linked to viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus across ten US regions.

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 18, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study by November 17, 2026 in Biology, Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 RSV Activity and Interference Shape Human Metapneumovirus Timing in US Study Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Transmission rates of human metapneumovirus (HMPV) are shaped by viral interference from respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) rather than regional climate conditions, according to an age-stratified dynamic transmission modeling study conducted by Ke Li and colleagues. HMPV causes acute lower respiratory infections that primarily affect young children and older adults, generating seasonal outbreaks that peak annually in March or April across the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. To determine the poorly understood drivers of this seasonality, the research team analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases alongside age-specific emergency department visits across ten distinct US regions. The researchers tested several candidate transmission models to evaluate whether environmental factors or viral interference governed observed spatiotemporal patterns. Dynamic models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all ten regions. In contrast, the timing of HMPV outbreaks was consistently associated with RSV activity, demonstrating that the HMPV transmission rate is directly reduced in the presence of circulating RSV. This viral interference proved essential for explaining regional variations in infection cycles. Among the candidate models analyzed, only those incorporating an RSV-associated term successfully reproduced the biennial patterns of HMPV documented in certain regions. These multi-year cycles are characterized by alternating epidemic waves classified by the authors as “late-small” and “early-large” outbreaks, a dynamic that purely climate-driven formulations failed to replicate. Using the best-fit model containing the RSV-associated term, the investigators predicted how future RSV interventions might influence HMPV spread. Although RSV interventions reduce viral competition between the two pathogens, model forecasts indicate that such measures are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity. The authors concluded that defining these spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen interactions will help inform future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV. Subject of Research: Spatiotemporal dynamics and RSV viral interference of human metapneumovirus Article Title: Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States Article References: Li, K., Perniciaro, S., Kwon, J., Grubaugh, N. D., Weinberger, D. M., & Pitzer, V. E. (2026). Spatiotemporal dynamics of human metapneumovirus and potential impact of respiratory syncytial virus interventions in the United States. HMPV causes acute lower respiratory infections that primarily affect young children and older adults, generating seasonal outbreaks that peak annually in March or April across the United States and other temperate regions in the Northern hemisphere. To determine the poorly understood drivers of this seasonality, the research team analyzed laboratory-confirmed HMPV cases alongside age-specific emergency department visits across ten distinct US regions. The researchers tested several candidate transmission models to evaluate whether environmental factors or viral interference governed observed spatiotemporal patterns. Dynamic models incorporating climate variables into the transmission rate, including vapor pressure, precipitation, potential evapotranspiration, and minimum temperature, could not capture the timing of HMPV activity across all ten regions. In contrast, the timing of HMPV outbreaks was consistently associated with RSV activity, demonstrating that the HMPV transmission rate is directly reduced in the presence of circulating RSV. This viral interference proved essential for explaining regional variations in infection cycles. Among the candidate models analyzed, only those incorporating an RSV-associated term successfully reproduced the biennial patterns of HMPV documented in certain regions. These multi-year cycles are characterized by alternating epidemic waves classified by the authors as “late-small” and “early-large” outbreaks, a dynamic that purely climate-driven formulations failed to replicate. Using the best-fit model containing the RSV-associated term, the investigators predicted how future RSV interventions might influence HMPV spread. Although RSV interventions reduce viral competition between the two pathogens, model forecasts indicate that such measures are unlikely to result in a substantial increase in HMPV activity. The authors concluded that defining these spatiotemporal dynamics and pathogen interactions will help inform future seasonal forecasting and intervention strategies for HMPV. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Wednesday, November 18, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Intranasal Poly I:C Adjuvant Enhances Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Protection in Mice by November 16, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 6 mins read 0 Intranasal Poly I:C Adjuvant Enhances Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Protection in Mice Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A preclinical study evaluating mucosal vaccination strategies against human respiratory syncytial virus demonstrated that formulating an intranasal prefusion F candidate with fifty micrograms of the double-stranded RNA analogue Poly I:C conferred substantial protection and enhanced mucosal immunity in mice. The investigation, conducted in female BALB/c mice and published in Frontiers in Medicine, compared three distinct dosages of Poly I:C against a positive control adjuvant and negative control mock immunizations. Human respiratory syncytial virus remains a primary viral pathogen responsible for severe acute lower respiratory tract infections such as bronchiolitis and pneumonia, disproportionately impacting young infants, immunocompromised individuals, and older adults. Worldwide epidemiologic surveillance from 2019 estimated that thirty-three million episodes of associated lower respiratory tract illness occurred in children under five years of age, causing roughly 3.6 million hospital admissions and 101,400 fatalities, alongside 5.2 million infections, 470,000 hospitalizations, and 33,000 in-hospital deaths among older adults in high-income nations. Although active prophylaxis advanced substantially with regulatory approvals of prefusion F recombinant protein vaccines such as Arexvy and Abrysvo alongside the messenger RNA platform mRESVIA, existing formulations are administered through intramuscular injection. These parenteral vaccines predominantly elicit circulating systemic humoral antibodies rather than direct mucosal protection. Because the virus initiates primary infection and transmission across respiratory tract mucosal surfaces, generating an active front-line immunological barrier directly at the portal of viral entry represents an important objective for next-generation vaccine designs. Secretory immunoglobulin A within respiratory secretions can mediate immediate viral neutralization and immune exclusion during initial exposure, thereby preventing downstream dissemination into lower pulmonary structures. However, non-replicating recombinant subunit proteins administered through intranasal routes frequently demonstrate weak intrinsic immunogenicity when applied without an immunostimulatory mucosal adjuvant capable of triggering local pattern recognition receptors. To overcome mucosal hyporesponsiveness, researchers evaluate synthetic agonists of pattern recognition receptors that mimic pathogen-associated molecular patterns, such as synthetic single-stranded CpG oligodeoxynucleotides that stimulate Toll-like receptor 9 and synthetic double-stranded RNA Poly I:C that targets Toll-like receptor 3. While CpG promotes robust T-helper-1 polarization and murine immunoglobulin G2a production, Poly I:C stimulates type I interferons, activating cytotoxic T lymphocytes and mucosal responses without necessarily following a linear dose-response trajectory. Given that excessive local innate stimulation can induce tissue damage, and prior studies revealed a restricted therapeutic dose window for CpG in which fifty micrograms worsened lung histopathology without boosting efficacy, the authors designed a controlled trial to assess the dose-dependent immunological profile and protective efficacy of Poly I:C combined with engineered prefusion F antigen. Discover more vaccines Find Vaccines vaccine Vaccine Vaccines The experimental antigen consisted of a stabilized recombinant prefusion F protein derived from human respiratory syncytial virus subtype A, expressed in Chinese hamster ovary cells. To retain the metastable prefusion architecture, investigators substituted residues 98 through 144—encompassing both furin cleavage sites, the intervening p27 peptide, and a portion of the hydrophobic fusion peptide—with a flexible twelve-amino-acid glycine-serine linker. The native transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains were excised and substituted with a bacteriophage T4 fibritin foldon trimerization domain at the carboxy terminus. Additionally, six specific stabilizing point mutations were engineered into the sequence: serine-155-cysteine, serine-190-phenylalanine, valine-207-leucine, serine-290-cysteine, aspartate-486-cysteine, and aspartate-489-cysteine. Female BALB/c mice aged six to eight weeks were divided into five experimental cohorts of six animals each: an unadjuvanted phosphate-buffered saline control, a reference group receiving fifteen micrograms of protein with ten micrograms of C-type CpG, and three test groups receiving fifteen micrograms of protein with ten, twenty-five, or fifty micrograms of Poly I:C. Vaccines were administered intranasally in a total volume of fifty microliters across two distinct immunizations delivered on day zero and day twenty-one. Blood samples were gathered thirteen days after the secondary vaccination to assess circulating humoral binding and neutralizing activity. Serum binding immunoglobulin G, immunoglobulin G1, and immunoglobulin G2a titers were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays against immobilized prefusion F protein, with endpoint half-maximal effective dilution values determined through four-parameter non-linear curve fitting. Functional neutralization was quantified using plaque reduction neutralization tests in HEp-2 cell monolayers challenged with human respiratory syncytial virus Long strain, applying the monoclonal antibody palivizumab and TrueBlue peroxidase substrate for plaque visualization, followed by half-maximal reduction titer calculation via the Kärber method. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Circulating antibody analyses revealed that all vaccinated animals mounted antigen-specific humoral responses, though systemic binding titers did not increase monotonically with Poly I:C dosage. The reference CpG group exhibited the highest total binding immunoglobulin G geometric mean titer at 42,781. Among the Poly I:C cohorts, the twenty-five-microgram dose generated the highest binding geometric mean titer at 22,158, whereas the ten-microgram and fifty-microgram doses produced comparable titers of 13,353 and 12,855, respectively. In contrast, functional neutralizing antibody titers demonstrated a clear upward numerical trend with increasing Poly I:C dose, yielding geometric mean titers of 262 in the ten-microgram cohort, 340 in the twenty-five-microgram cohort, and 1,173 in the fifty-microgram cohort, though differences among the three Poly I:C tiers did not achieve formal statistical significance. The ten-microgram CpG control group produced the highest overall neutralizing geometric mean titer at 1,802. Isotype differentiation showed marked divergences in helper T-cell polarization patterns between the two adjuvant classes. Serum from mice receiving CpG demonstrated elevated levels of both immunoglobulin G1 and immunoglobulin G2a, resulting in a significantly elevated G2a-to-G1 ratio indicative of a pronounced Th1-dominant humoral bias. Conversely, all Poly I:C groups produced higher concentrations of immunoglobulin G1 relative to immunoglobulin G2a, generating lower G2a-to-G1 ratios. Enzyme-linked immunospot assays performed on splenocytes stimulated ex vivo with 500 nanograms of purified prefusion F protein revealed that cellular responses did not mirror serum isotype ratios directly. The frequency of interferon-gamma-secreting splenocytes was significantly higher across all Poly I:C groups compared with CpG and mock groups, with the fifty-microgram Poly I:C dose stimulating the highest overall frequency. Splenocyte secretion of interleukin-2 and interleukin-4 showed variable patterns without linear dose correlation, whereas interleukin-5-secreting lymphocytes peaked prominently in the ten-microgram Poly I:C group and declined at higher adjuvant amounts. Fourteen days after their booster vaccination, all animals were anesthetized with isoflurane and challenged intranasally with five hundred thousand plaque-forming units of a mouse-adapted human respiratory syncytial virus Long strain. Mock-vaccinated controls demonstrated progressive clinical wasting, with body weight declining continuously to reach a nadir between post-infection days three and four before initiating slow recovery. In contrast, all four adjuvanted groups exhibited attenuated weight loss, stabilizing body mass within forty-eight hours after challenge and recovering towards baseline. The cohort receiving fifty micrograms of Poly I:C exhibited the most stable post-challenge weight trajectory among all vaccinated mice. Animals were euthanized on day five following challenge for tissue harvest, with the right lung dedicated to molecular viral quantification and mucosal antibody extraction, while the left lung underwent perfusion fixation for blinded histopathological assessment. Local mucosal immunity within lung tissue homogenates was measured by titration against coated prefusion F protein, defining positive binding at an absorbance exceeding 2.1 times negative control baseline. Lung prefusion F-specific immunoglobulin A titers rose alongside the Poly I:C dose, increasing from 1,185 in the ten-microgram cohort to 1,405 in the twenty-five-microgram cohort and 1,838 in the fifty-microgram cohort, approaching the 1,984 geometric mean titer observed with CpG, whereas mock-immunized mice registered an optical baseline titer of 497. Direct absolute quantification of viral replication by digital polymerase chain reaction targeting the viral nucleocapsid gene demonstrated significant viral suppression across all immunized groups relative to controls. Unvaccinated control lungs harbored 766.5 viral RNA copies per milligram of tissue. In comparison, viral burden measured 105.5 copies per milligram in the ten-microgram Poly I:C group, 112.3 copies in the twenty-five-microgram group, and dropped to 30.6 copies per milligram in the fifty-microgram Poly I:C group, representing an approximate twenty-five-fold reduction relative to control animals. The CpG reference group yielded 61.4 copies per milligram. Histopathological evaluation of hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained left lung tissue sections revealed extensive pathological lesions in control mice, distinguished by substantial loss of alveolar structural integrity, pronounced thickening of the alveolar septa, and dense interstitial inflammatory cellular infiltration. Immunized animals demonstrated variable degrees of pulmonary preservation, retaining open alveolar architecture with decreased septal expansion and reduced peribronchial inflammatory infiltrates. Semiquantitative lesion scoring across peribronchial inflammation, alveolar septal thickening, and alveolar interstitial infiltration confirmed lower cumulative injury scores across all vaccinated groups relative to control tissues, although scores did not display a statistically defined stepwise dose-response among the three Poly I:C concentrations. The study authors highlighted several methodological limitations that restrict immediate extrapolation of these findings. First, the experimental design omitted groups receiving unadjuvanted prefusion F protein alone or adjuvant molecules alone, precluding an isolated quantification of baseline protein immunogenicity independent of adjuvant synergy. Second, the evaluation tested three discrete Poly I:C concentrations, which narrows the empirical window necessary to declare a fully optimized clinical dose or establish comprehensive safety margins. Third, while local mucosal immunoglobulin A was quantified through binding assays in lung homogenates, the assay did not isolate or measure the specific functional neutralization potency of those mucosal antibodies. Consequently, the investigators concluded that while fifty micrograms of Poly I:C demonstrated the most favorable balance of neutralizing titer, local mucosal immunoglobulin A, splenic interferon-gamma induction, and post-challenge viral clearance within the tested parameters, its benefits must be validated in broader dose-escalation and functional neutralization studies before advancing to clinical formulation. The investigation, conducted in female BALB/c mice and published in Frontiers in Medicine, compared three distinct dosages of Poly I:C against a positive control adjuvant and negative control mock immunizations. Human respiratory syncytial virus remains a primary viral pathogen responsible for severe acute lower respiratory tract infections such as bronchiolitis and pneumonia, disproportionately impacting young infants, immunocompromised individuals, and older adults. Worldwide epidemiologic surveillance from 2019 estimated that thirty-three million episodes of associated lower respiratory tract illness occurred in children under five years of age, causing roughly 3.6 million hospital admissions and 101,400 fatalities, alongside 5.2 million infections, 470,000 hospitalizations, and 33,000 in-hospital deaths among older adults in high-income nations. Although active prophylaxis advanced substantially with regulatory approvals of prefusion F recombinant protein vaccines such as Arexvy and Abrysvo alongside the messenger RNA platform mRESVIA, existing formulations are administered through intramuscular injection. These parenteral vaccines predominantly elicit circulating systemic humoral antibodies rather than direct mucosal protection. Because the virus initiates primary infection and transmission across respiratory tract mucosal surfaces, generating an active front-line immunological barrier directly at the portal of viral entry represents an important objective for next-generation vaccine designs. Secretory immunoglobulin A within respiratory secretions can mediate immediate viral neutralization and immune exclusion during initial exposure, thereby preventing downstream dissemination into lower pulmonary structures. However, non-replicating recombinant subunit proteins administered through intranasal routes frequently demonstrate weak intrinsic immunogenicity when applied without an immunostimulatory mucosal adjuvant capable of triggering local pattern recognition receptors. To overcome mucosal hyporesponsiveness, researchers evaluate synthetic agonists of pattern recognition receptors that mimic pathogen-associated molecular patterns, such as synthetic single-stranded CpG oligodeoxynucleotides that stimulate Toll-like receptor 9 and synthetic double-stranded RNA Poly I:C that targets Toll-like receptor 3. While CpG promotes robust T-helper-1 polarization and murine immunoglobulin G2a production, Poly I:C stimulates type I interferons, activating cytotoxic T lymphocytes and mucosal responses without necessarily following a linear dose-response trajectory. Given that excessive local innate stimulation can induce tissue damage, and prior studies revealed a restricted therapeutic dose window for CpG in which fifty micrograms worsened lung histopathology without boosting efficacy, the authors designed a controlled trial to assess the dose-dependent immunological profile and protective efficacy of Poly I:C combined with engineered prefusion F antigen. Discover more vaccines Find Vaccines vaccine Vaccine Vaccines The experimental antigen consisted of a stabilized recombinant prefusion F protein derived from human respiratory syncytial virus subtype A, expressed in Chinese hamster ovary cells. To retain the metastable prefusion architecture, investigators substituted residues 98 through 144—encompassing both furin cleavage sites, the intervening p27 peptide, and a portion of the hydrophobic fusion peptide—with a flexible twelve-amino-acid glycine-serine linker. The native transmembrane and cytoplasmic domains were excised and substituted with a bacteriophage T4 fibritin foldon trimerization domain at the carboxy terminus. Additionally, six specific stabilizing point mutations were engineered into the sequence: serine-155-cysteine, serine-190-phenylalanine, valine-207-leucine, serine-290-cysteine, aspartate-486-cysteine, and aspartate-489-cysteine. Female BALB/c mice aged six to eight weeks were divided into five experimental cohorts of six animals each: an unadjuvanted phosphate-buffered saline control, a reference group receiving fifteen micrograms of protein with ten micrograms of C-type CpG, and three test groups receiving fifteen micrograms of protein with ten, twenty-five, or fifty micrograms of Poly I:C. Vaccines were administered intranasally in a total volume of fifty microliters across two distinct immunizations delivered on day zero and day twenty-one. Blood samples were gathered thirteen days after the secondary vaccination to assess circulating humoral binding and neutralizing activity. Serum binding immunoglobulin G, immunoglobulin G1, and immunoglobulin G2a titers were quantified using enzyme-linked immunosorbent assays against immobilized prefusion F protein, with endpoint half-maximal effective dilution values determined through four-parameter non-linear curve fitting. Functional neutralization was quantified using plaque reduction neutralization tests in HEp-2 cell monolayers challenged with human respiratory syncytial virus Long strain, applying the monoclonal antibody palivizumab and TrueBlue peroxidase substrate for plaque visualization, followed by half-maximal reduction titer calculation via the Kärber method. Discover more Study Biology Check Symptoms Respiratory Syncytial Virus Vaccine Circulating antibody analyses revealed that all vaccinated animals mounted antigen-specific humoral responses, though systemic binding titers did not increase monotonically with Poly I:C dosage. The reference CpG group exhibited the highest total binding immunoglobulin G geometric mean titer at 42,781. Among the Poly I:C cohorts, the twenty-five-microgram dose generated the highest binding geometric mean titer at 22,158, whereas the ten-microgram and fifty-microgram doses produced comparable titers of 13,353 and 12,855, respectively. In contrast, functional neutralizing antibody titers demonstrated a clear upward numerical trend with increasing Poly I:C dose, yielding geometric mean titers of 262 in the ten-microgram cohort, 340 in the twenty-five-microgram cohort, and 1,173 in the fifty-microgram cohort, though differences among the three Poly I:C tiers did not achieve formal statistical significance. The ten-microgram CpG control group produced the highest overall neutralizing geometric mean titer at 1,802. Isotype differentiation showed marked divergences in helper T-cell polarization patterns between the two adjuvant classes. Serum from mice receiving CpG demonstrated elevated levels of both immunoglobulin G1 and immunoglobulin G2a, resulting in a significantly elevated G2a-to-G1 ratio indicative of a pronounced Th1-dominant humoral bias. Conversely, all Poly I:C groups produced higher concentrations of immunoglobulin G1 relative to immunoglobulin G2a, generating lower G2a-to-G1 ratios. Enzyme-linked immunospot assays performed on splenocytes stimulated ex vivo with 500 nanograms of purified prefusion F protein revealed that cellular responses did not mirror serum isotype ratios directly. The frequency of interferon-gamma-secreting splenocytes was significantly higher across all Poly I:C groups compared with CpG and mock groups, with the fifty-microgram Poly I:C dose stimulating the highest overall frequency. Splenocyte secretion of interleukin-2 and interleukin-4 showed variable patterns without linear dose correlation, whereas interleukin-5-secreting lymphocytes peaked prominently in the ten-microgram Poly I:C group and declined at higher adjuvant amounts. Fourteen days after their booster vaccination, all animals were anesthetized with isoflurane and challenged intranasally with five hundred thousand plaque-forming units of a mouse-adapted human respiratory syncytial virus Long strain. Mock-vaccinated controls demonstrated progressive clinical wasting, with body weight declining continuously to reach a nadir between post-infection days three and four before initiating slow recovery. In contrast, all four adjuvanted groups exhibited attenuated weight loss, stabilizing body mass within forty-eight hours after challenge and recovering towards baseline. The cohort receiving fifty micrograms of Poly I:C exhibited the most stable post-challenge weight trajectory among all vaccinated mice. Animals were euthanized on day five following challenge for tissue harvest, with the right lung dedicated to molecular viral quantification and mucosal antibody extraction, while the left lung underwent perfusion fixation for blinded histopathological assessment. Local mucosal immunity within lung tissue homogenates was measured by titration against coated prefusion F protein, defining positive binding at an absorbance exceeding 2.1 times negative control baseline. Lung prefusion F-specific immunoglobulin A titers rose alongside the Poly I:C dose, increasing from 1,185 in the ten-microgram cohort to 1,405 in the twenty-five-microgram cohort and 1,838 in the fifty-microgram cohort, approaching the 1,984 geometric mean titer observed with CpG, whereas mock-immunized mice registered an optical baseline titer of 497. Direct absolute quantification of viral replication by digital polymerase chain reaction targeting the viral nucleocapsid gene demonstrated significant viral suppression across all immunized groups relative to controls. Unvaccinated control lungs harbored 766.5 viral RNA copies per milligram of tissue. In comparison, viral burden measured 105.5 copies per milligram in the ten-microgram Poly I:C group, 112.3 copies in the twenty-five-microgram group, and dropped to 30.6 copies per milligram in the fifty-microgram Poly I:C group, representing an approximate twenty-five-fold reduction relative to control animals. The CpG reference group yielded 61.4 copies per milligram. Histopathological evaluation of hematoxylin-and-eosin-stained left lung tissue sections revealed extensive pathological lesions in control mice, distinguished by substantial loss of alveolar structural integrity, pronounced thickening of the alveolar septa, and dense interstitial inflammatory cellular infiltration. Immunized animals demonstrated variable degrees of pulmonary preservation, retaining open alveolar architecture with decreased septal expansion and reduced peribronchial inflammatory infiltrates. Semiquantitative lesion scoring across peribronchial inflammation, alveolar septal thickening, and alveolar interstitial infiltration confirmed lower cumulative injury scores across all vaccinated groups relative to control tissues, although scores did not display a statistically defined stepwise dose-response among the three Poly I:C concentrations. The study authors highlighted several methodological limitations that restrict immediate extrapolation of these findings. First, the experimental design omitted groups receiving unadjuvanted prefusion F protein alone or adjuvant molecules alone, precluding an isolated quantification of baseline protein immunogenicity independent of adjuvant synergy. Second, the evaluation tested three discrete Poly I:C concentrations, which narrows the empirical window necessary to declare a fully optimized clinical dose or establish comprehensive safety margins. Third, while local mucosal immunoglobulin A was quantified through binding assays in lung homogenates, the assay did not isolate or measure the specific functional neutralization potency of those mucosal antibodies. Consequently, the investigators concluded that while fifty micrograms of Poly I:C demonstrated the most favorable balance of neutralizing titer, local mucosal immunoglobulin A, splenic interferon-gamma induction, and post-challenge viral clearance within the tested parameters, its benefits must be validated in broader dose-escalation and functional neutralization studies before advancing to clinical formulation. analysis_zh.location_and_population: 该研究是在六至八周龄的雌性 BALB/c 小鼠上进行的,其中有五只实验 队列研究,每只六只动物,研究结果与人类 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 感染相关。

analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 该研究表明,鼻内制剂为小鼠提供了实质性保护并增强了粘膜免疫,尽管所提供的证据中没有报告具体病例数、死亡数或住院人数。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 该研究是一项临床前研究,研究结果基于小鼠实验结果。该研究发表在《医学前沿》上,方法包括对照试验和免疫学评估。

The investigation, published in Virology Journal, detailed the virological, age-related, and clinical characteristics of positive episodes detected between January 2021 and December 2023. The study authors highlighted that comprehensive data on respiratory viral infections in western Saudi Arabia remained limited following the coronavirus disease 2019 mitigation period, establishing a clear need to describe hospital-based detections, patient characteristics, and clinical outcomes during this post-mitigation transition. To characterize the circulating pathogens, the researchers retrospectively reviewed clinical episodes in which at least one respiratory virus was confirmed through real-time polymerase chain reaction testing of nasopharyngeal specimens, primarily utilizing a multiplex diagnostic panel. Because testing denominators detailing total negative and overall test counts were unavailable in the clinical records, the investigation evaluated the relative composition and patterns among positive cases. The team applied rigorous statistical methodologies to evaluate the data, incorporating exact tests, odds ratios with corresponding 95 percent confidence intervals, Firth logistic regression modeling, and the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction to adjust for multiple hypothesis testing. The final analyzed cohort encompassed 149 real-time PCR-positive episodes occurring among 143 individual patients, though the dataset was constrained by intermittent surveillance gaps across the three-year evaluation window. Specifically, hospital clinical records were unavailable for December 2021, the nine-month span from January through September 2022, and January 2023. Among the episodes with recorded patient age, the median age was 9.0 months, with an interquartile range spanning from 3.0 to 29.0 months, while patient age was unknown or unrecorded for 32 of the episodes included in the series. Virological evaluations demonstrated that human respiratory syncytial virus was the leading pathogen, identified in 40.9 percent of the analyzed episodes, representing 61 total detections. Human rhinovirus or enterovirus was the second most prevalent viral group, documented in 34.2 percent of the episodes, making these two categories the predominant drivers of positive tests. In addition, viral co-detections involving more than one respiratory pathogen were identified in 16.8 percent of the episodes. The observed proportions of both respiratory syncytial virus and rhinovirus or enterovirus differed substantially across study years, with notable variations occurring even between identical calendar months, such as October and November, while testing sites across the medical facility also shifted over time. Age-specific analyses demonstrated that human respiratory syncytial virus detections were heavily concentrated in the youngest pediatric age brackets. Among episodes with documented patient age, 70.2 percent of all positive episodes in infants younger than 6 months were positive for human respiratory syncytial virus. This striking age concentration maintained statistical significance following Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment, yielding a corrected q-value of 0.005. Furthermore, at least 33 of the 61 total respiratory syncytial virus episodes identified throughout the entire multi-year hospital series occurred within this cohort of infants under 6 months of age. The investigators also conducted detailed evaluations linking viral identity with documented clinical presentations, but observed that symptom profiles did not reliably differentiate specific pathogens. Although a range of clinical features was documented in patient medical records at the time of presentation, no statistical association between documented symptoms and specific virus detections remained statistically significant after multiple-testing correction was applied. Pre-existing medical conditions were documented in 46.3 percent of the positive episodes across the hospital cohort and showed an initial nominal divergence based on viral classification. Specifically, underlying conditions appeared less frequent among patients with human respiratory syncytial virus, yielding an unadjusted odds ratio of 0.31 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 0.14 to 0.64; however, this association did not reach statistical significance after adjustment, concluding with a corrected q-value of 0.057. Markers of acute clinical severity were substantial across the patient series: clinical specimens were collected while patients were admitted to an intensive care unit in 22.4 percent of episodes, and 9 of the 143 patients, representing 6.3 percent, had a recorded death at the time of data extraction. Addressing the broader public health context, the authors underscored that the absence of clinical testing denominators precludes interpreting these findings as measures of overall disease incidence or community seasonality, as the figures characterize only the proportional composition of positive detections. Nonetheless, the authors concluded that this single-center dataset provides vital local hospital reference data from the period immediately preceding infant respiratory syncytial virus immunization. They noted that accurately evaluating the future clinical and epidemiological impact of newly introduced infant immunization programs will require robust, denominator-based surveillance systems. analysis.time: The study analyzed respiratory virus detections between January 2021 and December 2023, with the report published on November 16, 2026. The data collection period had intermittent gaps, including no records for December 2021, January through September 2022, and January 2023.
analysis.location_and_population: The study was conducted at King Abdulaziz University Hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, focusing on pediatric patients, particularly young infants. The median age of patients with recorded age was 9.0 months, with an interquartile range from 3.0 to 29.0 months. Patient age was unknown for 32 episodes.
analysis.event: Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was identified as the leading pathogen in respiratory episodes, with 40.9% of the analyzed episodes testing positive for RSV, representing 61 total detections. Human rhinovirus or enterovirus was the second most prevalent, accounting for 34.2% of episodes. The study was reported by Kristina Jarvis and published in the Virology Journal.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: RSV was the primary virus detected, with 61 cases out of 149 positive respiratory episodes. It was heavily concentrated in infants under 6 months, with 70.2% of positive episodes in this age group being RSV. There were 9 recorded deaths (6.3%) among the 143 patients. The study noted that symptom profiles did not reliably differentiate specific pathogens, and pre-existing conditions were documented in 46.3% of episodes, though no significant association was found after statistical correction.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The investigation was retrospective and based on real-time PCR testing of nasopharyngeal specimens using a multiplex diagnostic panel. Due to the lack of testing denominators, the findings only reflect the relative composition of positive detections, not overall disease incidence. The authors emphasized the need for robust surveillance systems to evaluate the impact of future immunization programs.

analysis.brief_en: A study published in the Virology Journal on November 16, 2026, analyzed respiratory virus detections at King Abdulaziz University Hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between January 2021 and December 2023. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was the most frequently identified pathogen, accounting for 40.9% of 149 positive respiratory episodes, with 61 total detections. Human rhinovirus or enterovirus was the second most common, making up 34.2% of cases. The study found that RSV was heavily concentrated in infants under 6 months, with 70.2% of positive episodes in this group being RSV. However, no significant association was found between symptoms and specific pathogens after statistical correction. The dataset had gaps, including no records for December 2021, January through September 2022, and January 2023. The authors highlighted the need for denominator-based surveillance to assess the impact of future infant immunization programs against RSV.

The dataset had gaps, including no records for December 2021, January through September 2022, and January 2023. news.title_zh: 呼吸道合胞病毒 在吉达医院领导小婴儿检测
news.source_body_en: A study published in the Virology Journal on November 16, 2026, analyzed respiratory virus detections at King Abdulaziz University Hospital in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, between January 2021 and December 2023. Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) was the most frequently identified pathogen, accounting for 40.9% of 149 positive respiratory episodes, with 61 total detections. Human rhinovirus or enterovirus was the second most common, making up 34.2% of cases. The study found that RSV was heavily concentrated in infants under 6 months, with 70.2% of positive episodes in this group being RSV. However, no significant association was found between symptoms and specific pathogens after statistical correction. The dataset had gaps, including no records for December 2021, January through September 2022, and January 2023. The authors highlighted the need for denominator-based surveillance to assess the impact of future infant immunization programs against RSV.

news.content: English Login Homepage Topic News Political System Destination Event Travel Happy Vietnam Enterprise Product Heritage Museum Figure Multimedia Data Home News Economy Respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in older adults: From seemingly mild symptoms to a risk of hospitalization. A 65-year-old female patient, whose only pre-existing condition was spinal degeneration, initially presented with symptoms of cough, mild fever, sore throat, and sputum production. However, approximately three days later, she developed severe shortness of breath, wheezing, and hypoxemia, requiring hospitalization and treatment with oxygen therapy, non-invasive ventilation, and nebulization. The treatment lasted approximately 10 days. Báo Pháp Luật Việt Nam•17/11/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on Google Add Vietnam.vn on Google 0 The above case demonstrates that respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection in adults is not always mild. The disease often begins with familiar symptoms such as cough, fever, sore throat, or phlegm, making it easily mistaken for the flu and many other respiratory illnesses. In older adults, especially those with underlying health conditions or weakened immune systems, the condition can worsen rapidly. According to Assoc. Prof. Dr. Le Thuong Vu - Department of Respiratory Medicine, University Medical Center of Ho Chi Minh City, when the infection progresses to the lower respiratory tract, patients may experience progressively worsening shortness of breath, rapid breathing, rapid heartbeat, decreased blood oxygen levels, and even respiratory failure. RSV can also destabilize existing medical conditions. In people with asthma, COPD, bronchiectasis, or lung cancer, the disease can trigger an acute exacerbation; while in people with cardiovascular disease, an infection can be associated with events such as acute heart failure, arrhythmias, or myocardial infarction. Khám phá thêm Tìm hiểu lịch sử Đọc Mẹo Du Lịch Khám phá ĐNA At the Respiratory Department of the University Medical Center of Ho Chi Minh City, approximately 2,600 cases have been examined in the last 2-3 years, with 84 cases of RSV infection recorded. The majority of hospitalized patients were over 60 years old; those 75 years and older were at higher risk of severe complications. Some cases required intubation, mechanical ventilation, and prolonged treatment. Among the underlying conditions requiring special attention, diabetes is a factor that can affect the ability to fight off infections. Associate Professor Dr. Tran Quang Nam, Head of the Endocrinology Department at the University Medical Center of Ho Chi Minh City, stated that when blood sugar levels are high and not well controlled, the immune system's function can be affected, making patients more susceptible to infections, including respiratory infections such as influenza, pneumonia, and RSV. You may also like The dangers of RSV virus to childrenVTV.vn - Since the beginning of October, the number of children infected with RSV virus being treated at Nghe An Obstetrics and Pediatrics Hospital has increased compared to the same period in 2015, including cases with severe symptoms. The woman unexpectedly suffered acute heart failure after experiencing symptoms she thought were the flu.(Dan Tri Newspaper) - A patient with a history of heart failure, hypertension, and coronary artery disease was admitted to the hospital due to acute heart failure accompanied by respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infection, after about a week of experiencing cough, fatigue, and mild shortness of breath. Thinking it was just a common cold, a woman was hospitalized with acute heart failure.A 67-year-old woman was unexpectedly hospitalized with acute heart failure after a week of coughing, fatigue, and mild shortness of breath. Her initial symptoms resembled those of a common cold. Associate Professor, Doctor Tran Quang Nam - Head of the Endocrinology Department, inpatient examination. According to Associate Professor Dr. Tran Quang Nam, besides the commonly mentioned complications in the cardiovascular, renal, or neurological systems, infections are also a significant concern in people with diabetes and can lead to hospitalization. Therefore, good blood sugar control, maintaining a proper diet, and regular exercise should go hand in hand with proactive infection prevention, especially in older adults or those with multiple underlying conditions. Another difficulty in identifying RSV is that its symptoms are quite similar to those of influenza and COVID-19, making it difficult to determine the causative agent based solely on clinical manifestations. When necessary, doctors may order respiratory samples for testing to identify the cause and determine appropriate monitoring and treatment. Currently, there is no specific, routinely used treatment for RSV. In mild cases, patients are primarily treated symptomatically and monitored; in severe cases, oxygen support or other resuscitation measures may be required depending on the patient's condition. You may also like For older adults and those with underlying health conditions, prevention plays a crucial role. Besides hand hygiene and limiting close contact with people exhibiting respiratory symptoms, patients should monitor their health and seek medical attention promptly if they experience shortness of breath or their condition worsens. Furthermore, each health check-up or follow-up visit provides an opportunity for patients to discuss their personal risk factors and appropriate preventive measures with their doctor. RSV may begin as a common respiratory infection, but in high-risk groups, it can rapidly worsen underlying conditions and lead to serious complications. Proactive risk assessment, effective management of existing conditions, and appropriate preventive measures are crucial in limiting the risk of severe progression and contributing to maintaining health and quality of life. Besides hand hygiene and limiting close contact with people exhibiting respiratory symptoms, patients should monitor their health and seek medical attention promptly if they experience shortness of breath or their condition worsens. Furthermore, each health check-up or follow-up visit provides an opportunity for patients to discuss their personal risk factors and appropriate preventive measures with their doctor. RSV may begin as a common respiratory infection, but in high-risk groups, it can rapidly worsen underlying conditions and lead to serious complications. Proactive risk assessment, effective management of existing conditions, and appropriate preventive measures are crucial in limiting the risk of severe progression and contributing to maintaining health and quality of life. news.content_zh: 该文章强调了 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 对老年人的风险,强调其症状最初可能看起来很轻微,但很快就会发展为严重并发症。一名患有脊柱退化的65岁女性患者在出现类似普通感冒的轻微症状三天后出现严重呼吸短促、喘息和低氧血症,被送往胡志明市大学医学中心。她需要住院治疗并接受氧疗、无创通气和雾化治疗,治疗持续约10天。在过去的2-3年里,该中心检查了大约2,600例病例,其中84例确诊为RSV感染。大多数住院患者年龄超过 60 岁,75 岁及以上的患者面临更高的风险。RSV 会加剧糖尿病、哮喘和心血管疾病等现有疾病,可能导致住院。由于症状与流感和 COVID-19 类似,医生可能会使用呼吸道样本进行检测来识别病毒。预防措施包括手部卫生、避免与有症状的人密切接触以及监测健康状况。该文章强调了主动进行风险评估和管理潜在状况以防止严重后果的重要性。

news.content: Nov 17, 08:54 pm EST Medical Daily VITALITY MENTAL HEALTH INNOVATION HEALTHY LIVING CONDITIONS Search form Search Vitality How to Live Better, Longer Rural Minnesota Seniors Could Pay Thousands More as Medicare Advantage Plans Disappear in 2027 Crow Wing, Wadena and Lake of the Woods counties will lose all Medicare Advantage plans in 2027, forcing rural seniors to compare more expensive alternatives before open enrollment ends Dec. 7. Medicare Extends Freeze on New Hospice and Home Health Agencies Into May 2027 but Lets Existing Providers Expand CMS extended its freeze on new Medicare hospice and home health agencies through May 2027, while allowing currently enrolled providers to add locations and continue serving patients. Medicare Doctors Face a 2.31% Pay Cut in January as Physician Groups Warn Seniors Could Lose Access Doctors treating Medicare patients face a 2.31% payment cut in 2027 unless Congress acts. Physician groups warn access could suffer, but no impact has yet been measured. Anthem Drops More Than 200 New York Social Adult Day Care Centers Amid a Statewide Fraud Crackdown Anthem is ending contracts with more than 200 New York social adult day care centers. What older adults and caregivers should check before Jan. 1. Mental Health Blood Markers May Signal Who Benefits From Psilocybin or Ketamine for Depression in Early Conference Research Early conference research from University of Colorado Anschutz suggests blood plasma markers may help predict depression response to psilocybin or ketamine, but the finding remains unvalidated and unavailable clinically. Adults With Schizophrenia or Bipolar Disorder Can Now Use Igalmi Film at Home for Acute Agitation Episodes The FDA expanded Igalmi's approval to at-home treatment of acute agitation in eligible adults with schizophrenia or bipolar disorder, but the home trial primarily assessed safety and tolerability. Mental Health Conditions Became the Leading Cause of Pregnancy-Related Deaths in Texas in 2024 as Overall Rate Fell Mental health conditions became the leading cause of pregnancy-related deaths in Texas in 2024, while the overall mortality rate declined and Black women continued to face the highest risk. Kratom Involved in More Than 5,000 Overdose Deaths Since 2020 as Gas Station 7-OH Products Face Federal Scrutiny CDC data cited by 60 Minutes show kratom was involved in more than 5,000 U.S. overdose deaths since 2020. Experts warn about opioid-like effects, addiction and concentrated 7-OH products. Innovation Ivonescimab, a Closely Watched Lung Cancer Drug From China, Rejected by FDA Without Significant Survival Gain The FDA declined to approve Summit Therapeutics' ivonescimab with chemotherapy for advanced EGFR-mutated lung cancer after the HARMONi trial missed its prespecified overall-survival threshold. Wilserdly Pill Nearly Doubled Time Without Progression in ESR1-Mutated Advanced Breast Cancer, Winning FDA Approval With Everolimus The FDA approved Wilserdly, or giredestrant, with everolimus for eligible adults with ESR1-mutated advanced breast cancer after a trial nearly doubled progression-free survival. Pebrilzo Becomes Second FDA-Approved Perjeta Biosimilar for HER2-Positive Breast Cancer but Cannot Launch Before Third Quarter 2028 The FDA approved Biocon's Pebrilzo, a second Perjeta biosimilar for adults with HER2-positive breast cancer. It will not launch in the United States before the third quarter of 2028. At-Home 40 Hz Light and Sound Alzheimer's Device Missed Its Main Goal in 673-Person Pivotal Trial Cognito Therapeutics' Spectris headset failed to slow Alzheimer's disease overall in a 673-person trial, while exploratory results in a milder subgroup require further study and regulatory review. Healthy Living Man From Kazakhstan Accused in Hospital Ransomware Extortion Appears in Knoxville Court After Extradition From Italy Roman Khlynovskiy, a Kazakhstan national accused of joining a ransomware group that targeted hospitals and schools, appeared in Knoxville federal court after extradition from Italy. Connecticut HUSKY D Members Will Not Lose Medicaid for Missing Work Rules Before July 2027 Under New Plan Connecticut HUSKY D members will keep Medicaid coverage through June 2027 if they fail to meet new work rules, but reporting requirements begin January 1. UHealth Will Leave Aetna, Preferred Care Network and Solis Medicare Advantage Plans in Miami After December 31 UHealth dejará fuera de su red a Aetna, Preferred Care Network y Solis tras el 31 de diciembre de 2026. Los afiliados deben revisar opciones antes del 7 de diciembre. UnitedHealth's Commissioned Review Praised How It Writes Medical Policies but Left Individual Patients' Coverage Denials Unexamined A UnitedHealth-commissioned review praised UnitedHealthcare's medical policy process but did not assess individual coverage denials, while outside data show many denials are overturned on appeal. Healthy Living Moderna RSV Shot 82% Effective Against Hospitalization in Veterans 50 and Older, but Infection Protection Fell With Age Published Nov 14, 2026 9:02 PM EST By Cole Mercer Scott Olson | Getty Images Share on Twitter Share on Facebook Share on WhatsApp Moderna's mRNA vaccine against respiratory syncytial virus was 81.8% effective at preventing RSV-related hospitalization among U.S. veterans 50 and older, according to a large Veterans Affairs study in JAMA Network Open reported by CIDRAP. Protection against any documented infection was lower, at 60.3%. Protection against infection also dropped steeply with age. news.title_zh: Moderna RSV 对 50 岁及以上退伍军人住院治疗的有效率为 82%,但感染保护率随着年龄的增长而下降 - 医学日报
news.source_body_en: Moderna's mRNA vaccine against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV), mResvia, was found to be 81.8% effective at preventing RSV-related hospitalization among U.S. veterans aged 50 and older, according to a study published by the Veterans Health Administration on Nov 14, 2026. The study, reported by CIDRAP, tracked vaccinations from Oct. 31, 2026, with up to 24 weeks of follow-up. Protection against documented infection was lower, at 60.3%, and effectiveness against infection decreased with age, being 82.9% in veterans aged 50 to 59 and only 28.6% in those 80 and older. The vaccine's performance in subsequent seasons remains unknown, as it is currently given once. The FDA approved mResvia in May 2024 for adults 60 and older and expanded its use in June 2025 to adults 18 to 59 at increased risk of RSV lung disease. A separate VA preprint study estimated 87% effectiveness against hospitalization but has not been peer-reviewed. The results are part of the first large real-world analysis of the mRNA vaccine outside clinical trials.
news.content_zh: 根据退伍军人健康管理局于 2026 年 11 月 14 日发表的一项研究,Moderna 的针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 的 mRNA 疫苗 (RSV) mResvia 在预防 50 岁及以上美国退伍军人中与 RSV 相关的住院治疗方面有 81.8% 的效率。CIDRAP 报道的这项研究从 10 月 31 日开始追踪 疫苗接种,2026 年,随访时间长达 24 周。对记录在案的感染的保护率较低,为 60.3%,并且感染的有效性随着年龄的增长而下降,50 岁至 59 岁的退伍军人为 82.9%,而 80 岁及以上的退伍军人仅为 28.6%。疫苗 在后续赛季中的表现仍然未知,因为目前已给出一次。FDA 于 2024 年 5 月批准 mResvia 用于 60 岁及以上的成年人,并于 2025 年 6 月将其用途扩大到 RSV 肺部疾病风险较高的 18 至 59 岁成年人。VA 的另一项预印本研究估计对住院治疗的有效性为 87%,但尚未经过同行评审。该结果是临床试验之外对 mRNA 疫苗 进行的首次大型真实分析的一部分。

analysis_zh.time: 该研究于2026年11月14日发表,疫苗接种周期从2026年10月31日开始追踪,随访时间长达24周。随着RSV季节在全国范围内的到来,调查结果被报道。
analysis_zh.location_and_population: 这项研究涉及 50 岁及以上的美国退伍军人,他们通过退伍军人健康管理局接受护理。该分析包括 74,926 名接种疫苗的退伍军人和 286,425 名未接种疫苗的退伍军人。
analysis_zh.event: CIDRAP 报道的 JAMA Network Open 上的一项大型退伍军人事务研究表明,Moderna 针对 呼吸道合胞病毒 (mResvia) 的 mRNA 疫苗 在预防 50 岁及以上美国退伍军人中与 RSV 相关的住院治疗方面的有效性为 81.8%。对任何记录在案的感染的保护率较低,为 60.3%,并且随着年龄的增长,对感染的保护率也急剧下降。
analysis_zh.scale_impact_and_risk: 疫苗 对 50 岁至 59 岁的退伍军人有 82.9% 的有效率,但对 80 岁及以上的退伍军人只有 28.6% 的有效率。该研究是首次大型现实世界研究 mRNA 疫苗 在临床试验之外的表现。FDA 于 2024 年 5 月批准 mResvia 用于 60 岁及以上的成人,并于 2025 年 6 月将批准范围扩大到 RSV 肺部疾病风险较高的 18 至 59 岁成人。
analysis_zh.response_status_and_uncertainty: 研究结果基于目标试验设计,该设计试图模仿使用健康记录的随机试验。CIDRAP 报道了这项研究,其结果是正在进行的分析的一部分。作为预印本发表的一项单独的 VA 分析估计,使用不同的设计对 RSV 住院治疗的有效性为 87%,但这尚未经过同行评审。mResvia 的保护是否能持续到第二季或第三季尚不清楚。

LM Otero photo By Joanna FrketichReporter Hamilton is seeing increasing spread of influenza A and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The number of tests coming back positive for influenza A in Hamilton has been on a steady increase over the past three weeks to 3.6 per cent on Nov. 7 from 2.9 per cent on Oct. 31 and 2.2 per cent on Oct. 24. Hamilton public health is also reporting the number of positive RSV tests is on the rise. ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW As a result, Hamilton Health Sciences (HHS) and St. Joseph’s Healthcare Hamilton are urging Hamiltonians to minimize the spread by getting immunized against flu, COVID-19 and RSV. In addition, stay home when sick and wear a mask in crowded indoor spaces. Eligible infants can get immunized against RSV at McMaster Children’s Hospital. LM Otero photo By Joanna FrketichReporter Hamilton is seeing increasing spread of influenza A and respiratory syncytial virus (RSV). The number of tests coming back positive for influenza A in Hamilton has been on a steady increase over the past three weeks to 3.6 per cent on Nov. 7 from 2.9 per cent on Oct. 31 and 2.2 per cent on Oct. 24. Hamilton public health is also reporting the number of positive RSV tests is on the rise. ARTICLE CONTINUES BELOW As a result, Hamilton Health Sciences (HHS) and St. Joseph’s Healthcare Hamilton are urging Hamiltonians to minimize the spread by getting immunized against flu, COVID-19 and RSV. In addition, stay home when sick and wear a mask in crowded indoor spaces. Eligible infants can get immunized against RSV at McMaster Children’s Hospital. news.content_zh: 安大略省汉密尔顿的甲型流感和 呼吸道合胞病毒 (RSV) 传播正在增加。据《汉密尔顿观察家》报道,截至 2026 年 11 月 7 日,甲型流感检测阳性率已稳步上升至 3.6%。汉密尔顿公共卫生部门还注意到 RSV 检测有所增加。作为回应,汉密尔顿健康科学公司和汉密尔顿圣约瑟夫医疗保健公司鼓励居民接种流感、COVID-19 和 RSV 疫苗,以最大程度地减少传播。他们建议生病时呆在家里,并在拥挤的室内空间戴口罩。符合条件的婴儿可以在麦克马斯特儿童医院接受 RSV 免疫接种。该文章没有提供具体的病例或死亡人数,但强调了人们日益增长的担忧,并呼吁社区采取行动以防止进一步传播。该信息截至发布日期 2026 年 11 月 17 日为最新信息。

Some criteria overlap, meaning people may qualify for multiple vaccines free of charge. ‌ ‌ The eligibility requirements are set to ensure that people in particularly vulnerable categories, including the elderly and children at clinical risk, receive the appropriate level of protection against these common illnesses. People will either be notified about these offers or will need to arrange them independently. ‌ In an Instagram post, the NHS said: "Winter viruses can be more serious as we get older. Flu, COVID-19 and RSV can all cause serious illness, but vaccination can help reduce your risk. Find out which vaccines you can get and how to get them." ‌ You can purchase all three vaccines privately at most high street chemists, supermarkets, and private healthcare facilities throughout the UK. They utilise the exact same licensed vaccines as the NHS, delivered by a qualified pharmacist or nurse following a quick health assessment - priced between £15 and £245, reports the Express. Content cannot be displayed without consent Am I eligible for a flu vaccine? Adults at higher risk of getting seriously ill from flu and most children are eligible for the flu vaccine. If you're eligible, getting your flu vaccine every year is important, as it reduces your risk of getting severe symptoms: ‌ People aged 65 or over (including those who will be 65 by March 31, 2027) People aged 18 to 64 with certain long-term health conditions People who are pregnant People who live in a care home People who are the main carer for an older or disabled person, or receive a carer's allowance People who live with someone who has a weakened immune system People aged 16 or over and rough sleeping or staying in a homeless hostel or night shelter The criteria are slightly different for children, but most young people could be eligible: ‌ children aged 2 or 3 years (born between 1 September 1, 2022, and August 31, 2024) children aged 4 years who have not started school yet school-aged children (reception to year 11) children aged 6 months to 17 years with certain long-term health conditions Frontline health and social care workers will be offered a free flu vaccine through their employer. The last date you can get your flu vaccine is March 31, but it's best to get vaccinated sooner to protect yourself during winter. ‌ Ensure our latest headlines always appear at the top of your Google Search by making us a Preferred Source. Click here to activate or add us as a Preferred Source in your Google search settings View 2 Images The NHS has a full list of everyone eligible to gain extra protection for free (stock)(Image: Prostock-Studio via Getty Images) ‌ Am I eligible for a COVID-19 vaccine? If you qualify, receiving your COVID-19 vaccination annually is crucial, as it reduces your risk of developing severe symptoms. COVID-19 transmits more readily in winter as we spend increased time indoors. COVID-19 vaccines are available to: People aged 75 or over (including those who will be 75 by January 31, 2027) People aged 6 months to 74 years and who have a weakened immune system because of a health condition or treatment People who live in a care home for older adults ‌ You do not need to wait for an invitation before booking an appointment. If you're eligible for the winter COVID-19 vaccine, you can book a COVID-19 vaccination appointment online (or in the NHS App) or find a walk-in COVID-19 vaccination site to get vaccinated without an appointment. Am I eligible for the RSV vaccine? The RSV jab helps guard against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) infections, a widespread cause of coughs and colds. The following groups automatically qualify for a free RSV vaccine on the NHS: Article continues below Anyone who is 28 weeks pregnant or more People aged 75 or over People aged 65 to 74 and have a weakened immune system or have a long-term lung condition (this does not include asthma that is under control) People who live in a care home for older adults GET MORE FROM US Choose Daily Mirror as a 'Preferred Source' on Google News for quick access to the news you value. ‌ Health NHS Winter Flu Coronavirus On Instagram Expert Advice At Reach and across our entities we and our partners use information collected through cookies and other identifiers from your device to improve experience on our site, analyse how it is used and to show personalised advertising. analysis.brief_en: Molecular Designs has secured its first FDA clearance for a diagnostic panel that tests for Flu A, Flu B, and RSV, as reported by Clinical Lab Products on November 16, 2026. This development is significant for respiratory infection diagnostics, particularly in the context of rising flu season activity and the dominance of H1N1. The panel is designed to enhance detection capabilities in clinical settings, potentially improving patient outcomes through earlier and more accurate diagnoses. However, the report does not provide specific details on the scale of impact or risk associated with the panel's implementation. The approval highlights advancements in molecular testing for respiratory pathogens, aligning with broader trends in diagnostic innovation.

news.title_zh: Molecular Designs 首次获得 FDA 批准的 Flu A/Flu B/RSV Panel - 临床实验室产品
news.source_body_en: Molecular Designs has secured its first FDA clearance for a diagnostic panel that tests for Flu A, Flu B, and RSV, as reported by Clinical Lab Products on November 16, 2026. This development is significant for respiratory infection diagnostics, particularly in the context of rising flu season activity and the dominance of H1N1. The panel is designed to enhance detection capabilities in clinical settings, potentially improving patient outcomes through earlier and more accurate diagnoses. However, the report does not provide specific details on the scale of impact or risk associated with the panel's implementation. The approval highlights advancements in molecular testing for respiratory pathogens, aligning with broader trends in diagnostic innovation.
news.content_zh: 据 Clinical Lab Products 于 2026 年 11 月 16 日报道,Molecular Designs 的测试 A 型流感、B 型流感和 RSV 的诊断面板已获得 FDA 的首次批准。这一进展对于呼吸道感染诊断具有重要意义,特别是在流感季节活动增加和 H1N1 占主导地位的背景下。该面板旨在增强临床环境中的检测能力,通过更早、更准确的诊断来潜在地改善患者的治疗结果。然而,该报告没有提供与该小组实施相关的影响或风险规模的具体细节。此次批准凸显了呼吸道病原体分子检测方面的进步,符合诊断创新的更广泛趋势。

news.content: MCKNIGHT’S LONG-TERM CARE NEWS MCKNIGHT’S SENIOR LIVING MCKNIGHT’S HOME CARE Log In Register Subscribe Log In MORE FROM MCKNIGHT’S MCKNIGHT’S LONG-TERM CARE NEWS MCKNIGHT’S SENIOR LIVING MCKNIGHT’S HOME CARE Subscribe Job Board Directory Clinical Latest News Care Delivery & Staff Development Clinical Programs & Prevention Patient Conditions & Therapies Business Latest News Finance & Investment On the Move Operations & Asset Management Workforce & Marketing Payment Workforce Regulatory Legal Regulations & Compliance Quality & Workforce Standards Technology Automation & Administrative Tech Clinical & Care Technologies Data, Security & Analytics McKnight’s Tech Awards + Summit Opinions & Features Editors’ Columns Guest Columns Marketplace Columns The Brighter Side Series and Special Coverage Column Submission Guidelines Live and Virtual Events McKnight’s Pinnacle Awards McKnight’s Tech Awards + Summit McKnight’s Women of Distinction Conference Coverage Webinars Online Forums Product Theaters Workforce Development Forums Resources Newsmakers Podcasts Market Leaders Podcasts E-Books E-Newsletters Magazine Partner content Videos Whitepapers Workforce Development Guide McKnight’s LTC News – Awards Won Clinical Daily News Vaccine offers strong protection against RSV in adults over 50, study finds Foster Stubbs (Photo: geargodz/Getty Images) November 13, 2026 Share › Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share by Email Print (Photo: geargodz/Getty Images) A single dose of Moderna’s mResvia RSV vaccine showed an estimated effectiveness of 60.3% against documented RSV infections, 60.2% against RSV-associated emergency department or urgent care encounters and 81.8% against RSV-associated hospitalizations at 24 weeks among adults 50 years and older. That is according to an October study published in JAMA Network Open. “In this cohort study using a target trial emulation framework to evaluate mRNA-1345 vaccine effectiveness (VE), veterans aged 50 years and older vaccinated with a single dose of mRNA-1345 had a lower risk of having RSV-related illness during the 2025 to 2026 respiratory illness season than unvaccinated individuals,” authors said. “Further follow-up is needed to assess the durability of mRNA-1345 protection over multiple seasons, whereas comparative effectiveness studies can inform relative protection of different RSV vaccine products.” The study analyzed data from 74,926 vaccinated veterans 50 years and older receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration. The vets were matched to 286,425 unique control individuals between October 2025 and May 2026. Primary outcomes tracked included any positive RSV test result occurring from day 14 after the index date until the end of the study period or 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included RSV-associated emergency department or urgent care encounters and RSV-associated acute care hospitalizations. The results showed that VE decreased steadily with increasing age. Specifically, VE was 82.9% among individuals ages 50 to 59, 66.3% among those ages 60 to 69, 64% among those ages 70 to 79 and 28.6% among those ages 80 and older. The FDA approved the vaccine in May 2024 for adults 60 and older; this approval was expanded in June 2025 to also include adults 18 to 59 who are at increased risk of lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV. news.content_original: MCKNIGHT’S LONG-TERM CARE NEWS MCKNIGHT’S SENIOR LIVING MCKNIGHT’S HOME CARE Log In Register Subscribe Log In MORE FROM MCKNIGHT’S MCKNIGHT’S LONG-TERM CARE NEWS MCKNIGHT’S SENIOR LIVING MCKNIGHT’S HOME CARE Subscribe Job Board Directory Clinical Latest News Care Delivery & Staff Development Clinical Programs & Prevention Patient Conditions & Therapies Business Latest News Finance & Investment On the Move Operations & Asset Management Workforce & Marketing Payment Workforce Regulatory Legal Regulations & Compliance Quality & Workforce Standards Technology Automation & Administrative Tech Clinical & Care Technologies Data, Security & Analytics McKnight’s Tech Awards + Summit Opinions & Features Editors’ Columns Guest Columns Marketplace Columns The Brighter Side Series and Special Coverage Column Submission Guidelines Live and Virtual Events McKnight’s Pinnacle Awards McKnight’s Tech Awards + Summit McKnight’s Women of Distinction Conference Coverage Webinars Online Forums Product Theaters Workforce Development Forums Resources Newsmakers Podcasts Market Leaders Podcasts E-Books E-Newsletters Magazine Partner content Videos Whitepapers Workforce Development Guide McKnight’s LTC News – Awards Won Clinical Daily News Vaccine offers strong protection against RSV in adults over 50, study finds Foster Stubbs (Photo: geargodz/Getty Images) November 13, 2026 Share › Share on Facebook Share on Twitter Share on LinkedIn Share by Email Print (Photo: geargodz/Getty Images) A single dose of Moderna’s mResvia RSV vaccine showed an estimated effectiveness of 60.3% against documented RSV infections, 60.2% against RSV-associated emergency department or urgent care encounters and 81.8% against RSV-associated hospitalizations at 24 weeks among adults 50 years and older. That is according to an October study published in JAMA Network Open. “In this cohort study using a target trial emulation framework to evaluate mRNA-1345 vaccine effectiveness (VE), veterans aged 50 years and older vaccinated with a single dose of mRNA-1345 had a lower risk of having RSV-related illness during the 2025 to 2026 respiratory illness season than unvaccinated individuals,” authors said. “Further follow-up is needed to assess the durability of mRNA-1345 protection over multiple seasons, whereas comparative effectiveness studies can inform relative protection of different RSV vaccine products.” The study analyzed data from 74,926 vaccinated veterans 50 years and older receiving care in the Veterans Health Administration. The vets were matched to 286,425 unique control individuals between October 2025 and May 2026. Primary outcomes tracked included any positive RSV test result occurring from day 14 after the index date until the end of the study period or 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included RSV-associated emergency department or urgent care encounters and RSV-associated acute care hospitalizations. The results showed that VE decreased steadily with increasing age. Specifically, VE was 82.9% among individuals ages 50 to 59, 66.3% among those ages 60 to 69, 64% among those ages 70 to 79 and 28.6% among those ages 80 and older. The FDA approved the vaccine in May 2024 for adults 60 and older; this approval was expanded in June 2025 to also include adults 18 to 59 who are at increased risk of lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV. analysis.brief_en: A study published in JAMA Network Open in October 2026 found that a single dose of Moderna’s mResvia RSV vaccine offers strong protection against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) in adults over 50. The analysis, conducted using a target trial emulation framework, tracked data from 74,926 vaccinated veterans aged 50 and older in the Veterans Health Administration, matched to 286,425 control individuals between October 2025 and May 2026. The vaccine showed effectiveness of 60.3% against documented RSV infections, 60.2% against RSV-related emergency department or urgent care encounters, and 81.8% against RSV-associated hospitalizations at 24 weeks. However, effectiveness decreased with age, ranging from 82.9% among those aged 50 to 59 to 28.6% among those aged 80 and older. The study emphasized the need for further follow-up to assess long-term protection and comparative effectiveness of different RSV vaccines. The findings are based on data from the 2025 to 2026 respiratory illness season, and the vaccine was approved by the FDA in May 2024 for adults 60 and older, with an expanded approval in June 2025 for adults 18 to 59 at increased risk of lower respiratory tract disease caused by RSV.
